content.text: ## Story S8: Orchestrator invocation contract in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md + Value validation canary
### Description

**What**: Document the orchestrator's invocation contract for the new primitive in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md: invoke `start` via `Bash(run_in_background: true)` → `bash_id`, drain progress via `BashOutput(bash_id)` for streaming only, poll `<state_dir>/done` for completion, read `<state_dir>/exit-code` as the authoritative result. Include an explicit "do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion" note. Separately, execute the Value validation SC: on a canary worktree, run one representative test-gate cycle under both the legacy `test-batched` path and the new primitive on the same commit, record tool-call counts and total tokens consumed in the epic closure comment, assert the new path uses ≤3 tool calls and reduces tokens by ≥50%. INSTALL.md is also updated here with a pointer to the new test-run primitive.

**Why**: The orchestrator contract is the agent-facing API of the new primitive. Without clear documentation, every caller risks misusing `BashOutput` as a completion signal (one of the critical scenarios from brainstorm). The Value validation canary is the SC that gates epic closure on measured improvement.
**Scope**:
- IN: COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md contract section, INSTALL.md pointer, canary measurement script + fixture, closure comment with numbers
- OUT: CLAUDE.md full architecture update (S9 doc refresh)
### Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md includes an "Orchestrator invocation contract" section describing `run_in_background` dispatch, `BashOutput` for progress-only, `done` marker polling, and `exit-code` read, with an explicit "do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion" note

← Satisfies: "Orchestrator invocation contract — documented in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md: the orchestrator invokes test-run start via Bash(run_in_background: true) ... Explicit 'do not treat BashOutput return-empty as completion' note"

- When this story is complete, a canary worktree runs one representative test-gate cycle under (a) the legacy path and (b) the new primitive on the same commit; both tool-call count and total tokens from dispatch to verdict are recorded in the epic closure comment

← Satisfies: "before closing the epic, a canary worktree runs one representative test-gate cycle under (a) the legacy test-batched path and (b) the new background primitive, on the same commit. The epic closure comment records both tool-call counts and total tokens consumed"
- When this story is complete, the closure comment documents that the new path completed in ≤3 tool calls AND reduced tokens by ≥50% vs the legacy path on the same suite

← Satisfies: "Acceptance: the new path completes in ≤3 tool calls (1 dispatch + ≤2 drains) and reduces tokens by ≥50% vs the legacy path on the same suite. Failure to meet either threshold blocks epic closure pending approach revision"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
### Considerations

- [Testing] The specific canary workload (suite or file-edit trigger) must be pinned and recorded alongside the numbers so future regression tests are comparable — reviewer-flagged minor refinement from brainstorm
- [Reliability] This is the SC that can block epic closure; run it before S9 docs update so docs reflect measured outcomes

content.text: ## Context

The existing kudos system (Epics 3e9b-afee and 71df-5bd8) includes 5 triggers that silently skip on non-Python stacks. T7 uses Python ast.NodeVisitor. T9 uses ruff (Python-only). T12 uses Python-anchored regexes. T13 and T4 use Python ast.dump() subtree hashing. Ruby and JavaScript developers receive zero kudos from these 5 triggers. This epic replaces them with polyglot equivalents so kudos fires across all supported stacks.
## Success Criteria
- T7 uses lizard -ENS instead of Python ast.NodeVisitor; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java; 30s timeout; --exclude for test dirs; when lizard absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal
- T9 reads commands.lint (from Epic B); when absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED; when present, fires on zero-violation result
- T12 uses line-start-anchored regexes covering Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java syntax for commented-out code detection
- T13 and T4 use jscpd (JSON reporter to temp dir, 30s timeout, exit code parsing); when jscpd absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- All five triggers emit machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal conforming to the signal format established by Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8); no shared library imported from Kudos Epic 2
## Closure Checks
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `commands.lint` (dso-config.conf, written by Epic B / 3818-310d) | `/dso:onboarding` writes per detected stack at project setup | Operator edit; re-onboarding APPENDS new stacks, never overwrites existing | T9 trigger reads at evaluation time | N/A — persistent per-stack config; key removed only if stack itself is removed from project |

| `TRIGGER_SKIPPED` signal format (shared with Kudos Epic 2) | Each polyglot trigger emits this format when its tool is absent (per the spec) | Format is versioned via `schema_version` field; breaking changes bump version + migration | Kudos Epic 2's aggregator consumes and surfaces in retro | N/A — wire-format protocol; retired only via formal schema version bump with consumer migration |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -E '^commands\.lint=' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the key with a sensible default OR an empty value that's documented as "stack-specific, set by /dso:onboarding".
- `grep -nE 'TRIGGER_SKIPPED|schema_version' <plugin-kudos-trigger-scripts>` confirms the signal format is emitted with explicit version field.

- Validation: sprint acceptance test environment has lizard and jscpd installed; test matrix covers all 5 triggers before/after on non-Python files; before: no kudos for Ruby file; after: kudos fires for quality improvement; Kudos Epic 1 must be present in CI or dispatch_kudos_trigger() mocked
## Dependencies
- Epic B (3818-310d): T9 reads commands.lint; without Epic B, T9 always emits TRIGGER_SKIPPED
- Kudos Epic 1 (3e9b-afee): T13 and T7 call the kudos dispatch function delivered by Kudos Epic 1; runtime blocking dependency (blocks relationship in ticket system)
- Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8): runtime consumer dependency — Epic C conforms to TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format so the existing event emitter can handle it
## Approach

Replace each of the 5 Python-specific trigger implementations with polyglot equivalents: lizard for AST-based nesting analysis (T7), jscpd for duplicate block detection (T13/T4), language-neutral regexes for commented-out code (T12), and commands.lint config key for lint-clean detection (T9). All triggers emit TRIGGER_SKIPPED when required tooling or config is absent.
## Research Findings
- External integration (lizard): -ENS flags emit nesting/size metrics; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java, C/C++; `command -v lizard` absence detection; 30s subprocess timeout required

- External integration (jscpd): JSON reporter to temp dir (`--reporters json --output <dir>`); exit code 0 = no duplicates, 1 = duplicates found; parse via `cat <dir>/jscpd-report.json` (file-based, not stdout); 30s subprocess timeout required
- Dependency (commands.lint from Epic B 3818-310d): polyglot lint config key; absent → TRIGGER_SKIPPED; present → fires on zero-violation exit
- Signal format (TRIGGER_SKIPPED): conforms to Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) signal format independently — schema duplicated, not imported, to preserve epic independence
## Scenario Analysis
- lizard binary absent in CI (high, deployment): T7 voids awards; TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal emitted per Kudos Epic 2 schema; document or accept skip as designed
- jscpd binary absent in CI (high, deployment): T13/T4 void awards; TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal emitted per Kudos Epic 2 schema; document or accept skip as designed
- commands.lint key absent from dso-config.conf (high, configuration): T9 always emits TRIGGER_SKIPPED; onboarding/architect-foundation must populate this key per detected stack
- lizard/jscpd subprocess exceeds 30s timeout (medium, runtime): kill and treat as TRIGGER_SKIPPED; explicit timeout handling required with SIGKILL after grace period

- TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format drift from Kudos Epic 2 schema (high, integration): format validated independently per epic; schema change in Epic 2 silently breaks Epic C signals — add schema conformance test in this epic
- T12 regex false-positive on language-specific block comments (medium, correctness): Python `"""`, Ruby `=begin/=end`, JS `/** */` need language-aware anchors beyond simple line-start matching
## Risk Register (from preplanning)
- Testing (03d4-062a, 988f-933e): External binaries need subprocess mocking
- Maintainability (all story): TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format must conform to Kudos Epic 2 schema independently
- Reliability (a1f9-2e8b): dispatch_kudos_trigger() from Kudos Epic 1 must be present or mocked in acceptance env
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (lizard, jscpd CLIs), dependency on another epic (Epic B commands.lint key, Kudos Epic 2 signal schema)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 6
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-commit polyglot triggers; not volume-sensitive

content.text: ## Story C: Test-gate recording scripts consume `commands.test_runner` (replace hardcoded pytest)
### Description

**What**: Update the test-gate recording script (hardcoded `python3 -m pytest`) and the test-gate exemption script (hardcoded `python3 -m pytest "$NODE_ID"`) to read `commands.test_runner` and invoke it with the target test path. This is the behavioral payoff — Ruby and JS projects get real test-gate signal from this story.

**Why**: Today `.rb` and `.js`/`.ts` files produce no test-gate signal because the recording script skips the hardcoded pytest call for non-Python files. Ruby and JS projects appear to pass the gate while their tests are never actually run.
**Scope**:
- IN: both hardcoded pytest call sites replaced with config-key reads, exit-code propagation preserved (0=pass, non-zero=fail), centrality-aware tier mapping unchanged
- OUT: per-file gate (Story E), reinstall-hooks.sh precondition change (Story D), config-absent warning path (covered by library helper if needed)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, neither script contains a hardcoded `python3 -m pytest` invocation

← Satisfies: "record-test-status.sh routes .rb, .js, .ts files to commands.test_runner instead of hardcoded python3/pytest" + "record-test-exemption.sh uses commands.test_runner instead of hardcoded python3 -m pytest"
- When this story is complete, recording on a `.rb` source file in a Ruby-detected project invokes `$commands.test_runner` and captures its exit code as the test result
← Satisfies: "record-test-status.sh routes .rb, .js, .ts files to commands.test_runner"
- When this story is complete, the recording script emits an actionable `[DSO WARN]` when `commands.test_runner` is missing at gate execution time and skips (does not silently pass)
← Satisfies: epic Scenario Analysis "commands.test_runner absent at gate execution time"
### Considerations
- [Testing] Mock `commands.test_runner` in unit tests; do NOT invoke real pytest/rspec/jest
- [Reliability] Exit code 0/non-zero contract identical across pytest/RSpec/Jest (confirmed in epic Research Findings); no per-runner special-casing required
- [Testing] Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Replace the Python-specific ast.NodeVisitor implementation of T7 with a lizard-based approach using `lizard -ENS` to measure cognitive complexity (nesting depth) across all supported stacks. Emit TRIGGER_SKIPPED when lizard is not on PATH.

**Why**: T7 today can only measure nesting depth in Python files. Ruby and JavaScript developers who reduce deeply-nested code receive zero kudos. Lizard supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, and Java, making it the natural polyglot replacement.
**Scope**:

- IN: `lizard -ENS` subprocess with 30s timeout; `--exclude` flag for test directories; compare before/after nesting depth from git diff; TRIGGER_SKIPPED when `lizard` not on PATH; TRIGGER_SKIPPED on non-zero lizard exit; award kudos when nesting depth decreases
- OUT: Installing lizard in CI (covered by SC6 / Story E); T9, T12, T13, T4
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, T7 fires and awards kudos on a JS/TS file where nesting depth decreased (measured by lizard), and does NOT fire on a file where nesting depth increased or stayed flat
← Satisfies: "T7 uses lizard -ENS instead of Python ast.NodeVisitor; supports Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java"
- When this story is complete, T7 emits a machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal (not an exception) when `lizard` is not found on PATH
← Satisfies: "when lizard absent: TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal"
- When this story is complete, T7 does not hang — subprocess call enforces 30s timeout; timeout → TRIGGER_SKIPPED
← Satisfies: "30s timeout"
- When this story is complete, test directories are excluded from lizard analysis (`--exclude` passed for dirs matching test/spec patterns)
← Satisfies: "--exclude for test dirs"
- When this story is complete, the TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal fields conform to Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) schema; no shared library imported from Kudos Epic 2
← Satisfies: "All five triggers emit machine-readable TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for: PATH-absent case (TRIGGER_SKIPPED), timeout case (TRIGGER_SKIPPED), nesting-decrease case (award), nesting-flat/increase case (no award)
## Considerations
- [Testing] Mock `subprocess.run` (or equivalent) to avoid requiring lizard binary in test environment; test PATH-absent, timeout, zero-exit-code-with-no-decrease, and award-path cases
- [Maintainability] TRIGGER_SKIPPED signal format: reference Kudos Epic 2 (71df-5bd8) for the required field schema; implement independently (no import from Kudos Epic 2 modules)
- [Reliability] dispatch_kudos_trigger() from Kudos Epic 1 (3e9b-afee) must be mocked in unit tests
- [Reliability] Timeout handling: subprocess timeout=30 must be caught and converted to TRIGGER_SKIPPED, not propagated as an exception
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** $(git rev-parse HEAD)
* **session:** intent-fidelity-pipeline Phase 2 implementation, worktree-20260526-204435
* **plugin:** dso-dev v1.17.84
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

Per REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Step 3: "You MUST run this command and use its output. Do NOT select a tier based on your assessment of diff complexity or file types — the classifier computes the tier deterministically from the diff." Per Step 4: "Inline dispatch is mandatory — dso:* labels are agent file identifiers, NOT subagent_type values." The model from the agent file frontmatter is authoritative.
#### Actual Behavior
During the Phase 2 review cycle, the orchestrator:
1. **Skipped the classifier** — looked at the diff (4 files, 64 lines) and manually selected light tier. This is the exact failure mode Step 3's HARD-GATE was designed to prevent.

2. **Used wrong dispatch form** — passed `subagent_type: "dso:code-reviewer-light"` directly instead of reading the agent file verbatim and using `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` with the file content as prompt.
3. **Used wrong model** — dispatched with `model: sonnet` when `dso:code-reviewer-light` has `model: haiku` in its frontmatter. The workflow says "Model is non-negotiable."

The same dispatch-form error occurred on all Phase 1 reviews as well (using `subagent_type: "dso:code-reviewer-standard"` directly instead of inline dispatch). The named subagent_type happened to resolve via the agent registry, but it bypassed the verbatim-content requirement.
### 3. Action History
| Step | Component | Action | Result |
| 1 | orchestrator | Assessed diff as "small" | Skipped classifier |
| 2 | orchestrator | Dispatched dso:code-reviewer-light via subagent_type | Wrong dispatch form |
| 3 | orchestrator | Used model: sonnet | Wrong model (should be haiku) |
### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The orchestrator optimized for speed over process compliance. The diff was genuinely small (prompt/skill text changes only), which made the shortcut feel justified. But the classifier exists precisely because "looks simple" is not a reliable indicator of review complexity — the very premise of the intent-fidelity-pipeline being implemented in this session.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* **Calling skill:** /dso:review (invoked manually during commit workflow)
* **Affected workflow:** REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Steps 3 and 4

* **Root cause:** The orchestrator's instructions in REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md are clear, but the orchestrator rationalized skipping them under time pressure. The HARD-GATE text is present but not mechanically enforced — it relies on the orchestrator following instructions, which is the same behavioral-only enforcement pattern the intent-fidelity-pipeline is designed to replace.
### Suggested Fix Directions
1. **Mechanical enforcement of classifier dispatch**: The classifier step could write a marker file that Step 4 checks before accepting a dispatch. Without the marker, the dispatch is rejected.

2. **Mechanical enforcement of inline dispatch**: The review gate could validate that the reviewer-findings.json was produced by an agent whose prompt starts with the canonical agent file content (hash check).
3. **Behavioral reinforcement**: Add the classifier-skip incident to KNOWN-ISSUES.md as a recurring pattern so future sessions see the warning.

content.text: ## Context

Multi-agent DSO sessions today coordinate via opaque `[LOCK]` placeholder tickets created by `agent-batch-lifecycle.sh:436` — an ad hoc convention that provides no typed semantics for claiming work, signaling availability, or passing messages between agents. The beads project (steveyegge/beads) provides first-class `claim`, `ready`, and inter-agent messaging primitives over its event log. This epic adds equivalent DSO-native primitives built on the existing event-sourced log — not a parallel mechanism — so all coordination is auditable through the same reducer pipeline as regular ticket state.
Agent-to-agent messages are distinct from COMMENT events in that they have a sender, a recipient (agent role or specific claim), a read state, and can gate agent behavior until delivery.
## Success Criteria

- `ticket claim <id>` performs an atomic compare-and-swap on the ticket assignee field: succeeds only if assignee is currently unset or held by the caller; exits non-zero with a clear error otherwise.
- Existing `[LOCK]` placeholder tickets replaced with typed `Agent:Coordination`-reporter tickets or a distinct CLAIM event type; `agent-batch-lifecycle.sh` migrated to the new mechanism.
- New MESSAGE event type (or typed COMMENT subtype) records sender, recipient, body, and read state; reducer computes unread queue per agent.
- `ticket messages <id> [--unread]` prints messages addressed to the calling agent; `ticket messages --ack <message-uuid>` marks read.
- Stale-claim TTL: claims older than a configurable threshold (default 4 hours) are auto-released on next `ticket claim` attempt with an audit event.
- Sprint orchestration integrates the new primitives: dispatched sub-agents claim their ticket on start, emit a completion MESSAGE on finish, and release the claim on landing.
## Approach

Extend the reducer schema with a `claim` field (holder + timestamp) and an unread-messages queue. Add `ticket-claim.sh` and `ticket-messages.sh` subcommands implemented as thin shims over a shared Python library (leverages epic 78fc-3858 sourceable lib). Introduce a CLAIM event type with CAS semantics (rejects if current holder != expected). Introduce a MESSAGE event type indexed by recipient. Migrate `agent-batch-lifecycle.sh` atomically.
## Dependencies
- Depends on Epic 1 (3e74-56da): ID hardening and concurrent-merge safety must land first before CAS semantics are robust.
- Coordinates with Epic 4 (reporter/resolution): MESSAGE sender field uses the same reporter enum.
## Out of Scope
- Cross-repo agent coordination
- Real-time notifications (push) — messages are pull-only
- Priority queues for messages

content.text: Context: The /dso:roadmap skill reads design-notes.md for project archetypes and golden paths but never writes captured design intent back to the file. When a non-engineer runs /dso:roadmap immediately after the bootstrap installer, design-notes.md contains template stubs (vision: 'TBD', archetypes: []). Roadmap captures vision and archetype information during Phase 0 intake but discards it; downstream skills (/dso:brainstorm, /dso:sprint) then operate on stale stubs rather than actual project intent. This epic adds a write-back step to /dso:roadmap Phase 0 that persists captured design intent into design-notes.md.

Approach: Modify /dso:roadmap SKILL.md to add a Phase 0 write-back step immediately after intake completes. Stub detection rule (authoritative definition): a field value is a stub if it matches '' (empty string), 'TBD', 'TODO', 'PLACEHOLDER', null, or [] (empty array). Non-stub values are preserved unchanged. Also update check-onboarding.sh to evaluate design field content against the stub detection rule (not just file existence). Cross-skill schema dependency: design-notes.md schema is co-owned by /dso:onboarding; any future onboarding field additions must be reflected in the write-back logic — document this coupling in plugins/dso/docs/SCHEMA-COUPLING.md.
Success Criteria:

1. After a roadmap session where the user provides a vision statement, design-notes.md is updated with the captured vision value; for projects with no UI component (no src/app/ or pages/ directory present), the archetypes field is not required and may remain at its existing value.
2. A non-stub value already present in design-notes.md (any value not matching the stub detection rule) is not overwritten when roadmap runs the write-back step.
3. A stub value (matching the stub detection rule: '', 'TBD', 'TODO', 'PLACEHOLDER', null, or []) in design-notes.md is replaced with the roadmap-captured value after Phase 0 completes.

4. check-onboarding.sh is updated (as part of this epic) to evaluate design fields for non-stub content — a design-notes.md with all stub values returns design_onboarding.pass == false; a design-notes.md with real values (as written by roadmap write-back) returns design_onboarding.pass == true.

5. A new integration test at tests/integration/test_roadmap_writeback.sh exists and passes green; the test: (a) simulates a roadmap Phase 0 session capturing a vision value by invoking the write-back step directly with a fixture input (vision string + archetype list) bypassing interactive intake, (b) asserts design-notes.md is written with that value, (c) asserts a pre-existing non-stub value is not overwritten, (d) asserts a stub value is overwritten; this test is written RED-first before any implementation.
Scenario Analysis (5 surviving red team scenarios):
- Stub detection false positive on intentionally short values (medium, runtime): project acronym 'TBD' classified as stub and overwritten
- Write-back fails silently when design-notes.md is read-only (high, runtime): must surface as hard stop, not silent continue
- Schema mismatch on bootstrapped repos with different field layout (medium, deployment): renamed/nested fields cause silent no-op merge
- Single-element stub array bypasses empty-array rule (medium, configuration): archetypes: ['TBD'] is non-empty, preserved as real content
- Multi-line vision string breaks YAML serialization (high, configuration): must use YAML-aware serialization, not string interpolation

Prompt Alignment: LLM-specific risks — value hallucination (LLM fills stubs with plausible-but-wrong values; SKILL.md must anchor each written value to intake transcript); over-eager stub detection (TODO-as-note values must be protected by non-empty sentence guard). Add read-back verification step after write.

Dependencies: 'DSO NextJS Starter: one-command bootstrap for non-engineer prototyping' (primary epic) must complete first — it establishes the stub-initialized design-notes.md in the installed template. check-onboarding.sh content update is scoped into this epic (not a prerequisite).
Priority: Value=3 (Measurable — removes re-prompt friction for non-engineer persona), Effort=3 (Moderate — SKILL.md modification + check-onboarding.sh update + integration test) -> P2

content.text: ## Context

After merging PR #37 (epic 4e55-a6ba), the `merge-to-main-pr.sh` script can detect CI check failures and merge conflicts, but exits with code 1 on any failure — leaving the user to manually diagnose and fix. This means the "agent-driven merge" promise is incomplete: the agent can create the PR, resolve review threads, and poll for CI status, but cannot remediate failures autonomously. Engineers must manually read CI logs, identify the failing check, fix the code, push a new commit, and re-trigger CI — exactly the toil the merge workflow was designed to eliminate.
## Success Criteria

- SC1: The remediation loop classifies CI check failures into four tiers — Tier 1 (llm-review, consumes reviewer-findings.json from CI artifacts), Tier 2 (test failures, consumes pytest/jest output from CI artifacts or gh run view logs), Tier 3 (lint/format failures, consumes ruff/eslint output from CI artifacts or logs), Tier 4 (other/unknown, captures check name and raw log tail) — and dispatches the appropriate fix strategy per tier. Tier definitions and normalizer format are specified in lib/ci-findings-normalize.sh.

- SC2: The remediation loop detects "merge conflict" PR status (via gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus or equivalent) and dispatches /dso:resolve-conflicts before re-triggering CI checks. If conflict resolution fails, the loop emits ESCALATION_REASON: "Conflict resolution failed" and exits to user escalation without retrying.

- SC3: Each tier maintains an independent attempt counter (ceiling: 5 per tier). A cross-tier regression (e.g., a Tier 1 fix breaks Tier 2) resets the regressed tier's counter to 0. A global ceiling of 15 total attempts across all tiers prevents infinite loops from cross-tier resets. At attempt 4 of any tier, budget-pressure context is injected into the sub-agent prompt ("This is attempt 4 of 5 — if you cannot resolve this finding, return ESCALATE with a clear explanation"). CANNOT_PROCEED is returned if the sub-agent signals it lacks capability. /dso:oscillation-check runs when the same files are targeted on attempt 2+. All counters and phase state persist in the merge-to-main state file for SIGURG resume safety.

- SC4: On exhaustion of any tier's ceiling, global ceiling, CANNOT_PROCEED, or oscillation detection, the loop exits with a structured JSON escalation payload written to stdout containing: tiers_attempted (array of tier names), attempts_per_tier (object mapping tier to count), remaining_findings (array of unresolved finding summaries), stop_reason (enum: TIER_CEILING | GLOBAL_CEILING | CANNOT_PROCEED | OSCILLATION | THROTTLE_PAUSE | CONFLICT_RESOLUTION_FAILED | ARTIFACT_MISSING), and suggested_next_step (human-readable string). The script exits with a distinct exit code (exit 2) differentiating remediation exhaustion from pre-remediation failure (exit 1).

- SC5: The full remediation loop (poll → classify → normalize → dispatch → push → re-poll) runs end-to-end in a sprint session against a branch with an injected CI failure (at least one tier), producing either FIXES_APPLIED with a green CI re-run or a structured escalation payload with correct stop_reason.
## Dependencies
Epic 4e55-a6ba (PR-merge mode + enforcement strategy) — the remediation phase is inserted after the poll phase added by that epic.
## Approach

New _phase_remediate function inside merge-to-main-pr.sh, inserted after _phase_poll's failure path. A sourced helper library (lib/ci-findings-normalize.sh) converts CI artifacts from each tier into the review-fix-dispatch findings format, enabling reuse of the existing review-fix-dispatch sub-agent for all tiers. Merge conflicts are handled by dispatching the existing /dso:resolve-conflicts skill. The remediation phase inherits the existing state file persistence pattern for SIGURG resume safety.

Architectural decision: No worktree isolation for remediation commits — fixes are pushed directly to the PR branch so CI re-runs reflect the actual merge target. This is consistent with the review-fix-dispatch ISOLATION PROHIBITION and follows the same pattern as _phase_resolve_threads.
## Scenario Analysis
### Addressed Scenarios

1. **Cross-tier regression loop** (critical): A Tier 1 fix breaks Tier 2 tests, Tier 2 fix breaks Tier 1 review — creating an infinite ping-pong. Mitigated by: global ceiling of 15 total attempts, oscillation detection via /dso:oscillation-check on same-file re-targeting, cross-tier regression counter reset with global cap.

2. **CI artifact not uploaded** (important): Repository CI workflow doesn't include upload-artifact steps for test/lint output. Mitigated by: Tier 2/3 normalizer falls back to gh run view log parsing; Tier 4 captures raw log tail. ARTIFACT_MISSING stop_reason when no parseable output exists for any tier.
3. **Stale artifact from previous run** (important): gh run download fetches artifacts from wrong run. Mitigated by: pinning download to the specific failed run ID from the poll phase, not "latest".

4. **SIGURG during remediation** (important): Claude Code sends SIGURG mid-fix. Mitigated by: all counters and phase state persist in existing state file; --resume flag continues from remediation checkpoint.

5. **Rate limit / throttle during sub-agent dispatch** (important): Usage-aware throttling returns MAX_AGENTS: 0. Mitigated by: THROTTLE_PAUSE stop_reason in escalation payload; remediation state preserved for manual retry.

6. **Conflict resolution partial success** (moderate): /dso:resolve-conflicts resolves some conflicts but not all. Mitigated by: checking merge state after resolution; if conflicts remain, emit ESCALATION_REASON without retry.

7. **Fix commit breaks unrelated check** (moderate): Remediation fix for Tier 3 introduces a Tier 2 regression. Mitigated by: cross-tier regression detection resets regressed tier counter; global ceiling prevents unbounded retries.

8. **Empty findings after normalization** (moderate): CI check failed but normalizer produces zero findings (e.g., infrastructure flake, timeout). Mitigated by: Tier 4 fallback captures check name + raw log tail; if still empty, emit CANNOT_PROCEED.

9. **Multiple tiers fail simultaneously** (moderate): Initial CI run fails on Tier 1 + Tier 2 + Tier 3. Mitigated by: tiers processed in priority order (1→2→3→4); each tier's fixes pushed and CI re-polled before advancing to next tier.

10. **Sub-agent returns FAIL but code is partially modified** (moderate): review-fix-dispatch returns RESOLUTION_RESULT: FAIL with uncommitted partial changes. Mitigated by: on FAIL, revert source changes (git checkout -- files) per review-fix-dispatch contract Step 4; increment attempt counter; retry with clean state.
### Cross-Epic Interaction Signals (consideration-level)

12 consideration-level signals identified from cross-epic scan against open/in-progress epics. Key interactions: shared merge-to-main-pr.sh state file format (epic 4e55-a6ba), CI workflow artifact upload requirements (create-dso-app template), review-fix-dispatch contract dependency (review workflow epics), oscillation-check integration (existing debug tooling).
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: retry/bounding policy design (autonomous agent fix-attempt limits)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 10 (of 14 red team findings)
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: not applicable (no volume decision)

content.text: EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural
## Context

Agents running design-review, ui-designer, brainstorm, preplanning, and sprint workflows currently operate without a shared corpus of UI/UX design knowledge. Each session starts without government-specific anti-patterns, USWDS component guidance, WCAG 2.2 compliance patterns, or established design principles, causing inconsistent and incomplete guidance. This epic establishes the foundational reference library — schema, corpus structure, full initial content, retrieval infrastructure, and source provenance tracking — that five subsequent epics will integrate into specific agent workflows. It absorbs the government anti-pattern catalog from epic 17de-a47a, seeds the full corpus from permissively licensed and Nava-internal sources, and establishes the retrieval contract (ref-query.sh) that all downstream integration epics depend on.
## Success Criteria

- A corpus directory at plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/ with domain-partitioned Markdown files (each ≤500 lines), YAML frontmatter per entry (id, title, domain[], component[], action[], compliance[], severity, story_type[], coverage, source, license), and three Markdown resolution tiers per entry (### Summary, ### Detail, ### Implementation). A _schema.yaml + check-corpus-schema.sh pre-commit hook enforce tag vocabulary across six dimensions: domain, component, action, compliance, severity, story_type. Domain vocabulary includes gov-benefit-flows. License vocabulary includes internal-nava (content from internal Nava sources committed verbatim; restricted to internal use).

- A _index.yaml manifest committed to the repository (not generated at build time), listing every entry with six-dimension tags, one-liner, file path, coverage tier, source, and license. Full inventory readable without loading any corpus file. Regenerated and recommitted on corpus changes.

- A plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh retrieval script using stdlib Python BM25 (self-contained, no external deps); bm25s used as optional performance accelerator if installed, falls back with stderr notice if not. Flags: --top-n (default 8), --tier=summary|detail|implementation, --session-hash dedup, zero-result stderr signal ([ref-query: no results for query: "..." with filters: ...]), completes within 10 seconds.

- Initial corpus covers the following content domains: (a) Government benefit application form patterns (domain: gov-benefit-flows) — one-question-per-page template and sub-patterns (repeatable items, stacking, looping, people list, someone-else option, I-dont-know option, grouping, optional answer); multi-step task list with linear/non-linear support and conditional logic; review page patterns (inline vs. section editing, accordion for long forms, minimal-submit); validation and error messages (dual-location errors, accessibility copy standards, no bottom-of-page errors, arbitrary-validity anti-pattern); claim/application status page (five most common claimant questions, deadline clarity, contact center alignment); document upload (mobile camera vs. desktop upload vs. third-party SDK trade-offs, vendor lock-in risk, camera onboarding pattern); mobile responsiveness (44px touch targets, 16px minimum font, help text over tooltips, reduce-typing-on-mobile principle); confirmation, e-signature, SSN collection, draft/resume, people composition, rights and responsibilities; paid leave application patterns across state PFML programs; employer dashboard, role-based access control, third-party administrator patterns; (b) Government benefit policy context (domain: gov-benefit-flows) — full SNAP lifecycle (application, interview, verification, eligibility, certification, reporting, recertification, program integrity) with state option variants and unhappy-path client flows; (c) Accessibility patterns (domain: accessibility) — WCAG 2.2 AAA patterns cross-referenced to Section 508/OMB M-24-08; 7-category government accessibility test checklist (content accuracy, content structure, responsiveness, keyboard navigation, screen reader, automated checks, time-based media); note that automated tools catch only 20-60% of issues; axe-core and Pa11y integration patterns; (d) Design principles and heuristics (domain: principles) — Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, Don Norman's principles, GOV.UK Government Design Principles, 18F UX Guide principles, digital.gov federal requirements, Inclusive Design Principles; (e) Anti-patterns (domain: anti-patterns) — 48 government UI/UX anti-patterns (from 17de-a47a at Detail tier; Implementation stretch); Brignull dark pattern taxonomy; SageSELab AidUI 27-class taxonomy; UX anti-patterns from CA EDD, NJ UI, and USDOL projects (users gaming eligibility questions, recertification deadline failure, state-to-state variation constraints); trauma-informed design anti-patterns (institutional trauma perpetuation, safety/trustworthiness/empowerment/cultural-sensitivity failures); (f) Behavioral and cognitive patterns (domain: patterns) — cognitive load checklists, defensive design checklists, representative entries from principles.design; (g) USWDS component and token guidance (domain: components) — USWDS v3 components and design tokens; react-uswds architectural rationale; USWDS selection decision record; (h) Federal copy and plain language (domain: gov-copy) — USWDS forms copy; GOV.UK error/form patterns and Service Manual writing guidance; VA.gov Content Style Guide (error anatomy, capitalization, punctuation); 18F Plain Language guide; Federal Plain Language Guidelines; CDC reading-level guidance; each entry carries a stable rule ID, prior-art citation, and precedence field; (i) Agentic design patterns (domain: patterns) — multi-level transparency for AI caseworker tools (status indicator, tool call log, data source labels); human-in-the-loop interaction patterns; persistent intervention controls; plain language do/don't pairs for agentic interfaces. Summary + Detail required for all entries; Implementation is stretch.

- Integration test at tests/integration/test-ref-library.sh (REPO_ROOT-based paths): (a) session-timeout query returns entry tagged auth/forms or containing "session timeout" in Summary; (b) --tier=summary output has ### Summary, no ### Implementation; (c) manifest integrity — every _index.yaml entry resolves to a file at its declared path; (d) no corpus file exceeds 500 lines; (e) precision sub-test — three representative queries ("USWDS form validation", "WCAG 2.2 keyboard navigation", "government authentication anti-pattern") each return a top result whose frontmatter tags match a predefined expected-tag mapping; (f) completes within 10 seconds.
- ref-query.sh registered as dso ref-query shim; check-shim-refs.sh does not block downstream skill file references.

- A docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml file at the project root tracks each reference source with fields: name, url, type (github-repo|github-repo-private|confluence-page|confluence-space|google-doc|web-spec|website), access (public|internal-nava), credentials_required (bool), pinned version/commit (where applicable), last-synced date, license, and which corpus domains it populates. Internal sources (Confluence pages, Google Docs, private GitHub repos) are supported first-class. navapbc/benefits-delivery-system is registered as type: github-repo-private, credentials_required: true, access: internal-nava, with a note that it is a rich source of benefits delivery design and implementation context pending credentials provisioning. This is the provenance record for all corpus entries.

- Initial corpus includes federal-style-canon entries for government UI copy editing — covering USWDS forms, GOV.UK error/form patterns and Service Manual writing for user interfaces, VA.gov Content Style Guide (error anatomy, capitalization, punctuation), 18F Plain Language guide, Federal Plain Language Guidelines (Plain Writing Act of 2010), and CDC reading-level guidance. Each entry carries a stable rule ID, a prior-art citation, and a precedence field. Required by depending epic f360-3a5b-b8f3-4f86 (gov-copy-writer sub-agent).
## Closure Checks
All success criteria are verifiable within the closing session (directory/file existence checks, script invocation, test run). No items required routing here via the session-infeasibility check.
## Dependencies
- Epic 17de-a47a: 48 anti-patterns (see ticket 17de-a47a description) copied at implementation start; closed as superseded on this epic's completion. Does not block this epic.
- No new runtime dependencies — stdlib BM25 implementation is self-contained.

- Downstream epics 2-6: Unblocked only after SC3 and SC5 pass. This epic must merge to main before downstream skill files reference plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh (pre-commit referential integrity enforcement).
## Approach

Option A — Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, domain-partitioned under plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/ (e.g., anti-patterns/auth.md, gov-benefit-flows/question-page.md, components/uswds-patterns.md). _index.yaml manifest committed to repo. ref-query.sh (stdlib BM25, optional bm25s accelerator) registered as dso ref-query shim. docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml at project root tracks all source provenance — public and internal. Internal Nava content committed verbatim with license: internal-nava. Only script output enters agent context — corpus files never loaded directly. All five downstream integration epics call .claude/scripts/dso ref-query.
## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/` corpus files | Story 9fee-6947 creates directory + seed entries; stories f5bd-27a9, fab0-d0e2, 5a09-615c, 6c26-4321, c642-4840 populate domains | Any sprint story adding corpus entries (manual authoring + commit) | `ref-query.sh` at query time; `check-corpus-schema.sh` at pre-commit | Never retired — persists for project lifetime |

| `plugins/dso/data/ui-reference/_schema.yaml` | Story 9fee-6947 | Vocabulary additions (e.g., new domain tags); requires check-corpus-schema.sh re-validation across full corpus | `check-corpus-schema.sh` pre-commit hook | Never retired |

| `plugins/dso/scripts/ref-query.sh` | Story 9fee-6947 (stdlib BM25 path) | Story 40a2-d037 adds bm25s accelerator path | All 5 downstream integration epics via `dso ref-query` shim; integration test cfa6-6c7f | Never retired — downstream epics depend on it permanently |

| `dso ref-query` shim entry | Story 9fee-6947 registers shim | Never — shim is static after registration | All downstream skill files that call `.claude/scripts/dso ref-query`; check-shim-refs.sh | Never retired |
| `check-corpus-schema.sh` in .pre-commit-config.yaml | Story 9fee-6947 registers hook | Never | Pre-commit hook runner on every corpus file edit | Never retired |
| `plugins/dso/data/**` in plugin-boundary-allowlist.conf | Story 9fee-6947 adds allowlist entry | Never | Plugin boundary pre-commit hook (every commit touching corpus paths) | Never retired |

| `docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml` | Story 9fee-6947 creates with all planned sources | Any story adding new source; future corpus contributor adding BDS entries | Documentation consumers; corpus contributors; docs/ui-reference-sources.yaml integrity check | Never retired |
## Scenario Analysis
- bm25s corpus load time timeout (high, runtime): addressed by SC3 10s target and SC5f timing check
- Tag pre-filter zero matches silently (high, runtime): addressed by SC3 zero-result stderr signal and SC1 vocabulary enforcement
- Missing _index.yaml on fresh checkout (critical, deployment): addressed by SC2 committed-not-generated requirement
- Integration test paths break in worktree sessions (high, deployment): addressed by SC5 REPO_ROOT-based path resolution
- Pre-commit integrity blocks downstream skill refs before merge (high, deployment): addressed by Dependencies merge-ordering note
- shim-exempt not applied to ref-query.sh (medium, deployment): addressed by SC6 shim registration
- YAML vocabulary drift causes silent retrieval gaps (high, configuration): addressed by SC1 schema file and check-corpus-schema.sh
- Internal Confluence source inaccessible in CI (medium, deployment): corpus content committed verbatim to repo; Confluence access not required at runtime or in CI

- Private GitHub repo (BDS) inaccessible without credentials (medium, deployment): addressed by credentials_required flag in ui-reference-sources.yaml; corpus seeding from BDS deferred to a contributor with provisioned access
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered — novel architectural pattern (BM25 corpus retrieval); re-triggered via gate for design tutorials and GitHub reference material research
- Bright-line conditions fired: novel architectural pattern, unfamiliar dependency (bm25s — resolved to stdlib implementation)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered — 8 of 14 scenarios survived blue team filter

- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered — follow-ons created as placeholders at user direction
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered
- Scale context (Step 0): small scale (default) — static corpus ~200-400 entries at initial seeding, CLI invocation only, no concurrent users, 10s query budget is sufficient

- Re-brainstorm enrichment (2026-05-23): Confluence and GitHub research sub-agents added Nava-internal sources; option (a) verbatim with license: internal-nava; SC4 reorganized by content domain; gov-benefit-flows added to schema vocabulary; SC7 expanded to support internal source types; BDS registered as reference-only; EPIC_CLASS line, Closure Checks section, State Lifecycle table, and scale_context PIL field added per skill template audit.
## Research Findings

Permissively licensed repos identified for corpus seeding: uswds/uswds (CC0), SteveBarnett/Checklists (MIT), benbrignell/principles.design (MIT), JenniKobylskiUX/WCAG-Accessibility-UX-Checklist (MIT), SageSELab/AidUI (MIT). navapbc/wic-participant-recertification-portal (Apache 2.0) identified as highest-value navapbc GitHub source: 10 screen-level docs covering a full user-tested government benefit recertification flow plus 10 ADRs with explicit UX rationale. navapbc/template-application-nextjs ADRs 0003+0004 document USWDS selection rationale and react-uswds trade-offs. navapbc/benefits-delivery-system is private and not accessible with current session credentials; registered as reference-only for future contributor. Nava Confluence Pattern Library (PL space, ~52 pages) is the richest single source: cross-project gov-benefit application form patterns from MA PFML, NJ UI, CA EDD, Vermont MABD, Nebraska IB, Login.gov, Maryland FAMLI, MN Paid Leave — all user-tested. Additional high-value Confluence sources: SNAP Policy Requirements hub (PM3, 17 pages), Accessibility Test Checklist (AAN), Trauma-Informed Design Practice Guide (DOH), Lessons Learned from CA EDD/NJ UI/USDOL (NUI), Agentic Design Patterns for Government Services (NL). Gap confirmed: no existing structured machine-readable government UI/UX reference catalog found — this epic fills a genuine void. Stdlib Python BM25 preferred over hard bm25s dependency at this corpus size; bm25s retained as optional accelerator.

content.text: # External-integration verification gate for /dso:fix-bug (in_review status + closure loop)
## Context

/dso:fix-bug front-loads investigation discipline — intent gate, feature-request gate, hypothesis testing, TDD RED-before-GREEN — but Phase E Step 4 only checks `$TEST_CMD`, `$LINT_CMD`, `$FORMAT_CHECK_CMD` before transitioning the bug to `closed`. For bugs whose symptom lives in an external integration (Jira bridge, GitHub Actions, hosted service) or a deployed environment (staging, production), a green local suite does not prove the symptom is gone. The Jira-bridge fix history shows ≥7 commits across multiple bug tickets, each shipped green, each followed by symptom recurrence; today's session almost shipped the 8th (bug 76d2-e46f) — the GitHub Actions workflow YAML hardcoded `ref: main` so the fix wouldn't run until merged, but unit tests had no way to surface that.

Each recurrence costs the on-call engineer 30–90 minutes of re-triage, re-filing, and context-reconstruction for the same root symptom — a sunk cost that compounds across the cluster. This epic closes the loop by introducing a new `in_review` ticket status, capturing a bug-reporter-owned Verification Plan in the create-bug template, and gating closure of external-integration bugs on observed evidence — captured in-session when possible, or via a recorded verification command run manually post-merge.

**Haiku-classifier contract.** /dso:fix-bug Phase A dispatches a haiku-tier classifier sub-agent that returns a structured response: `{"unreachable": bool, "reason": "<one-sentence>", "local_repro_step_present": bool}`. The bug is treated as requiring external verification when `unreachable=true AND local_repro_step_present=false`. When `reason` is empty or under 5 words, the orchestrator deterministically re-dispatches with sonnet (the "classifier=yes" shorthand used elsewhere in this spec means "requires external verification per this rule").

**Post-ship signal (not a sprint SC).** Zero unverified-closure recurrence events across the next 5 external-integration bug fixes is the long-term health target — audited at the end of the following debug session as a retrospective signal, NOT a gate on this sprint. The 9 numbered SCs below constitute the sprint's definition of done; this paragraph is a forward-looking monitoring note only.
## Success Criteria

1. **Routing to `in_review`**: A bug whose Phase A haiku classifier (or sonnet re-dispatch) returns `unreachable=true AND local_repro_step_present=false` (the external-verification predicate as defined in the Haiku-classifier contract in Context) AND for which Phase C/G emitted `VERIFICATION_STATUS != local_verified` transitions to `in_review` — not `closed` — at /dso:fix-bug Phase H. Verified by `dso ticket show <id> | jq -r '.status' == "in_review"` against a synthetic test bug.

2. **Verification metadata recorded**: The `in_review` ticket exposes `verification_command` and `verification_target_env` fields populated from the original bug's Verification Plan section, observable via `dso ticket show`. Both fields are non-empty strings (or the explicit ZIR placeholder `"unknown at filing time — to be defined before Phase C"` is treated as "missing" by Phase A's gate).

3. **Parent-close guard**: `dso ticket transition <epic-id> in_progress closed` exits non-zero when any direct child has status `in_review`. The error message names the `in_review` children and recommends `dso ticket reparent <bug-id> none` (using the command shipped by epic `5efb-06ea-0a65-4e96`). Until `5efb-06ea` ships, the message documents `--force` as the interim escape. The existing open-children-guard ALREADY treats new non-`CLOSED_STATUSES` values as open, so this SC is structural-message-content only — no new guard logic.

4. **`/dso:verify-fix` three-layer check**: `/dso:verify-fix <ticket-id>` runs the recorded `verification_command` (refusing to exec when the command appears to be a natural-language plan — heuristic: no leading executable token + contains spaces without shell metacharacters → prompts user to run manually instead), applies a three-layer pass/fail check (exit code + configurable stdout/stderr failure-pattern grep, default `error|fail|fatal` case-insensitive + NL-plan detection), and captures a TRUNCATED ticket-comment artifact (stdout+stderr capped at 8 KiB total per the existing comment-size guidance) including all three layer results. Transitions: all-three-layers-pass → `closed` with `--reason="Verified: <one-line>"`; any-layer-fails → `in_progress` with `--reason` recording the failing layer. `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` config key, default 120s; on timeout, transition to `in_progress` with reason `"Verification timed out — manual verification required."`

5. **`/dso:end-session` sweep — single A/B choice**: At session close, /dso:end-session lists every `in_review` bug in session-scope with its recorded `verification_command` and `verification_target_env`, then asks the user a SINGLE choice: (A) defer all to next session (each ticket gets a comment recording the deferral) OR (B) run `/dso:verify-fix` non-interactively against each in sequence. Per-bug interactive "paste evidence inline" is REMOVED from the sweep — that flow routes through standalone `/dso:verify-fix <ticket-id> --evidence="..."` invocations outside the sweep.

6. **Phase A Verification Plan gate**: `/dso:fix-bug` Phase A applies a two-prong field-level checklist to the bug's Verification Plan before dispatching Phase C investigation: (a) `verification_command` is non-empty AND starts with a shell-executable token OR contains backtick-wrapped named binary/tool/endpoint; AND (b) `verification_target_env` is non-empty AND not in the deny-list `["TBD", "N/A", "unknown", ""]`. When either check fails, Phase A pauses inline and presents a fixed structured form for the user to complete; the user's structured response is parsed and written to the ticket as `EDIT` events on the Verification Plan fields before Phase C dispatches. (Pre-existing bug tickets filed before this epic ships are exempted via a grace-period tag `verification:legacy` which Phase A respects but logs; tickets tagged `verification:legacy` are surfaced in /dso:end-session sweeps as deferred-by-default.)
7. **Bridge mapping and Jira workflow probe**: Three checks performed together as a single SC:
- **Outbound code**: `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` in `plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py` contains `"in_review": "In Review"`. Verified by grep.
- **Inbound config**: `gh variable get INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING` returns JSON containing `"In Review":"in_review"`. Verified by `gh variable get` parse.

- **Jira workflow probe (automated)**: A test fixture invokes `acli jira workitem search --jql 'project = $JIRA_PROJECT AND status = "In Review"' --limit 1` and asserts exit 0, contrasted against the same query with a known-invalid status name asserting exit 1. The fixture lives in `tests/` and runs in the test gate — not a one-time manual check. If the probe fails in CI, the bridge mapping change is rolled back and a BRIDGE_ALERT is filed.

8. **In-session dogfooding (validation signal)**: Before the epic's parent slice can be marked complete, a synthetic bug ticket is created via the updated `/dso:create-bug` flow with `verification_target_env: "staging"` (or equivalent non-local value). The synthetic bug is advanced through /dso:fix-bug, transitions to `in_review`, and an attempt to close it (`dso ticket transition <synthetic-id> in_review closed`) is rejected by the gate until /dso:verify-fix is invoked with a passing command. The full sequence is demonstrated in-session before story closure and the demonstration is captured as a ticket comment.

9. **Historical-audit signal (in-session)**: Before the epic's parent slice is marked complete, one of the ≥7 previously-reopened Jira-bridge bug tickets identified in the motivating evidence is walked through in-session: the bug's prior closure event is compared against the Phase A two-prong checklist (SC6) and the SC1 routing rule, and the walk-through is recorded as a ticket comment demonstrating that the new gate would have blocked that closure. This audit is performed and captured within the sprint session — not deferred to after merge. Confirms the gate catches the historical class of failures.
## Approach
Phased shipping in 3 slices, with an explicit contingency boundary between Slice 2 and Slice 3:

**Slice 1 — Infrastructure**: New `in_review` ticket status (event-sourced, like every other status: `ticket-transition.sh` allowlist extension; ticket-list filter default; `CLOSED_STATUSES` left unchanged so existing parent-close guard treats `in_review` as open; outbound mapping in `_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`; inbound mapping via `INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING` repo variable). `/dso:create-bug` template grows a Verification Plan section with two fields. `ticket-transition.sh` open-children guard error message enhanced. **Independently shippable.**

**Slice 2 — Gate**: /dso:fix-bug Phase A two-prong Verification Plan checklist with structured-form pause; haiku classifier dispatch with structured 3-field output + deterministic sonnet re-dispatch trigger; Phase C/G emit explicit `VERIFICATION_STATUS` field into structured handoff artifact; Phase H reads that field and routes to `in_review` (never inferring from absence). **Depends on Slice 1.**

**Slice 3 — Loop**: `/dso:verify-fix` skill with three-layer check + `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` + NL-plan detection; `/dso:end-session` A/B sweep; /dso:fix-bug opportunistic in-session verification when the target environment is reachable in the current session (e.g., post-merge `gh workflow run` — with pre-check that the target workflow declares `on: workflow_dispatch` and graceful skip when absent). **Depends on Slice 2.**

**Contingency**: If `/dso:end-session` coordination becomes blocked by the active end-session epic cluster (e7d6-8013, f27a-3c6a, fb32-215c, 71df-5bd8, f8b0-f816, e884-d0ad), Slices 1+2 ship independently and Slice 3 is deferred to a follow-on milestone. Slice 3 SCs (4, 5) are tagged `slice:3` for tracking; their deferral does not block parent-epic closure.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `in_review` ticket status | SC1 transition rule at /dso:fix-bug Phase H | SC4 /dso:verify-fix transitions in_review→closed (pass) or in_progress (fail) | SC3 parent-close guard; SC5 end-session sweep; SC8 dogfooding | N/A — status enum value, persistent within ticket-system status taxonomy |

| `verification_command` (ticket field) | Written at bug filing via /dso:create-bug Verification Plan | SC6 Phase A inline EDIT events when checklist fails | SC4 /dso:verify-fix execution | Implicit with ticket close — field persists as historical record |
| `verification_target_env` (ticket field) | Same as `verification_command` | SC6 Phase A inline EDIT events; operator | SC4 execution context; SC5 sweep display | Implicit with ticket close |
| `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (dso-config.conf key) | SC4 sets default 120s in template | Operator edit | SC4 timeout enforcement | N/A — persistent config key |

| `INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING` (GitHub repo var, JSON) | SC7 operator-set via `gh variable set` | Operator updates when Jira workflow changes | inbound-bridge.yml mapping lookup | N/A — persistent; entries retire per-entry only when Jira workflow status is removed (operator action) |

| `verification:legacy` tag | SC6 backfill at epic ship — applied to all bug tickets filed BEFORE this epic shipped | Stable (no mutation) | SC6 Phase A grace-period gate; SC5 sweep deferred-by-default | Per-ticket retirement: removed via `dso ticket untag <id> verification:legacy` when (a) the ticket's `verification_command` and `verification_target_env` both pass SC6's two-prong checklist, AND (b) the user confirms via Phase A's gate dialog. Until then, the tag persists per-ticket; the tag-class itself has no global retirement. |

| `VERIFICATION_STATUS` (handoff field, Phase C/G → Phase H) | Phase C investigator or Phase G fix-applier writes on completion | Same writers update on re-investigation | SC1 Phase H routing decision | Implicit — reset at next ticket reopen or persisted as historical record on close |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):

- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket show <synthetic-bug-id>` (from SC8 dogfooding) shows `verification_command`, `verification_target_env` populated and `status=in_review`; post-/dso:verify-fix shows `status=closed`.
- `grep -nE 'in_review|VERIFICATION_STATUS|verification:legacy' plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md` confirms every documented CONSUME reference resolves.
- `grep -n 'VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the default = 120.
Closes the audit's named gap: `verification:legacy` RETIRE = per-ticket untag after Phase A two-prong pass + user confirm.
### External-dependency verification — Jira "In Review" workflow (Probe-6 remediation, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The original 2026-05-16 pass deferred probe 6 because the audit framed it as requiring a closure-gating External Dependencies block over Jira workflow state. Reframing: `acli jira workitem search` is available in-session and SC7 already specifies an automated Jira workflow probe. Promoting SC7's probe to a structured external-dependency check:
| Resource | In-session verification command | Expected |

| Jira "In Review" status exists in target project workflow | `acli jira workitem search --jql "project = $JIRA_PROJECT AND status = "In Review"" --limit 1` | Exit 0 (status name recognized by Jira workflow) |

| Negative-case sanity check | `acli jira workitem search --jql "project = $JIRA_PROJECT AND status = "NotARealStatus"" --limit 1` | Exit 1 (proves the positive check actually distinguishes valid vs invalid status names) |
| Outbound bridge mapping in code | `grep -E '"in_review":\s*"In Review"' plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py` | Returns 0 |
| Inbound bridge mapping in repo var | `gh variable get INBOUND_STATUS_MAPPING \| jq -r '."In Review"'` | Returns `in_review` |

| BRIDGE_ALERT auto-files on Jira workflow mismatch | Synthetic test: run the SC7 fixture against a fake Jira project lacking "In Review"; assert the bridge raises a BRIDGE_ALERT ticket | Test pass before sprint close |

This converts SC7's prose into a structured verification surface. The Jira workflow itself remains externally owned by the Jira project administrator, but the dependency on its "In Review" status is detected and surfaced in-session before sprint closure rather than waiting for inbound-sync failures in production.
## Dependencies

- `depends_on 5efb-06ea-0a65-4e96` (Add ticket reparent CLI command + bulk orphan remediation). SC3's full remedy text requires `dso ticket reparent <id> none` to exist; until that lands, the error message documents `--force` as the interim escape.
## Scenario Analysis
15 surviving scenarios from red+blue team filtering. Material risks the implementation must address (full list of mitigations in approach + SCs above):
- **Classifier timeout** (`runtime`, `high`): bounded by sonnet-redispatch + interactive-prompt fallback + non-interactive `INTERACTIVITY_DEFERRED` + fail-closed default.

- **Concurrent fix-bug sessions on same ticket** (`runtime`, `high`): event-sourced reducer treats STATUS events as append-only; second session sees in_review and exits Phase H idempotently. Field writes use last-write-wins (acceptable; same-classifier produces same answer).
- **Unbounded stdout in verification_command output** (`runtime`, `medium`): 8 KiB cap (SC4) + `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (SC4).
- **End-session sweep blocks on unreachable env** (`runtime`, `medium`): A/B sweep + per-command timeout (SC5).

- **ticket-transition.sh callers unaware of `in_review`** (`deployment`, `high`): existing open-children guard treats non-CLOSED_STATUSES as open (already correct); explicit Slice 1 includes allowlist extension and ticket-list filter update.
- **Jira "In Review" status precondition** (`deployment`, `high`): SC7 automated CI probe + BRIDGE_ALERT on missing.
- **Pre-existing tickets without Verification Plan** (`deployment`, `high`): grace-period tag `verification:legacy` (SC6).
- **verification_command env context** (`configuration`, `high`): create-bug template guidance documents required env vars; verify-fix three-layer check surfaces missing-env errors clearly (SC4).
- **verification_target_env enum** (`configuration`, `medium`): deny-list at filing time + ZIR-compatible placeholder (SC6).
- **Sonnet re-dispatch criteria** (`configuration`, `medium`): deterministic 5-word-reason threshold (Context).
- **`in_review` not in ticket-list defaults** (`configuration`, `high`): Slice 1 explicitly updates ticket-list defaults.
- **Reporters writing actionable verification_command at filing** (`assumption`, `high`): ZIR placeholder + Phase A pause + structured-form re-entry (SC6).
- **"In-session evidence" undefined** (`assumption`, `high`): explicit `VERIFICATION_STATUS` field emitted by Phase C/G (Approach Slice 2).
- **Jira workflow guards on transitions** (`assumption`, `high`): SC7 automated probe + bridge-alert on transition failures; surface via existing BRIDGE_ALERT path.
- **Exit 0 ≠ symptom resolution** (`assumption`, `high`): three-layer pass/fail check (exit + failure-grep + NL-plan detection) (SC4).
## Prompt Alignment Findings
Matched signal: skill file modifications + agent definitions (haiku classifier + new /dso:verify-fix skill).
Behavioral review (bot-psychologist) produced 6 prompt-tightening recommendations, all folded into the spec above:
- Haiku classifier emits structured 3-field output with deterministic tiebreaker (Context).
- Phase C/G emit explicit `VERIFICATION_STATUS` field; Phase H reads it (avoids agent negative-existential inference) (Approach Slice 2).
- /dso:verify-fix three-layer pass check + timeout + NL-plan detection (SC4).
- Phase A two-prong field-level checklist for "concrete" verification plan (SC6).
- create-bug ZIR-compatible explicit placeholder for verification_command (SC2, SC6).
- /dso:end-session sweep simplified to A/B; per-bug "paste evidence inline" removed from sweep flow (SC5).

No open-source framework reviewed has an identical post-fix async verification gate; `in_review` status is a novel construct. LangSmith's `EvaluationResult` schema (score+reasoning+key as separate fields) is the closest prior-art pattern and informs the three-layer check in SC4.
## Research Findings

Step 2 web research was skipped. Rationale: no new third-party API (ACLI/Jira already integrated), no new dependency, no new auth/credential flow, no novel architectural pattern (status additions are an established codebase pattern; haiku classifier dispatch has in-codebase precedent at `dso:cross-epic-interaction-classifier`).

content.text: ## Context

DSO plugin developers and AI agents working on the codebase face increasing difficulty reviewing, testing, and reasoning about core infrastructure scripts. Three Python functions exceed 300 lines: bridge-outbound.py::process_outbound (629 lines), bridge-inbound.py::process_inbound (465 lines), ticket-reducer.py::reduce_ticket (353 lines). Seven files exceed 1000 lines: merge-to-main.sh (1,549), validate.sh (1,328), analyze-tool-use.py (1,225), ticket-graph.py (1,152), bridge-inbound.py (1,148), bridge-outbound.py (1,053), validate-review-output.sh (1,050). Five shell scripts have deep nesting (6+ levels): validate-review-output.sh (max 7, 280 lines), merge-to-main.sh (max 6, 124 lines), validate.sh (max 6, 118 lines), worktree-cleanup.sh (92 lines), sprint-next-batch.sh (75 lines). Additionally, 12 Python functions in the 100-180 line range should be decomposed. This epic does NOT include TODO/FIXME remediation or REVIEW-DEFENSE annotation work (owned by epic 5018-64ce).
## Success Criteria
- No Python function exceeds 180 lines
- No source file (Python or shell) exceeds 1000 lines
- No shell script nesting exceeds 6 levels (24 spaces)
- Extracted handlers organized into domain-grouped subpackages: bridge handlers to scripts/bridge/, ticket processors to scripts/ticket/, shell utilities to hooks/lib/lib-*.sh

- All existing tests pass without modification to test assertions; consumer import paths remain resolvable via re-export shims in the original entry point files or are updated in the same commit with no functional change to callers
- .test-index entries are created for all new handler modules before epic closure
## Scenario Analysis

- importlib path resolution breaks when handlers move (critical, deployment): bridge scripts resolve ticket-reducer.py via Path(__file__).parent. Original entry points must remain as dispatchers preserving sibling resolution.
- Guard clause flattening changes exception propagation (high, deployment): Nested try/except at different levels catch specific types. Flattening must audit and replicate catch semantics.
- New handler modules lack test-index coverage (medium, configuration): Must generate .test-index entries after extraction to avoid full-suite triggers.
- Module re-execution via importlib (medium, runtime): New handler modules should use standard imports, not importlib.
## Approach

Domain Module Reorganization: decompose monster functions into handler modules organized by domain (bridge/, ticket/), extract shell utility functions into lib-*.sh files, flatten deep nesting via guard clauses. Original script entry points remain as thin dispatchers that re-export all public symbols, preserving backward compatibility for 70+ consumers. Guard clause flattening must audit and preserve exception propagation semantics. New handler modules use standard Python package imports (not importlib).
## Dependencies
This epic should complete before epic 9d88-68ed (observability) begins work on bridge scripts, to avoid concurrent structural changes to the same files.

**What**: New plugins/dso/scripts/regenerate-strata-sdk-facts.sh pinned to specific upstream tag/commit recorded in plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh. content.text: ## Incident Overview

**Expected behavior**: When a sub-agent dispatched with `isolation: "worktree"` completes successfully (STATUS: pass), the agent's worktree should persist with committed changes until the sprint orchestrator harvests them via `per-worktree-review-commit.md`.

**Actual behavior**: Sub-agent worktrees are auto-cleaned immediately on agent completion. The platform removes the worktree directory when the agent process ends, regardless of whether changes were committed. All file modifications made by the agent are lost.

**Impact**: Sprint Batch 1 (spike task), Batch 2 (contract doc, lint wrapper, negative directive) — all 4 sub-agents completed successfully but their worktrees were removed before harvest. The orchestrator resorted to direct implementation (HARD-GATE violation) as a workaround.
## Technical Environment
- Platform: darwin (macOS 25.5.0)
- Claude Code version: Opus 4.7 (1M context)
- Worktree isolation: enabled (default)
- Sprint mode: ci-pr
## Action History
1. Sprint orchestrator dispatched spike task with `isolation: "worktree"`, `run_in_background: true`
2. Sub-agent ran for ~600s, created files, reported STATUS: pass
3. Orchestrator checked `git worktree list` — worktree was `locked`
4. Orchestrator checked files in worktree — worktree directory was gone
5. Pattern repeated for 3 more sub-agents in Batch 2
## Reproduction

Dispatch any sub-agent with `isolation: "worktree"` and `run_in_background: true`. After the agent completes, check `git worktree list` — the worktree entry will be absent. The platform auto-cleans worktrees on agent completion regardless of whether the agent committed changes.
## Root Cause Hypothesis

The Claude Code platform's worktree lifecycle management removes the worktree when the agent process ends. The `per-worktree-review-commit.md` protocol assumes worktrees persist until the orchestrator explicitly harvests them via `harvest-worktree.sh`, but the platform cleans them first.
Possible factors:
- The platform may auto-clean worktrees that have no new commits (no changes = auto-remove)
- Sub-agents may not be committing their work within the worktree before reporting completion
- The task-execution.md template may lack explicit commit instructions for worktree-isolated agents
## Skills and Workflows
- Sprint SKILL.md Phase E (Sub-Agent Launch) — dispatches with `isolation: "worktree"`
- Sprint SKILL.md Phase F — per-worktree-review-commit.md protocol assumes worktree persists
- task-execution.md — sub-agent task template; may lack commit instructions

content.text: ## Context

Epic 4e55-a6ba (PR-merge mode and enforcement-strategy config) introduces enforcement.strategy config and gates the local pre-commit and PreToolUse hooks on it; epic 5d6e-86a9 (CI LLM-review parity) ports /dso:review's classifier-driven multi-agent review architecture into the CI llm-review job. With both shipped, this project can safely move local enforcement responsibility to CI without losing review fidelity. This epic operationalizes the flip on the plugin's own repo, validates that CI catches what local enforcement caught, and identifies plugin scripts that become dead weight under ci mode for cleanup. Hooks themselves remain in the plugin codebase (config-gated by epic 4e55-a6ba) — operational, not destructive. Original 1083-fb3d scope (remove hooks; add PR-based merge) was decomposed: PR-merge work moved to epic 4e55-a6ba; hook-removal scope dropped (hooks stay, config-gated).
## Success Criteria

- This project's dso-config.conf updated: enforcement.strategy=ci. Pre-commit hooks and PreToolUse hooks emit HOOK_GATE: skipped reason=enforcement.strategy=ci on subsequent commits — verified in-session by inspecting one commit's hook output.

- Plugin scripts whose only consumers are the now-dormant local enforcement path identified via a Part C downstream-consumer scan using grep -rn against plugins/dso/skills/, plugins/dso/scripts/, plugins/dso/hooks/, and tests/ for each candidate script's filename; the scan produces an explicit candidate list; every script on the list is either deleted in this epic's commit OR annotated with the non-enforcement consumer that keeps it alive. The list may be empty if no scripts qualify — that is an acceptable outcome.
## Dependencies
Blocked by epic 4e55-a6ba (PR-merge mode and enforcement-strategy config) and epic 5d6e-86a9 (CI LLM-review parity). Both must be merged on origin/main before this epic begins.
## Approach

Sequenced flip: (a) PR-mode pre-validation on this repo, (b) flip enforcement.strategy=ci in dso-config.conf, (c) commit through epic 4e55-a6ba's PR-mode merge-to-main and observe epic 5d6e-86a9's parity-uplifted llm-review fire on the PR, (d) open deliberate-violation test PR and confirm CI-side block, close PR and delete branch, (e) Part C scan plus cleanup commit deleting confirmed-unused scripts.
## Scenario Analysis
- Required-checks list in .github/required-checks.txt not updated before flip — CI block never fires because the new check is not registered as required (critical, deployment).

- enforcement.strategy=ci is read by .pre-commit-config.yaml hooks but not by the PreToolUse hook (review-gate.sh), leaving one layer still actively enforcing — agent session blocked at the tool-use layer despite the pre-commit layer correctly skipping (high, configuration).
- Deliberate-violation test PR left open or merged accidentally after validation, polluting main history if a subsequent process or merge-queue flush merges it (medium, deployment).
- merge-to-main.sh PR mode is not yet proven on this specific repo before the flip — first real commit after flipping local enforcement off travels through an untested code path (high, deployment).
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): not triggered (operational epic; no new external integration)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 4
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (single project flip)
## Closure Checks

- Before the operational flip, an end-to-end PR-mode merge is exercised on this repo (a no-op test commit) — confirms that epic 4e55-a6ba's merge-to-main-pr.sh works correctly on this specific repo's configuration before local enforcement is turned off.

- Deliberate test PR opened that violates a rule the local gate previously caught (e.g., a critical security finding the security overlay should catch); CI-side enforcement (Ruleset checks via epic 5d6e-86a9's parity-uplifted llm-review plus the Ruleset's required-checks list) blocks merge — verified in-session via gh pr checks showing the failed check and gh pr merge --auto queued but not executing.
