content.text: EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural
## Context

Hand-authored UI code in DSO consumer projects drifts away from design-system tokens — hardcoded hex/rgb colors, off-scale spacing/padding/margin/gap, off-scale font-size/line-height, broken token references, and accidental WCAG-failing fg/bg pairings accumulate over time. LLM reviewers cannot reliably catch them. Today the project's design intent lives in a free-prose `.claude/design-notes.md` that no tooling can parse, and the `dso:ui-designer` agent has no canonical token reference to consult when proposing new patterns. This epic adopts Google Labs' open DESIGN.md spec as the canonical machine-readable design-system artifact at repo root, ships a lint wrapper enforcing token compliance at pre-commit / sprint / FP-recovery gates, and integrates DESIGN.md additions into the existing preplanning UI-designer flow so token introductions become deliberate design decisions rather than rubber-stamped commit-time accidents.
## Success Criteria

1. Linter-enforced token compliance on diffs: In consumer projects where `design.lint_enabled` resolves to `always` or `auto` with a UI stack detected, a commit that introduces a hardcoded hex/rgb color, an off-scale spacing/padding/margin/gap value, an off-scale font-size/line-height, a broken token reference, or a WCAG-failing fg/bg pair in any diff-touched line of a scope-eligible file (CSS family, JS/TS family with JSX/TSX, Vue, Svelte, Astro, HTML, and SSR template families: PHP, JSP, JSPX, ASP/ASPX, ERB, EJS, Handlebars, Twig, Jinja2, Razor `.cshtml`, Blade `.blade.php`) is blocked by `design-md-lint.sh` via the pre-commit hook. Pre-existing violations in untouched lines are not blocked.

2. DESIGN.md addition flow via preplanning, never via the linter: When `dso:ui-designer` is dispatched during `/dso:preplanning` Phase H Step 7 for a UI story that introduces tokens, the agent emits a structured DESIGN.md-additions payload (a nullable `design_md_additions` field inside the existing `UI_DESIGNER_PAYLOAD`) conforming to `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/design-md-additions-payload.md`; the preplanning orchestrator surfaces the payload to the user as part of preplanning approval; on approval, the accepted additions are written to repo-root `DESIGN.md` (flock-serialized) before the sprint implementing that story begins. On user decline, the orchestrator skips the write, tags the story `design:tokens_pending`, and continues sprint dispatch. In `PREPLANNING_INTERACTIVE=false` mode, the orchestrator emits an `INTERACTIVITY_DEFERRED` ticket comment. The linter (pre-commit, sprint, FP-recovery) is enforcement-only — it never adds tokens.

3. Sprint and FP-recovery enforcement integration: Sprint Phase F runs `design-md-lint.sh` against the batch's touched files between Step 11 and Step 12 (shared-directory mode) and at the equivalent point in `per-worktree-review-commit.md` (worktree-isolation mode), blocking the batch on violations. `/dso:fp-recovery` accepts DESIGN.md lint findings as eligible false-positive escape candidates using the same workflow it uses for code-reviewer findings.

4. Migration with spec-compliance verification: `plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-design-notes-to-design-md.sh` is invoked from the Migration Check block in onboarding, brainstorm, sprint, preplanning, fix-bug, roadmap, and debug-everything (matching the existing project pattern); when a consumer project has `.claude/design-notes.md` without a migration marker, the script maps each section into a spec-compliant repo-root `DESIGN.md` per the established mapping (Vision / User Archetypes / Visual Language → Overview; Anti-Patterns → Do's and Don'ts; Golden Paths / Accessibility / UI Framework → custom sections; Design System name → YAML `name`), prepends empty token YAML front-matter, leaves the old file as a deprecation tombstone, and writes the migration marker. The script refuses to create a DESIGN.md with empty token YAML front-matter on a greenfield project lacking `.claude/design-notes.md` (greenfield seeding is the responsibility of `/dso:onboarding`'s UI branch or template install). The resulting `DESIGN.md` passes `npx --yes @google/design.md@<pinned-version> lint DESIGN.md` with zero structural errors when exercised against a fixture in the closing session.

5. Single source of truth for DSO consumers and audit command: After migration, every DSO skill, agent, hook, and config-schema file that previously referenced `.claude/design-notes.md` reads repo-root `DESIGN.md` instead — verified at closure by a grep that returns zero references to `design-notes.md` in `plugins/dso/` outside the migration script and its tests. The `dso design-lint --report` command runs full-file across the repo on demand and emits a per-violation-class count to stdout; the command is documented in `plugins/dso/docs/DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md` and is auto-discoverable via `/dso:quick-ref`.

6. End-to-end dogfooding fixture verification at closure: Before epic closure, `design-md-lint.sh` is executed against a fixture consumer repo committed under `plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/design-md/` containing (a) one file per violation class — hardcoded hex, hardcoded rgb, off-scale spacing, off-scale padding, off-scale margin, off-scale gap, off-scale font-size, off-scale line-height, broken token reference, WCAG-failing fg/bg pair — and (b) one clean file per scope-eligible file family. The linter MUST block on each violation file (exit non-zero, finding emitted) and MUST pass on each clean file (exit zero). Cold-start and warm-cache wall-clock latency are recorded in the closure log; cold-start exceeding 30s emits a documented advisory in `DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md`.

7. Capability spike completed and recorded before any enforcement story ships: Story 0 produces a spike report at `plugins/dso/docs/spikes/design-md-cli-validation.md` recording (i) the pinned `@google/design.md` version selected, (ii) exit-code mapping (which exit codes are blocking errors vs. non-blocking warnings), (iii) cold-start and warm-cache latency measurements on at least one network environment without a warm npm cache, (iv) the diff-touched-line scoping behavior under at least one whitespace-normalizing IDE auto-formatter (e.g., Prettier on a `.tsx` file). Stories 1–8 do not begin until this report is committed and the pin is recorded in `DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md`.
## Closure Checks
- The file `plugins/dso/docs/spikes/design-md-cli-validation.md` exists and contains a heading recording the pinned `@google/design.md` version and the exit-code mapping.
- The file `plugins/dso/docs/DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md` exists and contains a `## Pinned CLI Version` heading.
- `grep -rln 'design-notes' plugins/dso/ | grep -v migrate-design-notes-to-design-md` returns no matches.
- The directory `plugins/dso/tests/fixtures/design-md/` exists and contains at least one violation file and at least one clean file per scope-eligible file family.
## Dependencies

None as input. This epic is a producer dependency for `2ca5-26ef`, `53ee-a9ac`, `6f33-2392`, `d7a0-a693` (those epics must not ship DESIGN.md-consuming or payload-extending code before this epic's schema artifacts land).
## Approach

Vertical-slice iteration over 9 stories (Story 0 capability spike + 8 implementation stories), end-to-end usable after Story 2. Story 0 is a 1-day time-boxed spike that produces a proof-of-concept `design-md-lint.sh` and validates `@google/design.md` exit-code semantics, cold-start latency mitigation (`--prefer-offline` or local devDependency install), fixture blocking behavior, and diff-touched-line scoping under auto-formatters. The spike has an explicit pass/fail gate; on failure the epic returns to brainstorm. Stories 1-2 ship the schema + lint script + config gate + pre-commit hook (consumer with `lint_enabled=always` gets spec-native enforcement at end of Story 2). Stories 3-6 add DSO-specific extensions, sprint Phase F integration, FP-recovery integration, and the `dso:ui-designer` payload + preplanning approval flow. Stories 7-8 ship the migration script + per-skill retargeting (sequenced per-skill: Migration Check block insertion does not close in any of the 7 skills until that skill's `design-notes.md` read sites are retargeted) + audit command + docs.

Linter wraps a pinned `@google/design.md` (`npx --yes @google/design.md@<pinned-version> lint`); pin recorded in `DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md`, bumped via DSO release with fixture re-verification. Three-state config gate `design.lint_enabled = auto|always|never` with explicit auto-detection heuristic (React/Vue/Svelte/Astro/Angular/Next/Nuxt/Gatsby/Remix/Tailwind/MUI in package.json OR `.css/.scss/.less/.sass` at depth ≤3 outside node_modules/vendor OR Jekyll `_config.yml`). `command -v npx` short-circuit when Node absent. Wide-net file scoping including SSR template families. `dso:ui-designer` emits the DESIGN.md-additions payload as a nullable field inside the existing `UI_DESIGNER_PAYLOAD` schema (no second top-level emitted block). All DESIGN.md read sites include a one-sentence negative directive against treating prose as AI behavioral instruction. Wireframe session file `version` bumped from 1 to 2 to detect stale pre-migration content.
## Scenario Analysis

14 surviving scenarios (7 high, 7 medium) covering: npx cold-start latency on slow/CI networks (high/runtime), concurrent sprint sub-agent DESIGN.md writes (high/runtime), generated-CSS false positives on diff-touched lines (medium/runtime), DESIGN.md token-key drift between linter and completion-verifier (medium/runtime), empty-DESIGN.md vacuous SC1 satisfaction (high/deployment), unpinned `@google/design.md` CLI breaking changes (high/deployment), Node/npx absence on auto-detected non-UI projects (high/deployment), undefined auto detection heuristic (medium/configuration), empty-token-front-matter footgun on freshly migrated projects (high/configuration), tombstone stale-read by consumer-side customizations (medium/configuration), `@google/design.md` exit-code contract assumption (high/assumption), DESIGN.md spec stability for production enforcement (high/assumption), diff-touched-line semantics under IDE auto-formatters (medium/assumption), single repo-root DESIGN.md in monorepos with multiple UI packages (medium/assumption). The capability spike (Story 0) and pinned-version + dogfooding SCs (SC6, SC7) directly address the high-severity items.
## Cross-Epic Interactions
Interactions with 7 open epics, all carried forward as acceptance criteria per Step 2.26 injection (one CONFLICT and 7 AMBIGUITY signals overridden by practitioner at Step 2.27):

- `dso:ui-designer` agent output contract (DESIGN.md-additions payload): Multiple peer epics extend or consume the payload — `1048-67d0`, `4001-7ad3`, `4f8e-a7a6`, `853a-c719`, `f3de-f651`. The `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/design-md-additions-payload.md` contract documents extension points and surfacing order for orchestrator-side user approval when multiple peer epics co-emit.
- Sprint Phase F design + reference injection ordering with `2ca5-26ef`: This epic's migration (SC4) must complete in any project before `2ca5-26ef` ref-query reads finalized DESIGN.md tokens.

- DESIGN.md schema and token-key definitions for `53ee-a9ac`: The migration script's output schema and the linter's off-scale detection reference the same canonical token-key names as the completion-verifier's UI conformance assertions.

- `dso:design-review` reviewer docs and completion-verifier UI-story payload extension with `6f33-2392`, `d7a0-a693`: A versioned multi-constraint payload schema for design-review constraints is defined in `DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md` and accepts appending of constraint classes from peer epics.

- Migration Check block execution order with `d63f-2c74`, `dfa1-f9fd`: Artifact-reference atomicity checks and coupling-principle enforcement run independently of `migrate-design-notes-to-design-md.sh`; no shared state; idempotent ordering.

- `design.lint_enabled` config gate semantics with `dso-fbky` autonomous-mode override: When `AUTONOMOUS_MODE=off`, `design.lint_enabled = auto` degrades to `never` for the session; documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md update.

- DESIGN.md artifact scope for documentation quality enforcement (`dso-q0lo`): `DESIGN-MD-REFERENCE.md` documents DESIGN.md's YAML+Markdown structure so doc-overlay agents can exempt machine-readable front-matter from prose-quality patterns.
## External Dependencies
| Source | Ownership | Handling | Claude Has Access | Verification Command |
| `@google/design.md` (Google Labs open-spec CLI; pinned) | external | claude_auto | yes (via npx) | `npx --yes @google/design.md@<pinned-version> --version` |
| Node.js + `npx` runtime in consumer projects | consumer-side | user_manual | depends on consumer env | `node --version && npx --version` |
## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| Repo-root `DESIGN.md` | `migrate-design-notes-to-design-md.sh` (existing project) OR onboarding Phase D UI branch (greenfield) OR template install | `/dso:preplanning` orchestrator on accepted DESIGN.md-additions payload from `dso:ui-designer` (flock-serialized) | `design-md-lint.sh`, `dso:ui-designer` agent, all `dso:design-review` reviewer docs, `/dso:brainstorm` Phase 1 Step 1, `/dso:ui-discover`, `/dso:roadmap`, `shared/prompts/scale-inference.md`, `/dso:dryrun`, `check-onboarding.sh` | never — persists for project lifetime |

| `.claude/design-notes.md` (deprecated) | onboarding Phase D Step 4 (pre-this-epic only) | never (post-this-epic) | none (post-this-epic; all reads retarget to DESIGN.md) | `migrate-design-notes-to-design-md.sh` (transforms to tombstone with deprecation banner; never deletes) |

| Migration marker (in `DESIGN.md` YAML front-matter as `_dso_migration_version` OR `.claude/.dso-design-md-migrated`) | `migrate-design-notes-to-design-md.sh` first successful run | never (one-shot) | `migrate-design-notes-to-design-md.sh` subsequent invocations (idempotency check) | never |

| Wireframe session file `version` | `ui-designer-dispatch-protocol.md` Section 1 (initial value `2` post-this-epic) | never | `dso:ui-designer` Phase 2 (rejects sessions with `version: 1` to avoid stale pre-migration content) | session file deletion at epic close |
## Research Findings
### External Integration: Google Labs DESIGN.md spec and `@google/design.md` CLI
- Trigger condition: External integration (third-party CLI tool not currently used)

- Source URLs: https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md, https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md/blob/main/docs/spec.md, https://github.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1008, https://www.designtokens.org/tr/drafts/format/

- Key insights: DESIGN.md is an established community standard (Apr 2026 open-source release) with broad ecosystem adoption (Stitch, Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, Aider, Sourcegraph Amp, Jules, Figma Make). YAML front-matter fields: `name` (required), `version`, `description`, `colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components` (optional); unknown keys tolerated. Markdown body has optional ordered sections; unknown headings preserved. Overview covers brand personality / target audience / emotional response (direct home for Vision, User Archetypes, Visual Language). Do's and Don'ts is the formal home for Anti-Patterns. Official CLI exits 1 on errors only; warnings-only findings exit 0. Spec is at alpha stability with explicit breaking-change warnings — pin a specific version. Exports to Tailwind v3/v4 and W3C DTCG token format. File location convention: repo-root `DESIGN.md` (uppercase).
### Migration / Compatibility: design-notes.md to DESIGN.md content mapping
- Trigger condition: Migration / compatibility (deprecating an existing file)
- Source URLs: same as above plus inspection of spec.md document

- Key insight: The DESIGN.md spec's Overview section and Do's and Don'ts section natively cover the strategic content currently in `.claude/design-notes.md`. Unknown sections (Golden Paths, Accessibility Target, UI Framework, Design System name) are preserved by the linter without error. Hard-cutover migration is feasible with no data loss.
## Prompt Alignment Findings

Bot-psychologist behavioral review (Step 5) surfaced six findings on the LLM-facing instruction changes proposed by this epic; all are incorporated as story acceptance criteria during implementation-plan. Matched signal category: skill file modifications (with secondary matches on agent definitions and hook behavioral logic).
1. Dual payload emission ambiguity — `design_md_additions` is a nullable field inside `UI_DESIGNER_PAYLOAD`, not a second top-level emitted block (single orchestrator parse path).

2. Decline path for DESIGN.md-additions approval — on user decline, skip write, tag `design:tokens_pending`, continue sprint dispatch; in `PREPLANNING_INTERACTIVE=false` mode, emit `INTERACTIVITY_DEFERRED` ticket comment.
3. Migration Check block / retargeting ordering gate — per-skill close conditions: Migration Check block does not close in a skill until that skill's `design-notes.md` read sites are retargeted.
4. Section-name extraction mismatch — `ui-designer.md` Lite Step 1 and Full Phase 2 retargeting includes updated section-name extraction strings matching DESIGN.md's structure; legacy names removed.

content.text: ## Context

The DSO project-setup workflow is fragmented across four user-invocable skills (/dso:init, /dso:onboarding, /dso:architect-foundation, /dso:generate-claude-md). Users — both project maintainers running setup for the first time and returning users coming back after editing a config artifact — do not know which skill to invoke first or whether re-running is safe. Each skill's SKILL.md is monolithic; conditional sections (stack-specific, CI-platform-specific, design-system-specific, infra-specific) load on every invocation regardless of relevance, inflating per-invocation context cost. The current /dso:onboarding SKILL.md is over 1,800 lines.

User impact today: a maintainer who edits workflow-config.yaml after onboarding has no obvious way to regenerate CLAUDE.md short of re-running everything; a returning user is forced through the entire Socratic dialog from scratch even when only one phase's output is stale; new users face the "which skill first?" cognitive tax.

This epic consolidates the four skills into a single resume-aware /dso:onboarding skill, decomposes conditional content into phase-scoped prompt files at skills/onboarding/prompts/ (loaded only when the phase determines the topic applies), and deletes the three subordinate skills.

Definitions: Freshness check = a phase-specific boolean predicate that returns true when the phase's output artifact is present AND structurally valid; defined per-phase in the SC7 contract table. Enforcement scaffolding = the set of files provisioned by the current /dso:architect-foundation skill (git hook scripts, review-gate config files, CI ruleset entries, fitness-function templates referenced from ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md). SUB-AGENT-GUARD = the block at the top of plugins/dso/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md that returns the literal error "ERROR: /dso:onboarding requires main session; invoke directly." when dispatched via the Task tool. Phase-invocation log = a structured artifact written by the orchestrator at ${WORKFLOW_PLUGIN_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/onboarding-phases.log with fields phase_name, invocation_reason, outcome per row.
## Success Criteria

- SC1: Running /dso:onboarding on a fully set-up project (all four phase artifacts present and pass their freshness checks) writes no files and surfaces no dialog questions. Verified in-session: SHA256 of all four phase artifact files (workflow-config.yaml, project-understanding.md, the enforcement-scaffolding file set, CLAUDE.md) match pre-run and post-run; phase-invocation log shows all four phases with outcome=noop.

- SC2: Running /dso:onboarding after editing workflow-config.yaml re-renders only CLAUDE.md. SHA256 of project-understanding.md and each enforcement-scaffolding file unchanged; SHA256 of CLAUDE.md differs. Phase-invocation log shows generate-claude-md outcome=executed with invocation_reason=dependent_artifact_changed.

- SC4: The three previously-user-invocable skills (/dso:init, /dso:architect-foundation, /dso:generate-claude-md) no longer appear in `claude plugin list` output, and their directories under plugins/dso/skills/ are absent.

- SC5: Phase files in skills/onboarding/phases/<phase>.md are <=80 non-blank, non-comment lines each. Conditional dialogue and behavioral content for each conditional axis (stack, CI platform, design system, infrastructure type, plus any others identified during extraction) is decomposed into one or more skills/onboarding/prompts/<topic>.md files, loaded via Read only when the executing phase determines the topic applies.

- SC7: A freshness-check contract documented at plugins/dso/docs/onboarding-resume-contract.md containing a markdown table whose rows are the four phases and whose columns are output_artifact, freshness_predicate, dependent_inputs, re-run_trigger.

- SC8: The <SUB-AGENT-GUARD> is preserved on the new /dso:onboarding SKILL.md. Verified by dispatching /dso:onboarding via the Agent tool with subagent_type: "general-purpose" and asserting the returned text contains the literal string "ERROR: /dso:onboarding requires main session; invoke directly.".

- SC9: A behavioral test at tests/scripts/test-onboarding-resume.sh exercises each freshness predicate against a fixture project across four cases: (a) all artifacts fresh -> all phases no-op; (b) workflow-config.yaml modified -> only generate-claude-md executes; (c) project-understanding.md deleted -> dialogue and architect-foundation execute; (d) CLAUDE.md deleted -> only generate-claude-md executes. Test asserts on the phase-invocation log artifact and passes in CI.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The 136b sprint exercises the consolidated `/dso:onboarding` skill against a fixture project (or this DSO repo if appropriate) during sprint execution itself. At least one full onboarding run (or resume across phases) executes the consolidated skill end-to-end before sprint close.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- A test fixture project at `tests/fixtures/onboarding-consolidated/` exists; sprint executes `/dso:onboarding --fixture=tests/fixtures/onboarding-consolidated/`.
- The phase-invocation log at `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/onboarding-phases.log` contains entries for ≥2 distinct phases (proves phase-aware resume path is live).

- Sprint resumes the onboarding mid-flow (forced pause + restart) and the resume-aware logic skips already-completed phases per the freshness predicate. Verification: log entries are not duplicated on resume.
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `${WORKFLOW_PLUGIN_ARTIFACTS_DIR}/onboarding-phases.log` | Orchestrator writes on phase start | Each phase appends its completion entry | Resume-aware phases read predicates from this log | **Retired at onboarding completion**: orchestrator archives the log to `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/onboarding-phases.log.<timestamp>` and clears the working file. If onboarding is re-run from scratch, a fresh log is created. Closes the audit's RETIRE gap. |

| Freshness predicate state (derived from log entries) | Each phase emits its predicate state to the log | Subsequent phases update; each phase's predicate state is owned by that phase (no cross-phase mutation) | Resume-aware orchestration | Cleared with the log archive |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `test -f $ARTIFACTS_DIR/onboarding-phases.log.<timestamp>` shows the post-completion archive after a clean onboarding run; the working file is absent or empty.
## Dependencies

None. Supersedes jira-dig-1567 (narrower scope — "Integrate Claude's init skill into onboarding"). Relates to dso-zj3r (skills/prompts token-usage optimization — broader parent goal) and f6ad-6cad (/dso:next zero-friction auto-router — adjacent UX layer).
## Approach

Replace /dso:onboarding's SKILL.md with a thin orchestrator that runs four phases (init, dialogue, architect-foundation, generate-claude-md) in order, each gated by a presence + phase-specific freshness predicate. The orchestrator writes the phase-invocation log artifact for verification. Inline the deleted skills' logic into skills/onboarding/phases/<phase>.md (≤80 non-blank, non-comment lines each). Decompose conditional sections into skills/onboarding/prompts/<topic>.md files loaded via Read only when the phase determines the topic applies. Delete the three subordinate skill directories. Update cross-references in CLAUDE.md, plugins/dso/docs/MIGRATION-TO-PLUGIN.md, and other skills (roadmap, dryrun, anti-patterns.md). Onboarding remains interactive-only (existing <SUB-AGENT-GUARD> preserved); phases may dispatch sub-agents internally for codebase analysis.
## Scenario Analysis

- Phase gate skips dependent phase when artifact exists but is structurally incomplete (critical, runtime): A truncated artifact from a prior session interrupt may be treated as complete by a presence-only freshness check, causing a dependent phase to skip and leaving the project in a silently broken state.

- Missing prompts/ directory causes all lazy-load attempts to fail on fresh plugin install (critical, configuration): If skills/onboarding/prompts/ is omitted from the plugin distribution, every lazy-load fails — fail-open produces incorrect output, fail-closed aborts onboarding.

- Freshness predicate evaluates stale on file-only edits inside artifact sections (high, runtime): Hand-editing whitespace or comments triggers full re-run because mtime/hash check has no notion of "no semantic change."
- Lazy-load routing picks wrong prompt file on ambiguous stack signal (high, runtime): Polyglot repos (e.g., package.json + pyproject.toml) cause the wrong stack-specific prompts to load.

- Prompt-file Read failure silently skips conditional content (high, runtime): A phase Reading a missing prompt file without an explicit guard generates output missing the conditional sections with no warning.

- Skills that name deleted skills fail at invocation time, not at reference-scan time (high, deployment): Dynamic skill-name construction (variable interpolation) evades the SC6 grep and fails at runtime.

- Malformed workflow-config.yaml causes freshness check to throw instead of falling back (high, configuration): YAML syntax errors from hand-edits abort the entire skill mid-run rather than emitting a helpful malformed-config message.

- Hand-edited project-understanding.md loses required section headers (high, configuration): User edits remove sections that downstream phases depend on; phase silently receives wrong values and generates incorrect scaffolding.
- CI-platform-specific prompt loaded based on file presence rather than active platform (medium, configuration): Stale .github/workflows/ after CI migration causes the wrong CI prompts to load.
## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Architect-foundation phase = integration point for stack/CI/architecture additions. Six open epics (622a-3955 Azure DevOps, 70d5-37ee Java, 6add-c1fc Semgrep CI, ee22-4785 .NET, f06e-9c43 language type validation, dfa1-f9fd loosely coupled architecture) add stack-specific, CI-platform-specific, security-tool, or architectural-principle content to architect-foundation. Constraint: those epics' content must land as skills/onboarding/prompts/<topic>.md files following this epic's decomposition pattern; this epic's phase-conditional Read mechanism is the canonical extension point.

- CLAUDE.md generation = integration point for new repository rules and downstream introspection. Shared with 4911-c7ba (reviewer rubric expansion adding pipefail/mktemp/BASH_SOURCE rules), dso-q0lo (prevent doc explosion — quality enforcement), dso-uvyl (implementation-plan migration awareness — CLAUDE.md introspection). Constraint: the generate-claude-md phase output must remain compatible with downstream skills that read CLAUDE.md by section.

- Plugin skill registry shape changes. Shared with d97a-6bb7 (/dso:doctor health check) and a8e8-0b23 (specialized skill/agent authoring sub-agent). Constraint: skills that audit or generate the plugin skill registry must be updated to recognize the consolidated onboarding structure (3 deletions, new phases/ and prompts/ subdirectories).

- Brainstorm/preplanning attestation patterns. Shared with c183-ed2a (brainstorm completeness attestation) and d63f-2c74 (atomicity-check on AC generation). Constraint: the new phase-invocation log artifact must not interfere with future attestation/atomicity validation; log schema in SC7 contract doc should be referenceable by those epics.

- dso-config.conf config-gating syntax. Shared with dso-0wi2 (project-level config flags). Constraint: phase-conditional and topic-conditional logic must align with the project-level config flag naming and resolution order established by dso-0wi2.

- Token usage of new prompt files. Shared with dso-zj3r (skills/prompts token-usage optimization). Constraint: new prompts/<topic>.md files become candidates for dso-zj3r's audit; maintain reuse-friendly structure (avoid duplicated headers/preambles across topics).

- Sprint story-closure forcing function. Shared with a154-98de (PRECONDITIONS degradation channel + sprint forcing function). Constraint: sprint must observe all four phase outputs and degrade gracefully when phases are skipped.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): not triggered

- Bright-line conditions that fired: none (internal refactor; no external integration, unfamiliar dependency, security/auth, novel architecture, performance/scalability, or migration/compatibility signal)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 9 (of 18 red team findings)
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered

- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: skill file modifications (bot-psychologist dispatch skipped via graceful degradation: structural refactor, no draft prompt text or LLM-instruction content authored)
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (developer-tooling skill refactor; no volume-sensitive decision)
## Closure Checks

- SC3: Running /dso:onboarding after deleting project-understanding.md (precondition: workflow-config.yaml and CLAUDE.md present and fresh) runs only the dialogue and architect-foundation phases. Post-run: workflow-config.yaml and CLAUDE.md SHA256 unchanged; project-understanding.md and enforcement-scaffolding files written. Phase-invocation log shows exactly four entries: init outcome=noop, dialogue outcome=executed, architect-foundation outcome=executed, generate-claude-md outcome=noop.

- SC6: Cross-references in CLAUDE.md, plugins/dso/docs/**/*.md, and other skills' SKILL.md files are updated. `grep -rn "dso:init\|dso:architect-foundation\|dso:generate-claude-md" plugins/ .claude/ CLAUDE.md` returns zero matches.

content.text: ## Context

DSO's design workflow is fully autonomous — design-wireframe produces a 3-artifact manifest (spatial-layout.json, wireframe.svg, tokens.md) reviewed by LLM-based design reviewers. Teams with a human designer have no structured way to collaborate. This epic adds the first half of a Figma collaboration loop: DSO's wireframe.svg is optimized for Figma import, the user imports it into Figma for the designer to review and revise, the user exports a revision PNG and places it in the project, and the implementation agent uses the original manifest (for behavioral specs) alongside the revision image (for visual intent).
## Success Criteria

1. When design.figma_collaboration=true (opt-in per design), wireframe.svg is written with Figma-optimized structure (semantic group names, element IDs matching spatial-layout.json), and the story is tagged design:awaiting_import with instructions for the user
2. User exports PNG from Figma to designs/{uuid}/figma-revision.png, runs approval command that validates file exists at path before replacing tag with design:approved
3. Sprint skill skips design:awaiting_import stories and surfaces them as "Awaiting designer input" in status reports

4. Implementation agent uses original manifest (authoritative for behavior) + revision image (authoritative for visual layout/styling); manifest governs behavior, image governs visual; contradictions flagged as [NEEDS_REVIEW]
5. No effect on projects without the flag
## Scenario Analysis

13 surviving scenarios. Key risks: PNG at wrong path (mitigation: approval validates file exists), implementation agent multimodal capability (mitigation: specify model tier), SVG/JSON ID divergence (mitigation: shared ID registry), worktree lifecycle for designs/ (mitigation: explicit git policy), permanent awaiting_import if designer abandons (mitigation: staleness warning), manifest/image out of sync after re-run (mitigation: guard regeneration when approved).
## Dependencies
None beyond existing DSO infrastructure. No external APIs, no npm packages, no Figma account required from DSO's side.
## Approach

Minimal-infrastructure collaboration loop. DSO's existing wireframe.svg is optimized for Figma import. The designer imports SVG, revises in Figma, user exports revision PNG. Implementation agent uses dual-source strategy: manifest for structure/behavior, image for visual intent. Zero API integration, zero auth, zero external dependencies. Establishes the workflow pattern that the Pull epics later automate.
## Research Artifacts
- .claude/artifacts/figma-integration-research-guide.md
- .claude/artifacts/design-format-research-synthesis.md
- .claude/artifacts/figma-feasibility-synthesis.md
- .claude/artifacts/design-manifest-pull-format-analysis.md
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research**: triggered (8 research agents: Figma MCP/API, GitHub integrations, alternatives, design intent for LLMs, agentic projects, custom plugin, REST API, lateral thinking)
- **Scenario analysis**: triggered (17 red team → 13 surviving blue team)
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: web research re-run 2x (feasibility investigation + 5-agent parallel alternatives investigation)

content.text: ## Context

PR-G (Week 3 audit remediation) updated `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/inference-envelope.md` to honestly document the current state: the contract claimed `fix-bug Phase B` and `sprint Phase H` parsed `INFERENCE_CHALLENGE` and `INFERENCE_SKIP`, but a grep against both skill files returns zero references. The only emitter is `plugins/dso/agents/red-team-reviewer.md`, which emits JSON objects in its structured report.

So the signal is emitted but never consumed. The "always-challenge" tier in red-team-reviewer.md is therefore advisory text only — the orchestrator does not halt on inferences flagged for user confirmation.
## Decision needed
Wire an orchestrator-level parser that, on receiving a sub-agent report containing `output_type=="INFERENCE_CHALLENGE"`:
1. Halts the calling flow
2. Surfaces the `evidence_against_inference` text to the user
3. Requires explicit user approval before allowing the calling flow to proceed
4. Logs `INFERENCE_SKIP` records to a session ledger for dedup
Open design questions:
- Where in the orchestrator does the parser live (sprint Phase 18 area? a shared post-dispatch hook?)
- Is the halt blocking or advisory?
- Where is the session-level inference ledger persisted (artifacts dir? ticket comment trail?)
## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: A red-team-reviewer dispatch that emits INFERENCE_CHALLENGE causes the orchestrator to surface the challenge to the user before any downstream step proceeds.
- AC2: `inference-envelope.md` Consumers table is updated to name the actual parser (replacing the "Future orchestrator parser (planned)" entry).

content.text: Placeholder epic for human-adjudicated kudos awards. Deferred from epic 3e9b-afee (Agent Kudos System core) to keep V1 scope manageable.
RESEARCH NOTES FROM BRAINSTORM SESSION (2026-04-08):

MOTIVATION: V1 kudos system is fully mechanical (no LLM judgment, no human input). User-awarded points would add a human oversight layer and cover quality behaviors that are observable to humans but not structurally verifiable from git diff alone.
CANDIDATE TRIGGER PATTERNS:
- User explicitly recognizes a design decision during interactive session ('that was a great approach')
- User approves a particularly well-reasoned implementation-plan proposal
- User notes that an explanation or doc update was especially clear
- Post-session retro: human rates session quality and awards bonus points
DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:
- Mechanism: CLI command or slash command for human to award (e.g., /dso:kudos award <points> <reason>)
- Integrity: human-awarded points should be stored separately from mechanical awards in .kudos/ ledger (different trigger_id prefix) to maintain audit trail
- Anti-gaming: human-awarded points should have a session cap independent of mechanical cap to prevent solicitation behavior
- Solicitation disqualifier: agent explicitly asking for kudos points should disqualify the session from human awards
- Goodhart risk: higher risk than mechanical triggers since human judgment is more gameable (agents could optimize for human approval rather than quality)
- Attribution: human-awarded points carry session ID of the human session, not agent session
INTEGRATION QUESTIONS:
- Should human awards propagate to sub-agent framing in subsequent sessions?
- Slack/comment integration: award via PR comment or Slack reaction?
- Cross-session visibility: should human awards be visible in the running total display?
OPEN RESEARCH:
- Social recognition systems in software teams (peer recognition vs. manager recognition)
- Gamification research on human-in-the-loop reward systems
- Whether human awards reinforce or undermine mechanical award signal

content.text: ## Story D: `reinstall-hooks.sh` installs on any supported stack (not just Python)
### Description

**What**: Remove the hard-fail-on-missing-pyproject.toml check in `reinstall-hooks.sh` and replace it with a stack-aware precondition that accepts `pyproject.toml` OR `Gemfile` OR `package.json`. Missing all three produces an actionable error, not a silent skip.
**Why**: Today Ruby and Node projects cannot install DSO hooks because `reinstall-hooks.sh` refuses to proceed without a `pyproject.toml` — an invariant that never made sense for non-Python stacks.
**Scope**:
- IN: precondition check replaced, `[DSO ERROR]` with actionable message when all three signal files are missing, existing Python project behavior unchanged
- OUT: per-stack hook variants, hook-behavior differences across stacks (hooks themselves are stack-agnostic once installed)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, running `reinstall-hooks.sh` in a Ruby-only project (Gemfile present, no pyproject.toml) completes successfully and installs hooks
← Satisfies: "reinstall-hooks.sh removes the hard-fail on missing pyproject.toml; installs hooks on any supported stack"
- When this story is complete, running `reinstall-hooks.sh` in a project with none of {pyproject.toml, Gemfile, package.json} exits non-zero with a message listing the accepted signal files
← Satisfies: epic Scenario Analysis "reinstall-hooks.sh removal of pyproject.toml check inadvertently breaks a Python-project invariant"
- When this story is complete, running `reinstall-hooks.sh` in an existing Python-only project produces identical behavior to pre-change
← Satisfies: regression-free change
### Considerations
- [Maintainability] Precondition logic shared with detect-stack.sh; consider extracting a helper so the list of accepted signal files is defined once
- [Testing] Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Context

Plugin maintainers triaging post-deploy regressions today must cross-reference session transcript logs — which expire or get compacted — to identify which sub-agent authored a suspect change. There is no durable, queryable record attached to the commit itself, forcing manual error-prone archaeology and making automated auditing impossible. By accumulating a contributor list in the session artifacts dir and emitting it as git-native trailers at commit time, every DSO-produced commit carries its own provenance chain, queryable via standard git log without leaving the terminal. The trailer set resets after each successful commit so per-commit attribution stays accurate across a multi-commit session.
## Success Criteria

- SC-0: A plugin maintainer investigating any DSO-produced commit can identify all contributing agents and the triggering skill within one git command, without opening any log file or session transcript.

- SC-1: When attribution.enabled=true, commits produced by /dso:commit include DSO trailers appended via git interpret-trailers. Scalar trailers (Jira-Ticket, DSO-Task, DSO-Story, DSO-Epic, DSO-Review-Score) included only when non-empty; DSO-Task/Story/Epic resolved by traversing the active task's parent chain upward, emitting each level only when that ticket type exists; DSO-Review-Score read from $ARTIFACTS_DIR/reviewer-findings.json score field. Multi-value trailers (DSO-Agent, DSO-Skill, DSO-Model) emit one line per unique value accumulated since the last commit.
- SC-2: attribution.enabled is opt-in via dso-config.conf (default: false).

- SC-3: For any attributed commit in a multi-agent sprint session, git log --format="%(trailers:key=DSO-Agent,valueonly)" returns at least two distinct non-empty lines, one per unique agent type that contributed.
- SC-4: When no contributor records exist and no scalar values resolve, the commit message contains no DSO trailer lines and /dso:commit exits 0.

- SC-5: A test asserts that when attribution produces trailers, the lines before the final blank-line separator contain no strings matching ^(Jira-Ticket|DSO-[A-Za-z-]+): — only the trailer block following the separator does. Commits with no body (subject-only) also satisfy this constraint.
- SC-6: After git commit exits 0, $ARTIFACTS_DIR/attribution-contributors.jsonl exists and has size 0. If truncation fails, /dso:commit emits a warning to stderr but does not fail.

- SC-7: When git <2.6 is detected, TRAILER_SKIPPED is emitted to stderr, attribution is skipped, and /dso:commit continues. A test verifies this by injecting a mock git version string below 2.6 and asserting TRAILER_SKIPPED on stderr with no DSO trailer lines in the commit message.
## Dependencies
- Soft interaction with 6d90-93d5 (Conventional Commits) — both modify /dso:commit; not a hard sequencing dependency
- 1083-fb3d (PR-based merge) depends on Jira-Ticket and DSO-Task trailer infrastructure delivered here — this epic should reach done before 1083-fb3d enters sprint
## Approach

Introduce $ARTIFACTS_DIR/attribution-contributors.jsonl as a session-scoped append-only log. A PostToolUse hook on the Agent tool (adds a branch to the existing post-agent.sh dispatcher) captures .tool_input.subagent_type and model; a PostToolUse hook on the Skill tool (new post-skill.sh dispatcher) captures skill names by reading .tool_input.skill. Both append entries to the same JSONL log. The commit workflow reads the log, deduplicates by field, constructs --trailer flags for git interpret-trailers, and pipes the final commit message through before passing to git commit. Scalar values sourced separately: Jira-Ticket from SYNC event jira_key, DSO-Task/Story/Epic via parent traversal, DSO-Review-Score from $ARTIFACTS_DIR/reviewer-findings.json score field. File truncated on git commit exit 0. attribution.enabled defaults to false.
## Scenario Analysis
- Concurrent JSONL writes from parallel agent completions (high, runtime): non-atomic shell appends corrupt the JSONL; commit either drops lines or parse-errors
- JSONL dirty on failed commit (medium, runtime): re-accumulated contributors appear in next commit's trailers across change boundaries
- Nested Agent tool calls inflate DSO-Agent list (medium, runtime): sub-sub-agents both appended to orchestrator's log
- Trailer injection splits existing trailer blocks (high, runtime): Signed-off-by or Co-authored-by present in message; blank-line boundary misdetection inlines DSO trailers into body
- Truncation/write race on rapid sequential commits (medium, runtime): hook write for commit N+1 wiped by truncation from commit N
- Vendor-patched git version string misparsed (medium, deployment): 2.39.3-1.el9 suffix causes TRAILER_SKIPPED on capable git install
- ARTIFACTS_DIR absent in CI (high, deployment): hooks write to wrong path silently; commit proceeds with no trailers, no error signal
- post-agent.sh regression when attribution disabled (critical, deployment): unconditional code path breaks all Agent dispatches for all users
- Review gate hash mismatch from message mutation (critical, deployment): trailer injection after review hash recorded causes gate to flag mismatch on next commit
- JSONL written to repo root when ARTIFACTS_DIR unset (high, configuration): file staged and committed as tracked source, leaking attribution history into repo
- Stale DSO-Review-Score from previous review cycle (medium, configuration): docs-only commit inherits score from unrelated prior review
- Unbounded JSONL growth on repeated commit failures (medium, configuration): hundreds of accumulated entries produce impractical trailer block on eventual success
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): not triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: none
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered — 12 scenarios surviving blue team filter
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keyword: skill file modifications (COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md); bot-psychologist skipped — purely mechanical pipeline steps, no behavioral guidance changes

content.text: ## Incident Overview

**META-PROCESS BUG. Not a request to fix the missing inbound-leaf implementations or the mode→cap wiring in epic 4047 — those are the symptoms. This bug is about the decomposition machinery that produced an epic closure (P1=PASS at every story) with the load-bearing application behavior unimplemented.**

Epic 4047-3cb1-6cb4-46a1 (Derivable level-triggered Jira reconciler) closed P1=PASS across all 11 stories. Live verification per the epic's phased-rollout plan (Phase 0 dry-run → Phase 1 bootstrap-strict → Phase 2 bootstrap-throttle → Phase 3 live-uncapped) was attempted on 2026-05-26. The Phase 0 dry-run "converged" with `OK: steady-state pass converged — 2050 mutations` — but post-hoc audit reveals the convergence flowed through no-op stub handlers. The reconciler computed 2,050 inbound `create` mutations, dispatched each one through `_apply_typed` → `_LEAVES[(inbound, create)]` → `_apply_inbound_create(mutation, *, client=None) -> ApplyResult(mutation.direction, mutation.action, {})` — i.e., direction-guard, return empty result. Zero local tickets were created. The "no new events to commit" log message in the workflow's commit-back step was literal.
## What was observed (audit of 11 stories × 67 tasks under epic 4047)
### Inbound leaf implementation status
| Leaf | Status | Owning story | DD that required body |
| `_apply_inbound_create` | Empty stub | none | none |
| `_apply_inbound_update` | Empty stub | none | none |
| `_apply_inbound_delete` | Empty stub | none | none |

| `_apply_inbound_probe` | Empty stub; real logic lives in separate `inbound_probe.py` module, called from `reconcile.py`, not via the applier leaf | 60c3 | "The inbound_probe leaf classifies four branches" — implementer put logic in a separate file, applier leaf left as stub, verifier accepted "reconcile.route_inbound_probe routes 4 branches" |

| `_apply_inbound_repair_property` | Empty stub at applier.py:318; real implementation exists at applier.py:1110 per task 44e6's spec but **dead code** (never invoked) | 7a75 / Task 44e6 | Task had a detailed function-level spec; no DD said "wire into `_LEAVES`" |
| `_apply_inbound_conflict` | Empty stub | 26de | All DDs about differ-side provenance; nothing about the applier leaf |
| `_apply_inbound_clean_label` | ✅ Real, wired | 2f51 / Task 5615 | Explicit task: "Implement `_inbound_clean_label` leaf — remove dso-id-* via `_call_with_retry(remove_label)`" |
6 of 7 inbound leaves are no-ops. The one that works is the only one with an explicit per-leaf task in the decomposition.
### Mode→cap machinery

The epic spec defined phased mutation caps: Phase 0 cap=0, Phase 1 cap=10, Phase 2 cap=100, Phase 3 uncapped. `mode.py` defines the four modes, `__main__.py` validates the mode string at entry and checks the `.reconciler-phase-gate` lockfile. **`target_mode` is never passed into `reconcile_once` or `applier.apply`.** Story 9e3f's DDs:
- "Invalid `--mode=<unknown>` exits non-zero before fetcher call" ✅ (validates at entry)
- ".reconciler-phase-gate refuses bootstrap-strict→bootstrap-throttle transition" ✅ (operator-gate)
- "Orchestrator dispatches every applier leaf in the draft-1 taxonomy" ✅ (dispatch through stubs counts)
The DDs measured "is the mode flag honored?" — and the answer is yes, AT THE ENTRY POINT. They did not measure "does the mode flag change the apply behavior?" — which it doesn't.
### Validation-class deferral was load-bearing
Story 83ac (rollout-completion audit gating each phase advance, validation-class) DDs included:
- "Bridge-fsck label-only-orphan count after bootstrap-throttle phase completes is 0"
- "5 consecutive workflow_dispatch runs in Phase 3 each emit ≤5 mutations"
- "For every synced ticket pair across all 350 bootstrapped tickets, comments_in_jira == comments_in_local …"

The completion-verifier ruling: **"VERIFIER_VERDICT P1=PASS — 5/5 DDs satisfied. Live-evidence (after_count=0 attach) deferred to rollout-time operator execution per runbook Step 5; deliverables (scripts, tests, runbook) complete."**

"Deferred to rollout-time operator execution" was the explicit closure path. The operator role does not run pre-merge; the system has no automated channel that would have fired this validation before main accepted the epic.
## Critical gaps in the decomposition pipeline
### Gap 1 — DD wording measures shape, not behavior
Story 2f51's DDs (the leaf-implementation story) included:
> "Each (direction, action) leaf raises DirectionMismatchError when called with a Mutation whose direction does not match the leaf's direction"
This passes against any function that calls `_direction_guard()` and then returns an empty `ApplyResult`. The DD describes a guardrail, not a workload.
> "An applier invocation with an unknown action value raises UnknownActionError and **performs zero side-effects**"
This passes if the function does nothing. The whole DD set for "the applier leaves" is satisfied by an applier whose leaves do nothing.
The only DD across all 11 stories that explicitly required a specific leaf BODY was:

> "inbound_clean_label applier leaf **removes the dso-id-* label from a Jira issue** when no matching local row exists; unit test against a captured ACLI response asserts the **label-removal call payload**"
That's the only inbound leaf with a body in production. Pattern is exact.
### Gap 2 — Task decomposition only emits tasks for DD-named work

Story 2f51 → 10 tasks. The one task name with "inbound" in it: `5615: Implement _inbound_clean_label leaf`. No task for `_apply_inbound_create`, `_apply_inbound_update`, `_apply_inbound_delete`, `_apply_inbound_repair_property`, `_apply_inbound_conflict`. The task-decomposer agent operates on the story's DDs; absent DD lines for those bodies, no tasks emerged. This is consistent across the toolchain — the agent is doing what it's instructed to do.
### Gap 3 — "Leaf" was an ambiguous noun the verifier didn't pin

Story 60c3's DD: "the inbound_probe **leaf** classifies four branches against per-branch throwaway DIG issue fixtures." Implementer reading: "I need a function I'll call `inbound_probe` that classifies 4 branches." Put it in `inbound_probe.py`. Wired through `reconcile.route_inbound_probe`. Applier's `_apply_inbound_probe` left as a stub. **The verifier accepted this** — the closure narrative says "reconcile.route_inbound_probe routes 4 branches" — but the applier dispatch path `_LEAVES[(inbound, probe)]` still ends in a no-op. The reconcile.route_inbound_probe call happens BEFORE applier.apply, and emits follow-on mutations that are then dispatched through applier leaves... which are no-ops.
The verifier was looking for behavioral satisfaction of the DD phrase. The phrase was ambiguous about where the work landed. The verifier didn't insist on the specific call chain.
### Gap 4 — Existing real code was never wired

Task 44e6 specced and produced `inbound_repair_property` at applier.py:1110 — the full implementation per its spec. `_LEAVES[(inbound, repair_property)]` points at the empty stub at line 318, not at line 1110. The function exists, has tests, was reviewed and merged — but is **dead code** because nothing imports or calls it. The task's closure required:
- ✅ "happy path: client.set_issue_property called once" (test asserts this against the real function)
- ✅ "failure path: client.remove_label called once" (test asserts this against the real function)
- ✅ "applier.py does NOT import invariants" (grep assertion)

What no AC required: **"_LEAVES[(inbound, repair_property)] is the function this task implements."** So the task closed P1=PASS with the wired _LEAVES still pointing at the stub written in an earlier story.
### Gap 5 — Validation-class deferral was treated as an escape valve, not a tracked obligation
Story 83ac's "deferred to rollout-time operator execution" deferred 4 of 5 DDs to an operator role. The system has:
- No tracked TODO that the operator-execution must run
- No CI step that blocks main acceptance until validation runs
- No bug ticket that's auto-filed if validation doesn't run within N days of epic closure
Live verification ATTEMPTED on 2026-05-26 is the moment this debt came due. Without the attempt, the deferred state would have remained indefinite.
## Concrete artifacts to consider as remediation
This bug intentionally does NOT prescribe a fix — the planning team should evaluate the tradeoffs. Possible mechanisms:
- **DD lint rule**: any story DD whose verb is "raises X" or "exits non-zero" or "registers under key Y" must be paired with a "+ produces behavior Z" DD on the same story. Detect shape-only DD sets.

- **Task-from-DD coverage check**: when stories close, verify that every named function/leaf/handler in the story's Done Definitions or Implementation Approach has at least one task whose AC names that function's behavior. Detect omissions like the 5 missing inbound-leaf tasks.

- **_LEAVES (or analogous registry) coverage assertion**: a structural test that every entry in a dispatch registry resolves to a function with a non-trivial body (heuristic: > N lines OR contains a call to `client.*`). Detects empty stubs in production paths.

- **Validation-class SC tracking**: validation-class success criteria must produce a tracked OBLIGATION ticket at epic closure naming the operator role, the validation script, and a deadline. If the obligation isn't discharged by the deadline, the obligation auto-files a bug parented to the epic.

- **"Leaf" / dispatch-path noun specificity**: DDs that name a function by a partial-noun ("the X leaf" / "the X handler") must specify the call path (e.g., "invoked via _LEAVES[(direction, action)] dispatch"). Pin the verification target.
## Related corpus

Companion to bug f6cc-b174-9e9a-435c. f6cc covers the planning gap that allowed the unverified 1000-issue threshold to ship (one specific instance of the broader decomposition gap). THIS bug covers the structural decomposition machinery that produced f6cc plus the 6 no-op inbound leaves plus the unwired mode→cap routing plus the dead-code `inbound_repair_property` implementation. f6cc is a specific symptom; this is the diagnosis.
## Chain context
- code_version: ${HEAD_SHA}
- Detected: 2026-05-26 audit of epic 4047 stories/tasks during attempted live verification
- Originating epic: 4047-3cb1-6cb4-46a1 (closed P1=PASS, all 11 stories archived)
- Stories audited: 10e3, 25c7, 26de, 2f51, 3d5a, 4496, 60c3, 7a75, 83ac, 9e3f, cde1
- Tasks audited: 67 under epic
- Sibling chain bugs: 5be7, 96c5, bbf0, 5b1c, ec9a, 1788 (each a code defect); f6cc (the operational-threshold meta-bug)
**code_version:** ${HEAD_SHA}

content.text: ## Context

DSO's `detect-stack.sh` emits a single string (`python-poetry`, `ruby-rails`, `node-npm`, etc.) that conflates orthogonal axes — language, package manager, framework, infrastructure, CI platform, platforms-on-top. The flat schema cannot honestly describe a real project (a Strata Rails app on Terraform AWS deployed via GitHub Actions reduces to `ruby-rails`), and each pending first-class-platform epic (Java 70d5-37ee, Terraform jira-dig-1582, Jenkins jira-dig-1583, .NET ee22-4785, Azure DevOps 622a-3955, Strata Epic A2) compounds case-explosion in consumers that switch on the singular value. Polyglot projects cannot be represented at all. This epic migrates the schema to a namespaced flat array, preserving every existing value as an array element for back-compat, in-place across all consumers, with auto-migration of existing project configs and explicit in-session safety nets to mitigate the big-bang risk profile.
## In Scope

- Rewrite `plugins/dso/scripts/detect-stack.sh` to emit comma-separated namespaced array. Existing values (`python-poetry`, `ruby-rails`, `node-npm`, `golang`, `rust-cargo`, `ruby-jekyll`, `convention-based`, `unknown`) preserved as elements; atomic decompositions added (`python`, `ruby`, `node`, `go`, `rust`, `bundler`, `cargo`, `npm`, `poetry`, `rails`, `jekyll`); namespaced forms added (`language:ruby`, `package_manager:bundler`, `framework:rails`). When a compound value is detected, the array always includes both the compound form for back-compat AND every namespaced decomposition; the compound form is never suppressed.

- Author `plugins/dso/docs/DETECTION-SCHEMA.md`: namespaced-tag convention; axis enum (`language`, `package_manager`, `framework`, `infrastructure`, `ci`, `platform`, `build_system` — extensible); legacy-compound preservation rules; consumer query patterns; whitespace-strip rules; empty-value to `unknown` semantics; trailing-empty-element-strip; multi-`stack=` rejection at parse time; detector authoring guide.
- Update `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` to v2: `stack` and `commands.*` schemas; v1 to v2 migration table; semicolon delimiter for `commands.*` documented.

- Migrate every legacy-pattern consumer in DSO from singular-equality to array-membership. Pre-migration inventory committed as `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` BEFORE any migration commit. Known consumers: `resolve-stack-adapter.sh:44`, `prefill-config.sh:138`, `project-detect.sh:346,348`. Inventory is the migration checklist; sprint stories sized one-per-consumer; `dso:completion-verifier` confirms checklist 100% before A0 closes.

- Add pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` blocking future legacy patterns. Documented self-exclusion list covers the hook's own source, the synthetic-detector fixture, the schema doc's anti-pattern section; future tests use `# stack-case-exempt: <reason>` annotation.

- Auto-migrate existing project configs: when a v2-aware consumer reads `dso-config.conf` with legacy singular `stack=`, rewrite to v2 array using `flock` advisory file lock + `mktemp` + `mv` rename atomic write. Idempotent on v2 configs. Edge cases: missing trailing newline, malformed YAML rejected with named-line error, comments preserved, multiple `stack=` lines rejected, empty `stack=` migrated to single-element `unknown` array, read-only filesystem (EROFS) gracefully falls back to in-memory translation with `[DSO WARN]` log.

- Upgrade `commands.*` to multi-valued (semicolon `;` separator, NOT comma — chosen to avoid collision with comma-bearing command args like pytest `-k 'foo,bar'`): `commands.test_runner`, `commands.lint`, `commands.format`, `commands.format_check`, `commands.lint_ruff`, `commands.lint_mypy`. `commands.lint_ruff` and `commands.lint_mypy` are pre-existing single-valued keys being retrofitted; the polyglot fixture exercise is limited to `commands.test_runner` and `commands.lint`.
- Add `depends_on` link + one-line "blocked on A0" comment to each pending platform-integration epic: 70d5-37ee, jira-dig-1582, jira-dig-1583, ee22-4785, 622a-3955.

- Test fixtures (`tests/fixtures/stack-detection/`): one per existing stack value, two polyglot combinations (Python+JS, Ruby+Terraform), one Strata-anticipation fixture (`.template-application-rails/<name>.yml` with `_commit` + `_src_path`).
- Synthetic-detector behavioral test (`tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh` + `tests/scripts/test-synthetic-detector.sh`): exercises new tag introduction AND collision case.

- Pre-cutover review checklist appended to the final commit's PR body for the deep-tier reviewer: audit clean, fixture tests green, round-trip tests green, smoke run green, inventory 100% checked, polyglot fixture executes both runners.
## Out of Scope
- Detector implementations for new platforms (Strata = Epic A2; Java, Terraform, Jenkins, .NET, Azure DevOps = the linked epics).
- Per-detection confidence scoring; per-detection source-file attribution; JSON/YAML detector output formats.
- Multi-runner CI orchestration logic; per-axis precedence rules at the detection layer.
- Renaming/restructuring `dso-config.conf` keys beyond the migration noted.
- Rollback escape hatch (env var) — declined; rollback is `git revert` of the release.
- CI cache invalidation logic for the mixed-state-during-partial-deploy scenario — release-notes guidance only.
## Success Criteria

1. Detection emits namespaced array per fixture, including Strata-anticipation. Running `detect-stack.sh` against each fixture in `tests/fixtures/stack-detection/` (eight existing stack values + two polyglot combinations + one Strata-anticipation fixture) produces a comma-separated array matching golden-master assertions in `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md`. The Strata-anticipation fixture (with `.template-application-rails/<name>.yml`) plus a stub Strata detector together produce an array containing `ruby,bundler,rails,ruby-rails,language:ruby,package_manager:bundler,framework:rails,framework:strata-rails,platform:strata`. End-to-end smoke test runs `validate.sh --ci` against the polyglot fixture (Python+JS) AND asserts the emitted stack array contains exactly `{python, ruby, poetry, bundler, python-poetry, ruby-rails, language:python, language:ruby, package_manager:poetry, package_manager:bundler, framework:rails}`. The multi-command iteration path through `commands.test_runner` is exercised (both `pytest` and `npm test` execute and report separately). Verified by `tests/scripts/test-detect-stack-fixtures.sh` passing in CI.

2. All consumers migrated; existing configs auto-migrate idempotently. Pre-migration inventory `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` enumerates every legacy-pattern hit before migration commits. Post-migration, the same audit script returns zero legacy-pattern matches across `plugins/` and `.claude/`. Pre-commit hook `check-no-stack-case.sh` blocks reintroduction with documented self-exclusion list. Round-trip tests cover (a) v1 to v2 rewrite on first read with audit comment using atomic write+flock, (b) v2 idempotency, (c) edge cases — missing trailing newline, malformed YAML rejected with file+line error, comments preserved, multiple `stack=` rejected, empty `stack=` to `unknown`, EROFS graceful fallback with warn-log.

3. `commands.*` keys are multi-valued; polyglot iteration verified. Schema documents semicolon-separated lists for the listed `commands.*` keys. SC3's exercise is bounded to `commands.test_runner` and `commands.lint`; other listed keys retrofitted but not fixture-exercised in this epic. The polyglot Python+JavaScript fixture demonstrates `commands.test_runner=pytest;npm test` with both runners executing during one `validate.sh --ci` run, both results reported separately, empty trailing list elements stripped.

4. Synthetic-detector and collision behavioral tests pass with specific outcomes. `tests/fixtures/detect-fake.sh` synthetic detector emits a new namespaced tag (`platform:fake`) AND a tag colliding with an existing compound (`ruby-rails` from a non-Ruby fixture). Test asserts: (a) the synthetic `platform:fake` tag is present in consumer output without error; (b) the colliding `ruby-rails` tag from the non-Ruby fixture is deduplicated to a single occurrence in the emitted array; (c) no gate exits non-zero solely due to the collision.

5. Detector author can implement a new detector using only the published contract; documentation and dependent epics linked. A detector author can implement `detect-terraform.sh` (or any pending platform-integration detector) using only the published `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` contract, with no changes to shared consumer code; verified by the synthetic-detector behavioral test passing without modification to any consumer in `plugins/dso/scripts/`. `DETECTION-SCHEMA.md` and `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` v2 published; referenced from `CLAUDE.md`. Each of 70d5-37ee, jira-dig-1582, jira-dig-1583, ee22-4785, 622a-3955 has a `depends_on` link to A0 and a one-line "blocked on A0" comment.
## Scenario Analysis
10 surviving scenarios from red/blue team filter; mitigations folded into In Scope. 1 critical scenario (mixed-state partial deploy) declared OUT (release-notes guidance).
- Auto-migration concurrent race (high, runtime) — flock + atomic mktemp/mv
- Whitespace-padded values (high, runtime) — schema-mandated strip
- commands.* embedded comma collision (high, runtime) — `;` separator
- Pre-commit hook self-trigger (high, deployment) — self-exclusion list
- Mixed state during partial deploy (critical, deployment) — OUT of scope; release-notes only
- Read-only CI checkout (high, deployment) — EROFS in-memory fallback
- Smoke run polyglot coverage (high, deployment) — SC1 explicit
- Empty `stack=` (high, configuration) — empty to unknown semantics
- Trailing empty list element (medium, configuration) — strip-empty rule
- Multiple `stack=` lines (high, configuration) — reject at migration time
## Approach

Big-bang in-place migration in one epic with explicit in-session safety nets: pre-migration consumer audit committed as artifact; post-migration audit-gate enforcement (zero legacy patterns); pre-commit hook preventing reintroduction; fixture matrix covering all stack values plus polyglot plus Strata-anticipation; auto-migration round-trip tests with edge cases; synthetic-detector + collision behavioral tests; end-to-end smoke run; pre-cutover review checklist for deep-tier reviewer.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| v2 `stack` array (dso-config.conf) | Auto-migration script rewrites v1→v2 at first /dso:onboarding run post-upgrade; `/dso:onboarding` writes fresh on new projects | Operator edit; multi-stack project adds entries | All stack-aware scripts (detect-stack.sh, generate-semgrep-config.sh, polyglot test gate, polyglot kudos triggers, mutation-testing.yml) | N/A — persistent per-project; entries removed when stack uninstalled |

| Semicolon-delimited `commands.*` keys (multi-value support) | Auto-migration or onboarding write | Operator edit; APPEND-by-default, operator must explicitly clear to overwrite | Polyglot consumers parse on `;` | N/A — persistent |

| `verification:legacy`-style v2 migration sentinel | Migration script writes once at first v1→v2 conversion | Stable | /dso:onboarding skips re-migration on subsequent runs by reading the sentinel | **Removed after the v1→v2 migration window closes (operator manually unsets when v1 support is dropped from the plugin entirely).** The plugin maintains v1 read-compat for a documented N-version window; the sentinel is RETIRED at the version boundary when v1 read-compat is dropped. |

| `# stack-case-exempt` inline annotations (in dso-config.conf) | Operator manually adds when a stack name needs case preservation | Operator edit | Migration / detection scripts skip case-normalization for annotated lines | N/A — persistent per annotation; removed manually if no longer needed |

| Pre-commit hook self-exclusion list | Hook installation step writes the exclusion list (the hook excludes itself + the migration script from its own checks) | Re-installation rewrites; manual edit otherwise | The hook reads at every commit | Removed if the hook is uninstalled |

| `tests/audits/A0-stack-consumer-inventory.md` (consumer audit artifact) | Sprint that ships this epic writes the initial inventory | **UPDATE owner: each future epic that adds a new stack-consuming script is responsible for adding its consumer entry to this file** (preplanning-checklist item; CI grep test asserts that any new script under `plugins/dso/scripts/` matching `*stack*` has an entry in the inventory) | Operators reviewing stack-detection scope; future audits | N/A — persistent project artifact; closes the audit's "future consumer drift" gap by making each new consumer add itself |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -nE '^stack\s*=' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows the v2 array format.

This is a scrutiny:pending stub epic capturing planning-workflow insights surfaced during the 2026-05-24 re-brainstorm of the Jira sync remediation epic (superseded epic 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f). Expand via /dso:brainstorm <epic-id> when the team has bandwidth to design the enhancements.
## Problem

The brainstorm/preplanning pipeline (Agent Clarity, Scope, Value, Feasibility, Red Team, Blue Team reviewers + scrutiny gate + cross-epic scan) does not reliably surface architectural defects that live in the *integration* between modules — only those visible in single-module code or single-document review. The Jira sync remediation epic (3a03) shipped a snapshot-diff design that all reviewers passed; pass-1 live verification surfaced a P0 inversion bug in the differ→applier contract that none of the review layers could see. Same shape recurred across multiple brainstorm rounds for the same functionality. Each prior implementation bug (ProjectKey null → priority dict → add_label flag → architectural inversion → bridge_state persistence) hid the next; reviewers saw code in isolation while the integration was never exercised end-to-end until live pass 1.
## Candidate enhancements (for future brainstorm)

1. Mandatory live-spike before scrutiny for class:architectural epics. A throwaway script that exercises the core pipeline against real external state with no writes. The empirical first-line check catches bug classes the reviewer pipeline structurally cannot.

2. Bug-class-to-property-test mapping requirement at spec-write time. Every prior in-class bug must correspond to a property assertion in the new design; unmapped bug classes signal a design hole. Enforce as a gate.

3. Targeted pre-mortem dispatch beyond Red Team's adversarial scenarios. A focused 'find the next architectural bug class that reviewers won't catch' dispatch using the prior failure pattern as priming context.

4. Capability probe layering correctness. The existing capability_check convention is too easy to write at the wrong layer (verifying surface features that aren't the load-bearing contract). Require probe layer to be specified explicitly: surface / contract / integration / topology.

5. Integration-test-first gate for replacement epics. When a new epic supersedes a closed-with-defect epic, require the new spec to include a property test that would have caught the prior defect. Forcing function: the new design must demonstrably differ from the prior design at the level the prior failure occurred.

content.text: ## Story S5: Config migration + fail-closed guards + `{file}` placeholder substitution
### Description

**What**: Before `start` launches, validate: (a) `commands.test_runner` is set and non-empty → missing/empty exits non-zero with a fail-closed error (never a silently-green gate); (b) the resolved runner path does not reference `plugins/dso/scripts/runners/` (the per-language runner scripts this epic deletes) → if it does, emit a migration warning with the recommended replacement value and exit non-zero. For the per-file gate: `commands.test_file_runner` uses a documented `{file}` placeholder that the gate substitutes before invoking; when the key is unset, fall back to `$commands.test_runner <file>` with file appended positionally.

**Why**: Without fail-closed guards, a missing or stale config key produces silently-green gates that let broken code merge. The `{file}` placeholder convention is what makes the per-file gate polyglot without per-language code.
**Scope**:
- IN: start-time config validation, migration warning for deleted-runner references, `{file}` placeholder substitution, fallback semantics
- OUT: host project's actual config-file migration (users run `dso update-artifacts` or edit config manually — the launcher just warns), onboarding-side write (covered by 87e9-0bc8)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, running `test-run start` with `commands.test_runner` unset or empty exits non-zero with a fail-closed error (no silent success)
← Satisfies: "start validates (a) commands.test_runner is set and non-empty — if missing/empty, exits non-zero with a fail-closed error (no silently-green gate)"
- When this story is complete, a host config pointing `commands.test_runner` at `plugins/dso/scripts/runners/*` produces a migration warning with the recommended replacement value and exits non-zero
← Satisfies: "validates the resolved path does not reference plugins/dso/scripts/runners/ — if it does, emits a migration warning with the recommended replacement value and exits non-zero"

- When this story is complete, the per-file gate substitutes `{file}` in `commands.test_file_runner` with the target path before invocation; when the key is unset, the per-file invocation is `$commands.test_runner <file>`

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

content.text: ## Context

Three attribution gaps converge here. First, bug closure today requires a freeform `--reason` string with narrow prefix rules (`Fixed:` or `Escalated to user:`) — unstructured, unqueryable, lossy to Jira. Jira ships five default resolutions (Fixed / Won\t Fix / Duplicate / Incomplete / Cannot Reproduce) that map directly onto agent use-cases. Second, the local `author` field conflates two distinct concepts: the human who opened the ticket vs the agent/skill/event that precipitated it. Replacing `author` with a typed `reporter` enum (User / Jira / Agent:Skill:<name> / Agent:Skill:Unknown / Agent:Deferral / Agent:Gotcha / Agent:Suggestion / Agent:Coordination) gives both Jira-compatible attribution (accountId for humans) and DSO-local agent provenance (trigger source for agents). Third, the real tickets tracker currently holds 336 open (plus 1,571 archived) tickets authored by `Test` — leakage from test fixtures into the production tracker. These must be purged and prevented.
## Success Criteria
- New `resolution` field written as part of STATUS=closed event; enum: `Fixed` | `Wont_Fix` | `Duplicate` | `Incomplete` | `Cannot_Reproduce`. Jira-compatible names.

- Bug close no longer requires freeform `--reason`; `--resolution` replaces it as the structured field. `--reason` becomes optional free-text sugar (blank allowed, historical tickets preserved unchanged). Migration maps existing "Fixed: X" -> resolution=Fixed,reason=X; "Escalated to user: X" -> resolution=Incomplete,reason=X.

- `author` field renamed to `reporter` with enum above. Backfill migration: `Claude` -> `Agent:Skill:Unknown`, `Joe Oakhart`/`Main` -> `User`, `Test` -> DELETE ticket (not mapped), `github-actions[bot]` -> `Agent:Coordination`, `<missing>` -> `User`.

- Guard: `ticket create` rejects `--reporter=Test*` unless `DSO_TEST_FIXTURE=1` environment variable is set. Pre-commit hook scans for Test-authored tickets in `.tickets-tracker/` and fails if any are present.
- Force-delete of all 336 open + 1,571 archived `Test`-authored tickets from the real tracker in a single atomic migration commit.

- Bridge outbound writes resolution via Jira REST API `transitions.resolution`; inbound reads Jira resolution field and maps to local enum. `reporter=Jira` and `reporter=Agent:*` values sync to Jira as labels (since Jira assignee/reporter require accountId).
## Approach

Four migrations land in sequence within this epic: (1) reducer schema extension to add `resolution` and `reporter` fields with defaults; (2) CLI surface extension — new `--resolution` flag on transition, new `--reporter` flag on create, deprecation of `--reason`; (3) backfill migration that reads all existing events and emits EDIT events mapping the legacy fields; (4) Test-ticket purge + guard hook.
