DIG-4273.summary: CI-enforced quality gates: staged CI pipeline with LLM review and GitHub Ruleset enforcement

content.text: ## Context

DSO's host-project configuration today distributes a single conceptual choice — workflow mode — across four correlated `dso-config.conf` keys (`merge.strategy`, `enforcement.strategy`, `worktree.isolation_enabled`, `attribution.enabled`) plus three session-scoped environment variables (`SPRINT_MODE` derived by `mode-detect.sh`, `DSO_SPRINT_MODE` set by sprint Phase F, `MERGE_TO_MAIN_PR_MODE` set by `merge-to-main-pr.sh`). The four config keys can be set into combinations that have no coherent meaning (e.g., `merge.strategy=pr` + `enforcement.strategy=local`), and consumers branch on derived signals as if they were primary, so silent half-states pick the wrong pipeline. The proximate failure surfaced as bug `e21b-1809-eb04-477c`: PR #124's sprint inferred the wrong mode, never created or pushed `story/4100-95a4/*` branches, and `sprint-story-review.yml` never fired. This epic collapses the four keys + three env vars into a single `dso.workflow=local|ci-pr` toggle, with a hybrid shim+migrator strategy that follows the project's established `ticket-migrate-*.sh` pattern.

Cleanup blast-radius (three-tier breakdown): (a) hot-path scripts (`merge-to-main.sh`, `merge-to-main-pr.sh`, `mode-detect.sh`, `check-sprint-trailer.sh`, `apply-attribution-trailers.sh`) — require TDD regression tests written RED before any change; touched by the sprint/commit pipeline. (b) Orchestrator-facing skill files (~14 `plugins/dso/skills/**/*.md`) — change-and-validate via existing skill tests. (c) Reference / documentation files (`CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `WORKTREE-GUIDE.md`, `CI-INTEGRATION.md`, `dso-config.reference.conf`, host-level `CLAUDE.md` and ADRs) — update last; grep-verified by SC6.

Semantic change acknowledged: `mode-detect.sh` today checks `merge.strategy=pr AND enforcement.strategy=ci AND git remote non-empty` to return `ci-pr`. The new design moves remote detection to `/dso:onboarding` (write-time) and trusts the committed `dso.workflow` value at read-time. A host project with `dso.workflow=ci-pr` committed but no remote (offline / local dev) now returns `ci-pr` rather than `local`. The migration trigger pattern matches the existing ticket-migrate-* invocations: the migrator runs silently from skill preambles with `|| true`, marker-gated; the resulting `dso-config.conf` diff is staged and committed by the migration commit.
## Success Criteria

1. After the migrator runs on a host project, `.claude/dso-config.conf` contains the literal line `dso.workflow=<local|ci-pr>` exactly once, and each of the four legacy keys appears only as a commented-out line annotated `# migrated to dso.workflow (v<plugin-ver>)`. The migration commit auto-stages both the rewritten config and the sentinel file. Verifiable by `git diff` on the file before and after migrator invocation against a fixture project.

2. `read-config.sh dso.workflow` returns the correct value when invoked against four fixture configs: (a) legacy keys only — returns the shim-derived value with a one-time stderr deprecation warning per process invocation naming each legacy key (CI-suppressible via `DSO_DEPRECATION_QUIET=1`, which `validate.sh --ci` sets automatically); (b) `dso.workflow` only — returns the canonical value with no warning; (c) contradictory legacy config — emits a stderr warning naming the conflicting keys and falls back to `local`. Contradictory is defined as any combination where the four legacy keys imply conflicting pipeline modes (test fixture covers `merge.strategy=pr` + `enforcement.strategy=local` and `merge.strategy=direct` + `enforcement.strategy=ci`); (d) no `dso-config.conf` present — non-zero exit with stderr message directing to `/dso:onboarding`. Verifiable by a shell test invoking the shim against four checked-in fixture configs.

3. `migrate-dso-workflow-config.sh` is idempotent following the existing `ticket-migrate-*` pattern: running it twice on the same fixture project produces a zero-byte diff on the second run; supports `--dry-run` (read-only); self-guards by exiting 0 without modifying anything when invoked from within the plugin's own source tree (shell test covers true-positive AND false-positive: host project with a `plugins/dso/` subdirectory that is NOT the plugin source repo). The migrator writes the new config to a temp file in the same directory, fsyncs, then renames atomically; the sentinel `.claude/.dso-config-v2-migrated` is created after the config-rename succeeds. The migrator documents the supported `dso-config.conf` grammar (unquoted `key=value`, `# comment` lines, blank lines); rejects files with inline comments after values, quoted values, duplicate keys, or CRLF line endings with a non-zero exit and clear diagnostic, without mutating the file. If a `.dso-config.conf.pre-migrate-backup` from a prior failed run exists, the migrator detects it and does not overwrite it. No `--rollback` flag — recovery is `git checkout HEAD -- .claude/dso-config.conf` (documented in the migrator's header comment). Verifiable by shell test that runs the migrator twice and asserts `git diff` is empty, plus separate tests for grammar rejection and self-guard cases.

4. `/dso:onboarding` writes `dso.workflow=ci-pr` to `dso-config.conf` when invoked on a project whose `git remote get-url origin` matches `https://github.com/` or `git@github.com:`, and `dso.workflow=local` otherwise; enterprise GitHub hosts default to `local` pending explicit user override. `read-config.sh` directs the user to run `/dso:onboarding` when no `dso-config.conf` is present. Verifiable by a shell test covering fixture remotes: https GitHub, ssh GitHub, no origin, GitLab — each producing the expected `dso.workflow` value.

5. After the per-project sentinel `.claude/.dso-config-v2-migrated` exists (committed to the host repository, not gitignored), subsequent reads via `read-config.sh` of any of the four legacy keys produce a non-zero exit code with a stderr message referencing the recovery command (`git checkout HEAD -- .claude/dso-config.conf`), and the shim's compat translation path is disabled. The migrator emits a reminder to `git add` the sentinel if it detects `.gitignore` covers `.claude/`. Verifiable by a shell test that touches the sentinel and asserts the error path against a fixture config containing a re-added legacy key.

6. No file in any of these categories references `merge.strategy`, `enforcement.strategy`, `worktree.isolation_enabled`, `attribution.enabled`, the `SPRINT_MODE` env variable, the `DSO_SPRINT_MODE` env variable, or the `MERGE_TO_MAIN_PR_MODE` env variable: (a) `plugins/dso/skills/**/*.md`; (b) `plugins/dso/scripts/**/*.sh|*.py`; (c) `plugins/dso/hooks/**`; (d) `.github/workflows/*.yml`. Exempt paths: the migrator script, the compat shim in `read-config.sh`, the reference docs (`dso-config.reference.conf`, `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `WORKTREE-GUIDE.md`, `CI-INTEGRATION.md`), the host-project `CLAUDE.md` and ADRs (rewritten to teach `dso.workflow` as primary), and the entire `tests/` tree. Verifiable by `grep -rln` with `--exclude-dir=tests` and an explicit allowlist for the named exempt files.
7. After this epic, `check-sprint-trailer.sh` and `apply-attribution-trailers.sh` operate under this four-cell behavior matrix, all four cells covered by shell tests:
- (1) `dso.workflow=ci-pr` + `.sprint-active` marker present → enforce trailer / inject trailer.
- (2) `dso.workflow=ci-pr` + no `.sprint-active` → no-op.
- (3) `dso.workflow=local` + `.sprint-active` → no-op (matches current local-mode behavior: trailer is not enforced during local sprints).
- (4) `dso.workflow=local` + no `.sprint-active` → no-op.
## Approach

Add `dso.workflow=local|ci-pr` as the canonical single key. Compat shim in `read-config.sh` maps the four legacy keys → `dso.workflow` at read time, with deprecation warning suppressible via `DSO_DEPRECATION_QUIET=1`. Idempotent `migrate-dso-workflow-config.sh` (modeled on `ticket-migrate-brainstorm-tags.sh`, marker-gated via `.claude/.dso-config-v2-migrated`, `--dry-run` only — NO `--rollback`, plugin-source-repo self-guard, atomic write semantics) rewrites `dso-config.conf` in place. Re-aim ~95 distinct references across the three blast-radius tiers (hot-path scripts, skill files, docs). `/dso:onboarding` writes `dso.workflow` based on GitHub remote detection. The `DSO_SPRINT_MODE` and `MERGE_TO_MAIN_PR_MODE` env vars are eliminated; their semantics derive from `dso.workflow=ci-pr` AND the `.sprint-active` marker. `mode-detect.sh` is reduced to a one-line `read-config.sh dso.workflow` lookup; the legacy git-remote guard is intentionally dropped (remote detection moves to `/dso:onboarding` at write-time). Migrator runs silently from skill preambles, matching the existing ticket-migrate-* invocation pattern; resulting config + sentinel diff are auto-staged and committed by the migration commit.
## Dependencies

None blocking. Relates-to / coordination (consideration signals from cross-epic scan): `136b-6758`, `2a13-0c87`, `8623-8d6a` (all touch `/dso:onboarding`); `70f6-05f1` (depends on `worktree.isolation_enabled` semantics); `7ac3-71a1` (adds new `dso-config.conf` keys on an orthogonal axis); `5018-64ce` (REVIEW-DEFENSE cleanup overlap on scripts/hooks). Resolved by this epic (close-as-superseded post-merge): `e21b-1809-eb04-477c`, `cd24-6553-9d69-40fe`, `fb32-215c-4c78-4e36`. Out of scope: `70fe-1c39-121b-4e08` (planning meta-bug, separate epic); plugin version-rollback compatibility (deferred — `--dry-run` plus git history is the manual recovery path); host-project automation outside `plugins/dso/` that may reference the eliminated env vars (deferred to a release-note migration guide); end-to-end regression test for `e21b-1809-eb04-477c` (accepted gap — Value/validation_signal=3 in fidelity review; PIL marker records the compromise).

content.text: ## Description **What**: Update the sprint orchestrator to drive a PR-per-batch loop: after each batch, create a PR via the merge primitive (delivered by 8787-ac16), wait for CI green via `gh pr checks`, and only start the next batch once the PR merges. Epic completion is the final batch's PR merge — not a separate cumulative push. **Why**: Once 8787-ac16 makes merge PR-based, sprint's existing "merge at epic close" model becomes incorrect. CI (including `validate.sh --ci` once 3aaa-0238's scope expansion lands) must be the inter-batch gate so regressions are caught between batches, not at epic close. **Scope**: - IN: sprint SKILL.md changes to invoke the PR primitive per batch, wait-on-CI loop between batches, removal of the cumulative epic-close push, handling of CI-red between batches (block next batch, surface failure), interaction with `--resume` so a sprint resuming mid-epic re-enters the per-batch loop correctly - OUT: merge-to-main.sh / PR primitive itself (8787-ac16), local hook removal (5428-bebd), documentation updates (ed9c-a277), CI pipeline definition (3aaa-0238) ## Done Definitions - When this story is complete, sprint creates a PR after each batch and waits for CI green before starting the next batch   ← Satisfies SC9: "sprint orchestrator creates a PR per batch ... waits for CI green ... merges via gh pr merge after each batch" - When this story is complete, epic completion in sprint is the final batch's PR merge — there is no separate cumulative push step   ← Satisfies SC9: "epic completion is the final batch's PR merge — not a separate cumulative push" - When this story is complete, a CI failure on a batch PR blocks the next batch from starting and surfaces the failure to the user with actionable context - When this story is complete, sprint `--resume` re-enters the per-batch loop correctly (detects in-flight PR, resumes wait-on-CI rather than re-creating) - When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic ## Considerations - [Interface dependency] Depends on 8787-ac16's merge primitive interface (PR create, wait, merge as a callable unit). Coordinate the contract before implementation. - [Latency] Inter-batch CI latency bounds sprint cadence. Documented in epic 1083-fb3d Scenario Analysis as expected behavior, not a regression. - [State] Sprint's existing batch state machine must be extended to track "PR open / CI pending / merged" between batches; resume must read this correctly. - [Caller impact] end-session SKILL.md and any other caller assuming sprint pushes at epic close must be reviewed for compatibility. ## Escalation Policy **Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Story S7: Host shim compatibility error + plugin version bump
### Description

**What**: When a host project's `.claude/scripts/dso` shim is outdated and does not expose the new `test-run` subcommand, running `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start` should produce an actionable error directing the user to run `dso update-artifacts`, not a raw `command not found`. The plugin version bump in the same commit as S6 triggers `update-artifacts` detection on next invocation, so host projects naturally sync. COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md documents this upgrade path.

**Why**: Host projects can be out of sync with the plugin version. A silent `command not found` sends users on a wild goose chase; a targeted error with the right next action is the difference between a 30-second fix and 20 minutes of debugging.
**Scope**:
- IN: shim error message for unknown `test-run` subcommand, plugin version bump, one-line note in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md
- OUT: automated host-project update (users run `dso update-artifacts` themselves)
### Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, running `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start` with an outdated shim returns an actionable error directing the user to run `dso update-artifacts` instead of a raw `command not found`

← Satisfies: "after upgrading the plugin, a host project that runs .claude/scripts/dso test-run start with an outdated shim receives an actionable error directing the user to run dso update-artifacts, not a raw command not found"

content.text: ## Why

Epic 4047 (Derivable level-triggered Jira reconciler) closed P1=PASS across all 11 stories on 2026-05-25, but a 2026-05-26 attempted live-verification revealed the load-bearing implementation is no-op scaffolding. The reconciler runs end-to-end without crashes (after the bug f6cc / defect chain was fixed) but every inbound mutation flows through stub applier leaves that return empty `ApplyResult` without writing anything. Mode→cap routing is validated at entry but never threaded to the apply step. Bug 1761-21ca-cb74-44a6 captures the planning/decomposition machinery that produced this — its remediation candidates are applied by hand throughout this epic to avoid reproducing the same pattern.
## Scope
Complete the reconciler so that:
- All 7 inbound `(direction, action)` leaves perform their documented behavior (5 unimplemented today + 1 dead-code + 1 already-working).
- The 4-mode rollout machinery (dry-run / bootstrap-strict / bootstrap-throttle / live) actually enforces per-mode mutation caps and emits asymmetric manifests per mode.
- The completion-verifier toolchain refuses to accept "deferred to operator execution" as DD satisfaction without producing a tracked obligation ticket (the bug 1761 fix — applied to ourselves).
- The live DIG project is bootstrapped through Phase 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 with operator-committed phase-gate transitions and rollback validation.
## Out of scope

- Per-element-class round-trip idempotency for ALL collection types — Story 4 exercises the round-trip path on representative classes (comments, labels, links); broader element-class coverage is a follow-on.
- Cross-project reconciler operation (DIG is the only project today).
- ACLI version upgrades.
## Constraints (lessons from bug 1761 applied by hand)
Every story DD MUST:
1. Pair a shape clause with a behavior clause ("function exists" + "produces observable file/state change Z").
2. Name the dispatch path explicitly when referencing a leaf/handler/router (e.g., `_LEAVES[(inbound, create)]`).
3. Enumerate every function body that must be implemented.
4. Refuse \"deferred to operator execution\" as a closure path UNLESS the deferral creates an obligation ticket via Story 3's mechanism with deadline + owner + validation command.
Every task list under a story MUST produce ≥1 task per function body named in the Done Definitions.
## Success Criteria (live-verified, with tracked obligations)
1. After Phase 0 dispatch on main, `ticket list --tag=imported:reconciler-bootstrap` returns zero tickets (cap=0 honored). Tracked obligation: Phase 0 dispatch within 7 days of Story 1+2 merge.
2. After Phase 1 dispatch (5 passes), `ticket list --tag=imported:reconciler-bootstrap` returns exactly 50 tickets. Tracked obligation per pass.
3. After Phase 2 dispatch (3 passes), `ticket list --tag=imported:reconciler-bootstrap` returns exactly 350 tickets cumulatively. Tracked obligation per pass.
4. After Phase 3 enablement, 5 consecutive scheduled cron runs each emit a manifest with ≤5 mutations. Tracked obligation: monitor for 7 days after Phase 3 enable.
5. Bridge-fsck label-only-orphan count drops from 197 (at Phase 1 start) to 0 (at Phase 2 end). Tracked obligation: capture both counts.
6. `_LEAVES` registry structural coverage test passes: every entry resolves to a function with ≥10 effective code lines OR contains a state-changing call. CI gate, NOT operator-deferred.
7. Mode→cap behavioral test passes: dispatching `mode=bootstrap-strict` against a 2050-mutation fixture produces a manifest with exactly 10 applied + 2040 deferred. CI gate, NOT operator-deferred.
## Closure Checks
- All 4 child stories closed P1=PASS via the new completion-verifier protocol (Story 3 extension).
- All Phase 0/1/2/3 obligation tickets discharged (closed with evidence) OR explicitly rolled into a follow-on epic with operator sign-off.
- `_LEAVES` registry coverage test in CI; passing.
- `rollback-phase-1.sh` exercised against a fixture and producing the documented teardown.

- relates_to bug 1761-21ca-cb74-44a6 (decomposition meta-bug — this epic applies its remediation by hand AND ships Story 3 as the toolchain fix)

content.text: ## Context

DSO uses an event-sourced ticket store on an orphan `tickets` git branch where parallel sessions (multiple worktrees, multiple agents, CI runs) concurrently append events. Two silent-data-loss failure modes exist today, both rooted in the same underlying pattern — "concurrent writes to shared state without a global ordering contract":

1. **ID collision** — `ticket-create.sh:169-177` derives ticket IDs from `uuid4[:8]`, yielding 32 bits of entropy. Birthday-paradox collision probability exceeds 1% at ~9,300 tickets and 50% at ~77,000. Current count ~1,907 — preemptive hardening before the curve bites. Under parallel session load this risk materializes earlier.

2. **STATUS conflict loss** — `ticket_reducer/_processors.py:60-75` records CAS-mismatched STATUS events into `state.conflicts[]` but never resolves them. Under concurrent writes across worktrees, STATUS transitions are silently dropped at merge time.

Both failure modes produce silent corruption of the ticket history — the beneficiaries of this epic are the DSO development teams and agents orchestrating multi-session work, especially those running parallel worktrees where race windows are largest. "Merge-safety" is the unifying property: it requires both ID uniqueness and write-order correctness as prerequisites for a consistent event-sourced store under parallel sessions. These SCs are prerequisites for each other — they share the reducer schema bump and SNAPSHOT rebuild — and shipping them together eliminates a redundant release cycle.
## Success Criteria
### Identity hardening

1. **ID entropy floor**: `ticket-create.sh` uses 16 hex chars for new canonical IDs (64 bits of entropy, <10⁻¹⁵ collision probability at any foreseeable count). Existing 8-char tickets are preserved untouched; both lengths are valid canonical forms. Forward-only migration — no backfill.

2. **CLI resolver accepts all ID forms**: All ticket CLI commands accept ticket references in any of — canonical (8 or 16 hex), alias (e.g. `brave-quiet-cedar`), `jira_key` (e.g. `DSO-123`), or an unambiguous prefix of any form. Resolution precedence is: exact canonical → jira_key → alias (if unique) → short-id (if unique) → prefix match. Ambiguous prefix or ambiguous alias → reject with a disambiguation list. All existing `ticket-lib.sh` consumers (`ticket-create`, `ticket-transition`, `ticket-link`, `ticket-tag`, `ticket-untag`, `ticket-edit`, `ticket-comment`, `emit-review-event`) continue to resolve legacy 8-char IDs without modification; parity is asserted by regression test.

3. **Display cascade + dual-output create**: Config key `ticket.display_mode` accepts the enum `auto | canonical | short`. Default `auto` renders `jira_key → alias → short → full` per ticket. Unknown config values fall back to `auto` with a startup warning. `ticket create` emits two lines on stdout: a human-readable summary line (`Created: brave-quiet-cedar (jira: DSO-123)`) followed by the canonical ID on the **last** line (no trailing blank lines). Scripts extract canonical via `| tail -1`.

4. **In-repo pet-alias word list**: `plugins/dso/resources/ticket-wordlist.txt` contains ~1500 adjectives + ~1500 nouns, each 3–6 letters. Alias format is `adj-noun-noun` (cap ≈20 chars including hyphens). Aliases are computed deterministically at ticket creation from `hash(canonical_id)` indexed into the wordlist **and stored in the CREATE event's `data.alias` field** (cached, not recomputed on read — immune to future wordlist edits). If the wordlist file is absent at create time, emit a startup warning and fall back to the short-form ID as display; never crash. When two tickets hash to the same alias, the display layer renders `alias (short)` to disambiguate.

5. **Consumer migration**: The four known consumers of the legacy `[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}` regex pattern are updated to extract canonical via `| tail -1`: `plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/SKILL.md:539`, `plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/SKILL.md:122`, `plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md:181`, `plugins/dso/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md:1518`. The epic ships with a grep audit log (`rg '\[0-9a-f\]\{4\}-\[0-9a-f\]\{4\}'` output) documenting all known call sites and the migration status of each.
### Concurrency hardening

6. **STATUS parent-chain resolution**: STATUS events carry a `parent_status_uuid` field referencing the prior STATUS event's uuid at the time of write (`null` for the first STATUS of a ticket, where the CREATE is the implicit root). The reducer detects forks (two or more events sharing the same `parent_status_uuid` — including two `null`-parent events on the same ticket) and resolves via **total-order deterministic tie-break**: all siblings of the chain sharing a parent are ranked lexically by their own uuid; lowest wins; losers are discarded. When a `parent_status_uuid` references an event not present after full replay, the event is treated as a new chain root and a `DANGLING_PARENT` warning log is emitted. On every fork resolution the reducer emits the structured log line `PARENT_CHAIN_FORK_RESOLVED ticket=<id> winner=<uuid> dropped=[<uuid>,...] loser_env_id=[<env_id>,...]` at INFO. Absence of this line when no fork exists is the negative assertion. `state.conflicts[]` accumulation is removed; all forks are now resolved at replay.

7. **Reducer schema bump + grandfathered replay**: Reducer compiled-state `schema_version` is bumped. SNAPSHOT rebuild backfills `parent_status_uuid` for existing STATUS events using timestamp order as fallback tie-break, so pre-migration state is fully consistent post-rebuild. Any pre-migration `state.conflicts[]` entries are resolved once during rebuild via the same fallback.
### Rollout, regression, and validation

8. **Transitional legacy-client behavior**: Old plugin copies (pre-upgrade worktrees, cached installs) that continue generating 8-hex IDs post-upgrade are documented as a transitional state. No enforcement gate is added — the epic accepts that legacy-entropy IDs may continue to appear for some bounded period post-release. This is called out in both the release notes and the ticket-system architecture doc. The `LEGACY_CLIENT_WRITE` advisory log is **out of scope** for this epic; may be added later if the transition proves slow.

9. **Zero regression**: Jira bridge (jira_key flows, SYNC/EDIT events), CLI surface, and full test suite pass unchanged. The epic ships with an explicit Jira bridge audit: grep the bridge source for any `[a-f0-9]{8}` or 8-char length assumption; document each finding as confirmed-safe or migrate it. Output of the audit is committed as `plugins/dso/docs/designs/3e74-56da-jira-bridge-audit.md`.

10. **Integration test: concurrency harness**: New integration test at `tests/integration/ticket-id-concurrency/` constructs 50 simulated concurrent STATUS writes on divergent branches, merges them, and asserts: (a) every write is represented in the reduced SNAPSHOT (either as winner or in the `dropped=` log entry — zero silent loss), (b) fork resolution is deterministic across 10 repeated runs (same winners every time), (c) `PARENT_CHAIN_FORK_RESOLVED` log lines are emitted per fork. **Excluded from `test_gate.test_dirs` default (tests/) — runs only via explicit invocation** (`tests/integration/ticket-id-concurrency/run.sh` or `make test-integration`). Not in CI's default gate; may be added to a nightly/weekly run separately.

11. **Integration test: collision probe**: New integration test at `tests/integration/ticket-id-collision/` generates 100,000 IDs via `ticket-create.sh`, asserts zero canonical collisions **and** zero alias collisions. Same integration-only classification as SC10 — explicit invocation, not in default CI or test-gate runs.
## Approach

- **`ticket-create.sh:169-177`** — widen uuid4 slice from 8→16 hex; compute pet-alias from canonical via hash→wordlist lookup; persist alias into CREATE event's `data.alias` field; dual-output stdout (human summary line + canonical on last line).

- **`ticket_reducer/_processors.py:process_status`** — require `parent_status_uuid` on STATUS events; detect forks (same parent, including `null==null`); resolve via total-order lexical tie-break; emit structured fork-resolution logs; remove `state.conflicts[]` accumulation. Handle `DANGLING_PARENT` case by treating as root + warning.
- **`ticket-transition.sh`** — read the current top-of-chain STATUS event's uuid at write time; embed as `parent_status_uuid` in the new STATUS event.

- **`ticket-lib.sh`** — extend input resolver to accept alias, short (with uniqueness check), and jira_key; precedence: exact canonical → jira_key → alias → short → prefix. Build `alias_counts` at state load (trivial since aliases are stored).
- **Display layer** — config-driven cascade in `ticket list`, `ticket show`, `ticket create`. `display_mode` enum validation at config-read with fallback warning.
- **New files**:
- `plugins/dso/resources/ticket-wordlist.txt` (~20 KB, curated — 3–6 letter words, no slurs, no ambiguous technical terms).
- `tests/integration/ticket-id-concurrency/run.sh` + fixtures.
- `tests/integration/ticket-id-collision/run.sh` + fixtures.
- `plugins/dso/docs/designs/3e74-56da-jira-bridge-audit.md`.
- **Config** — add `ticket.display_mode` to `dso-config.conf` defaults and `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`.
- **Consumer updates** — mechanical replacement of regex-extract with `| tail -1` in the 4 listed skill files, plus a documented grep audit of the full codebase.
- **Schema migration** — one-shot SNAPSHOT rebuild on first reducer run post-upgrade; backfills `parent_status_uuid` via timestamp order.
## Out of Scope
- No Jira-side ID format changes (jira_key unaffected as external anchor).
- No backfill or rewrite of existing 8-char ticket IDs — forward-only.
- No change to the event filename scheme (`timestamp_ns + full uuid4` is already unique).
- No new CLI subcommands (only behavioral extensions of existing commands).
- No external Python runtime dependency (coolname considered and rejected in favor of in-repo word list).
- No enforcement gate blocking old plugin clients from writing legacy-entropy IDs (transitional).
- No `LEGACY_CLIENT_WRITE` observability log (deferred; may revisit if transition is slow).
- No i18n or alternative wordlists (single curated English list; wordlist mutation constraints discussed above — aliases are cached at creation so edits don't retroactively rename tickets).
## Coordination Notes

Resolver surface (SC2) shares code with `6f7a-4ba6` (ticket delete subcommand) and `2c28-e5b9` (core query layer). This epic should land before or be coordinated with those two to minimize merge churn on `ticket-lib.sh`.
## Dependencies
None upstream. Downstream: `0777-0f3d` (multi-agent coordination primitives) already `depends_on 3e74-56da`.

content.text: Epic 1 of 2. Establishes the full kudos ledger infrastructure and 10 primary quality triggers for the process-reward tracking system.

CONTEXT: Engineering teams adopting AI coding agents need a feedback system that reinforces quality behaviors at commit time. Without explicit recognition, agents optimize for task completion over quality practices. This epic delivers the ledger, anti-gaming stack, and 10 triggers so that every commit produces an auditable record of recognized behaviors.

APPROACH: Implement ledger, award formula, anti-gaming controls, and 10 triggers as pure shell + Python stdlib anchored to commit-validate.sh in the existing commit workflow. Spikes S0/S1 de-risk sg pattern matching and Python AST clone detection before those triggers ship.

SPRINT SCOPE RATIONALE: Infrastructure without triggers produces zero awards. All 10 triggers share one user goal (recognizing quality behaviors at commit time) and depend on the same anti-gaming stack. Spike tasks are investigation prerequisites, not sprint work items.
SUCCESS CRITERIA:

SC-E1-1: .kudos/ledger.jsonl (append-only JSONL) — fields: session_id, trigger_id, diff_hash, artifact_sha, verification_method, workflow_phase, message, points (int >= 1), jitter_factor (float in [0.8,1.2]), timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC); all string fields JSON-escaped; .kudos/ in .gitignore
SC-E1-2: Award formula: Award(n) = round(BasePoints x (1/(n+1)) x jitter), jitter in [0.8,1.2] uniform random, min 1 point, floating-point division; n = prior session ledger entries for trigger_id
SC-E1-3: Deduplication: one award per (trigger_id, diff_hash) per session
SC-E1-4: Session ceiling: kudos.session_ceiling from dso-config.conf (default 100, validated >0; absent key uses default); awards blocked when reached, prohibition-block message shown
SC-E1-5: kudos-write-guard.sh PreToolUse hook blocks Edit/Write to .kudos/** (exit 2); jq-free parse_json_field; registered via onboarding/architect-foundation
SC-E1-6: commit-validate.sh integrated into COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md before commit gate; creates .kudos/ on first run; fails-open (any detection error skips with log, never aborts commit)
SC-E1-7: Session identity UUID written to .kudos/session-id at worktree creation; commit-validate.sh reads from file (fails-open with fresh UUID if absent)
SC-E1-8: Contributor rank displayed per commit: Contributor (0-25), Consistent (26-75), Distinguished (76-150), Exemplary (151-300), Principal Contributor (301+)
SC-E1-9: CLAUDE.md Kudos section: overview, prohibition block (listed before rewards), jitter disclosure (+/-20% random), Goodhart's Law disclosure, rank table

SC-E1-10: diff-to-sg-scope.sh wrapper: command -v sg pre-check (exit 2 if absent); checks HEAD~1 existence (exit 2 if first commit); git diff --name-only HEAD~1; sg run --pattern

--json=stream per file; parses NDJSON
SC-E1-11: Spike S0 validates sg --json=stream exit code (0=no matches, 1=matches) and NDJSON schema before T5/T11 implementation

SC-E1-12: Spike S1 implements/tests Python AST subtree hashing prototype (hashlib.sha256(ast.dump(node).encode())); measures false-positive rate; confirms jscpd file-output integration (cat $OUTPUT_DIR/jscpd-report.json, not stdout) if selected as fallback
SC-E1-T3: reviewer-findings.json shows dimension score=5; one award per dimension per diff_hash
SC-E1-T5: diff-to-sg-scope.sh detects function extracted to helper in staged Python files; grep fallback when sg absent
SC-E1-T6: commit message references bug ticket ID; dso ticket show confirms type=bug AND created_at predates git merge-base HEAD main
SC-E1-T7: staged Python file has >=4 control-flow nesting levels (if/for/while/with/try); depth via ast.NodeVisitor with counter (visit_If/For/While/With/Try increment, generic_visit decrement)
SC-E1-T9: all staged Python files pass: git show ":$f" | ruff check --stdin-filename "$(pwd)/$f" - (staged blob, absolute path fixes ruff #17405 config-discovery bug)
SC-E1-T11: diff-to-sg-scope.sh detects pass-through method removal; grep fallback when sg absent
SC-E1-T12: staged diff removes commented-out code blocks
SC-E1-T13: staged Python files show >=3 structurally identical AST subtrees removed (hashlib.sha256(ast.dump(node).encode()) fingerprinting; algorithm/threshold from Spike S1)
SC-E1-T14: .review-events/ JSONL shows important/critical findings event followed by resubmission event in same session
SC-E1-T15: .review-events/ JSONL shows blocked_by_test_gate:true commit followed by passing commit in same session; disqualified if only changes are .test-index RED marker lines (^\[.*\]$)
SC-E1-23: Integration test seeds synthetic T9-qualifying commit, runs commit-validate.sh, asserts ledger contains T9 entry with points>0 AND stdout contains per-trigger breakdown
RESEARCH FINDINGS:

- External integration (sg/ast-grep): --json=stream NDJSON confirmed; command -v sg is correct absence-detection method (not exit code); duplicate block detection infeasible via sg (Python AST subtree hashing is the correct approach)

- Novel pattern (PRM): 2025 research confirms step-level recognition reduces reasoning errors; immediate reward delivery critical for behavioral linkage; design aligns with AgentPRM and PRIME findings
SCENARIO ANALYSIS:
- diff-to-sg-scope.sh uses HEAD~1 diff during git commit --amend (medium, runtime): stale file set causes false T5/T7/T13 awards; implementation must detect amend context
- T14 races with concurrent reviewer JSONL write (medium, runtime): partial JSONL line causes parse error; handle gracefully
- kudos-write-guard.sh not registered after fresh clone (critical, deployment): hooks require onboarding re-run
- .kudos/ absent from .gitignore (high, deployment): commit-validate.sh must add .kudos/ to .gitignore on first run
- Missing kudos.session_ceiling key causes crash (high, configuration): validate/default at startup
- sg absent in CI silently voids sg-dependent triggers (medium, deployment): document or accept skip as designed
COORDINATION: Soft coordination with 1083-fb3d (local workflow simplification) for hook registration ordering.

DEPENDENCIES: This epic blocks all downstream kudos epics (01f5-28c1 Polyglot Triggers, 16df-b0a2 User-awarded points, 71df-5bd8 detection triggers and agent behavioral improvements) — infrastructure and primary triggers must ship first.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (sg/ast-grep CLI), novel pattern (process-reward modeling / PRM)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 6
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: triggered — cycles: 1, gap: AST subtree hashing false-positive rate unvalidated (resolved via Spike S1 in walking skeleton)
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-commit, per-session ledger; not volume-sensitive
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The 3e9b sprint exercises the kudos system on its own commits before sprint close. At least one commit during the 3e9b sprint produces a kudos ledger entry; the kudos-write-guard hook is exercised end-to-end (block path + allow path); the commit-validate.sh integration produces a kudos-aware commit message annotation on at least one sprint commit.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `test -f .kudos/ledger.jsonl && wc -l < .kudos/ledger.jsonl` returns ≥1 entry whose timestamp falls within the 3e9b sprint window.
- The git log of the sprint shows at least one commit whose message contains the kudos annotation pattern (per the spec's COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md integration).
- Synthetic test of the kudos-write-guard PreToolUse hook: an attempted bypass (e.g., direct write to .kudos/ outside the wrapper) is blocked AND the allow path (wrapper-invoked write) succeeds.
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `.kudos/session-id` (per-worktree file) | Worktree creation hook (per SC-E1-7) | Stable per worktree | commit-validate.sh (per SC-E1-6); session-bound kudos attribution | **Cleared on worktree teardown** — `/dso:end-session` removes `.kudos/session-id` as part of the worktree cleanup step; cascade-removed when the worktree directory itself is deleted by `claude-safe` cleanup. Closes the audit's RETIRE gap. |

| `.kudos/ledger.jsonl` | Created on first kudos trigger fire in a session | Append-only per kudos event | Retro aggregation; calibration-report.sh feeds; commit-validate.sh display | Persistent within the worktree; archived/removed with the worktree |

| `kudos.session_ceiling` (dso-config.conf, default value documented) | `/dso:onboarding` writes default at project setup | Operator edit | kudos-write-guard.sh enforcement | N/A — persistent config |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `test -f .kudos/session-id` returns 0 in the sprint worktree.
- After `/dso:end-session` simulation against a test worktree: the .kudos/session-id is absent from the cleaned-up worktree.

content.text: ## Incident Overview
design-md-lint.sh only operates on git diff --cached staged files. When called
with a positional file path argument, it ignores it and emits "No staged files"
exit 0. The fixture test harness (test-design-md-fixtures.sh) calls the linter
with file paths, expecting meaningful exit codes based on violation detection.
Expected: design-md-lint.sh accepts a file path and lints it directly.
Actual: design-md-lint.sh ignores the path, checks staged files, exits 0.
Resolution: Add a DSO_LINT_FILE env var or positional-arg mode to design-md-lint.sh
that accepts a single file path and calls npx directly against it.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Author behavioral test suite covering: (1) conditional load per-skill — non-Strata zero Reads; brainstorm Phase 1 Step 1 reads concepts + brainstorm-guidance ≤80 lines; on-demand decomposition.md when STRATA_UNCERTAINTY fires; preplanning tag-scoped Reads; implementation-plan tag inheritance via story→epic chain; strata.skip=true blocks all SDK Reads; STRATA_SKIP env var inherited by sub-agents; STRATA_SKIP absent treated as false (fail-open). (2) Brainstorm tag set/unset across canonical inputs ("intake form for SNAP applicants" yes; "deployment pipeline for Strata project" no); UX disclosure printed; correction path documented; ≤80 line cap at Phase 1 Step 1; read-after-write fence (preplanning's first action verifies tag with retry + named error). (3) Plan-validation: bad-fixture plan with 4 footguns produces ≥4 findings citing decomposition.md rules; non-Strata epic produces byte-identical scrutiny output (diff against tests/fixtures/scrutiny-non-strata-baseline.txt exits 0). (4) Parallel reviewers shared facts load (no duplicate Read in tool-use logs). (5) Regeneration round-trip + manual-residual-index.json integrity. (6) Implementation-plan task output references SDK generator commands with hyphenated flags. Plus pre-sprint-gate behavioral test at tests/scripts/test-b-pre-sprint-gate.sh against fixture with/without spike artifact.
**Why**: 5 behavioral guarantees + 6 SCs need observable failure modes; RED tests are the contract.
**Scope**:
- IN: All test scripts, fixture directories, golden-master facts files, scrutiny-non-strata-baseline.txt, bad-fixture with 4 SDK footguns, pre-sprint gate test.
- OUT: Implementation of regeneration tool, per-skill loads, plan-validation extension (separate stories).
## Done Definitions

content.text: ## PR Size Limits as Proactive Guidance

Activate sets a clear 400-line PR size guideline. DSO's review workflow has 300/600 line thresholds for model escalation/rejection, but doesn't guide PR sizing proactively. PR size is only surfaced reactively at review time — by then the work is already done and splitting is costly.
Surface PR size guidance earlier in the workflow — during implementation planning, not just at review time:
- Implementation-plan should estimate diff size per task and flag tasks likely to exceed the 300-line threshold
- Tasks exceeding the estimate should be split proactively during planning, not at review time
- Preplanning should consider PR size when slicing stories — vertical slices should produce reviewable PRs
- Sprint batching should be aware of cumulative diff size per commit/PR
- The 300/600 line thresholds from the review workflow should be referenced as planning constraints, not just review triggers

content.text: ## Context

The first attempt at replacing the edge-triggered Jira bridges (epic 3a03-b3f2-b34c-4e4f, now superseded) shipped the operational infrastructure successfully: legacy bridge YAMLs deleted from main, reconcile-bridge.yml workflow plus heartbeat canary plus weekly fsck audit live, ACLI integration hardened with 36 contract tests verifying 21 of 22 invocation patterns against authoritative Atlassian docs. Pass-1 live verification against the live DIG Jira project then surfaced an architectural defect: the snapshot-diff differ emitted create mutations without a direction marker, and the applier dispatched every create to client.create_issue() — creating duplicate Jira issues instead of mirroring unmapped Jira issues down as local jira-* tickets. The defect was compounded by bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json writes being lost between GHA runs because the workflow only committed the tickets-tracker dir, so every pass started with an empty prior-snapshot and emitted create for every Jira issue. Five duplicate Jira issues were created before the pass was halted; the JQL-label dedup short-circuit prevented approximately 1,820 more.
EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

This epic delivers the redesigned reconciler: derivable rather than snapshot-diff, with direction-tagged mutations that make the inversion bug structurally impossible at the type level. The design absorbed empirical findings from a live spike against current DIG state (direction safety operator gate PASSED; 197 stale-label bridge orphans identified as residue of the prior failed pass), a focused pre-mortem dispatch (found a real next-class defect — dedup-JQL fossilization of failed-rollback orphans — and proposed a 3-layer fix that is folded into this design), an architectural probe spec at docs/integration-harness-jira-reconciler-derivable.md, and a 84-ticket cruft cleanup of local state (4 telemetry bugs plus 80 PR-comment-deferred placeholders) that brought the day-one bootstrap working set to approximately 931 mutations across 388 outbound creates plus 346 inbound creates plus 197 inbound label-strips. Local state after that cleanup is accepted as source of truth for what Jira should mirror after migration.

Operator-trust signals are preserved from the prior epic: every reconciler pass produces either zero anomalies or an actionable bug ticket per anomaly class. Project maintainers and future DSO operators on Jira-mirrored projects need this convergent sync as platform-level infrastructure (currently single-project usage).
## Approach

Derivable reconciler topology. Single pass orchestrator (reconcile.py) loads local state via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list` (index, no per-ticket replay) and Jira state via scoped ACLI search, then calls a pure differ that returns a flat list of direction-tagged mutations, then dispatches via a narrow applier matrix. Stateless: two passes on identical (local, jira) inputs produce byte-identical mutation lists. No bridge_state/ persistence. No mapping.json source-of-truth.

Differ contract (differ.py). compute_mutations(local_state, jira_state) returns list[Mutation]. Each Mutation carries direction (inbound | outbound) and action (create | update | delete | probe | clean_label | repair_property). Direction is computed from source:

- Jira issue with no dso-id label and no matching dso_local_id entity property: (inbound, create) — mirror down as jira-<key> local ticket with all fields mapped from Jira plus the audit tag imported:reconciler-bootstrap
- Local ticket with no jira-* prefix and no Jira twin claiming its identity: (outbound, create) — push to Jira with mandatory dual identity write (label plus entity property)
- Both sides exist with field divergence: conflict_resolver chooses direction; local-wins on scalars produces outbound, additive merge on collections produces inbound
- Both sides exist with one side closed: close propagates per local-wins to outbound_delete (Jira close, not hard delete)

- Jira issue carries dso-id:<L> label but local has no ticket with id L AND no current jira-* mirror references the Jira key: (inbound, clean_label) — strip stale dso-id label; next pass mirrors normally as fresh jira-<key>. Addresses the 197 visible bridge orphans, residue of the prior failed reconciler pass.

- Jira issue carries dso-id:<L> label matching an active local L but is missing the dso_local_id entity property: (inbound, repair_property) — retry-wrapped REST PUT to complete the dual identity write. On retry exhaustion, file label-only-orphan-quarantine bug and suspend the outbound for L until human review. Addresses the pre-mortem's identified dedup-JQL fossilization bug class.

- Previously mapped local jira-* whose Jira twin is absent from JQL working set: (inbound, probe) — per-issue REST GET disambiguates the 4-way fork: hard-delete, redirect (issue moved to another project, key changed), out-of-window (closed and aged out), or trash (recoverable). On hard-delete, the local content is preserved and a fresh outbound create produces a new Jira issue with a newly-minted dso-id; local renames from jira-dig-XXXX to jira-dig-YYYY (new key). Probe runs even in dry-run mode (read-only REST calls).

Applier dispatch (applier.py). Narrow function per (direction, action) pair: inbound_create, inbound_update, inbound_delete, inbound_clean_label, inbound_repair_property, inbound_probe, outbound_create, outbound_update, outbound_delete. Each leaf accepts only matching-direction mutations and raises DirectionMismatchError on wrong-direction input — turns the prior inversion bug into a type error at unit-test time. Each leaf <= 50 LOC, independently testable.

Outbound updates apply status via a local_to_jira_status mapping config. Missing-entry behavior: if a local status has no entry in the mapping table, the differ raises StatusMappingError and aborts the pass before any outbound write. Operator alert is filed naming the unmapped status; comment-fallback is reserved exclusively for the case where a mapped target status is illegal in the Jira workflow scheme — preventing the comment channel from becoming a silent sink for stale-mapping noise. On 400-from-illegal-transition (the workflow scheme rejects the mapped target state), the applier emits a Jira comment ("local status changed to X") instead of retrying. Convergent OSS pattern from espressif and canonical gh-jira-sync-bot prior art.

JQL dedup at differ time requires both identifiers: label dso-id:<L> AND entity property dso_local_id=<L> must both be present and matching for a Jira issue to count as the canonical mapping target for local L. Label-only matches trigger (inbound, repair_property) or (inbound, clean_label), never silent binding. The rollback path in outbound_create wraps client.delete_issue in _call_with_retry (same budget, same backoff as the create itself) so transient API failures cannot convert a partial identity write into permanent corruption.

Fetcher scoping (fetcher.py). JQL: project = DIG AND (resolution = Unresolved OR updated >= -1h). Closed-on-both-sides issues exit the working set entirely; reopens are caught by the 1-hour grace window (grace > 20-min cron cadence). Pagination uses startAt offset (safe at the ~2k-issue working-set ceiling; never deprecated for low totals; avoids documented nextPageToken data-loss bugs JRACLOUD-94632 and Atlassian community thread #3066609). Fallback detector: if startAt is removed in a future ACLI version, same-nextPageToken-twice triggers abort-and-alert. Silent-truncation detector: Jira Cloud has an undocumented hard ceiling of 1000 results for JQL search; if a page returns exactly 1000 results AND ACLI's total-or-isLast indicator does not strictly confirm 'less than 1000 total in working set', the fetcher aborts the pass with a BRIDGE_ALERT jql-result-truncation-suspected. This prevents the differ from treating a silently-truncated set as authoritative. The --fields parameter excludes `resolution` and `updated` (ACLI rejects these); both are used in the JQL clause only.

Invariants (invariants.py). Preserves check_at_most_one_dso_local_id. Adds check_dual_identity_complete: for every issue with a dso-id label, verify the dso_local_id entity property is present and matches; for every issue with a dso_local_id property, verify the dso-id label is present and matches. Disagreement auto-files a bug ticket via the existing anomaly path (cap 5/pass + 24h dedup). Catches Jira admin renames and partial identity writes before they cascade.

Concurrency contract. reconcile-bridge.yml uses GHA concurrency group { group: reconcile-bridge, cancel-in-progress: false } to prevent overlapping passes from GHA cron. The orchestrator additionally checks for an in-flight tickets-branch advisory lock (.reconciler-pass-lock committed at pass start, removed at pass end) before dispatching the differ. If a concurrent pass is detected, the new pass exits cleanly with a manifest entry concurrent-pass-deferred and no mutations applied. This closes the operator+cron race in Phase 3 and the two-operator race in Phase 1-2.

Rollout machinery (reconcile.py). Mode flag (dry-run | bootstrap-strict | bootstrap-throttle | live) sourced from workflow_dispatch input per invocation (no persistent state). Strict allow-list validation at orchestrator entry: the mode string is compared case-sensitively against the 4 canonical values; any other value (typo, mixed-case, missing input, leading/trailing whitespace) raises ModeValidationError before any fetcher call. Operator alert is filed and the pass aborts. No silent default fallback to live. Phase advancement is gated by a tickets-branch advisory lockfile .reconciler-phase-gate whose contents declare the maximum-allowed mode for the next pass. After each pass completes, the operator updates and commits the lockfile (e.g., bootstrap-strict to bootstrap-throttle) explicitly. The orchestrator at pass entry reads the lockfile and rejects any mode greater than the lockfile-declared ceiling — converting informal operator review into a checked-into-git approval gate. Scheduled cron stays disabled through dry-run, bootstrap-strict, bootstrap-throttle phases; re-enabled at first live invocation. Phased mutation cap:
- Phase 0 (dry-run): 1 pass; cap=0 (manifest only, zero writes). All inbound_probe REST GET calls execute (read-only). Operator reviews full manifest before approving Phase 1.

- Phase 1 (bootstrap-strict): 5 passes at cap=10 mutations/pass. Asymmetric manifest each pass (outbound totals; inbound details with full field manifest; alerts with full detail). Operator reviews each pass before approving the next. Bounded blast radius: max 10 ticket-class damage per pass; 50-ticket cumulative sample is enough to detect class-level defects with manageable rollback cost.

- Phase 2 (bootstrap-throttle): 3 passes at cap=100 mutations/pass. Asymmetric manifest plus per-pass spot-check of 10% of mutations. Cumulative 350 tickets processed by end of Phase 2 — meaningful statistical confidence that no class-level defect has surfaced.
- Phase 3 (live-uncapped): scheduled cron resumes. Manifest logs to GHA workflow log only. Operator alerted only via anomaly bug tickets (cap 5/pass + 24h dedup).

Cap-overflow behavior: when derived mutation count exceeds cap, apply mutations up to cap in deterministic order (sorted by tuple (direction, action, jira_key or local_id)) then log deferred mutations to manifest. Next pass re-derives from current state (stateless), so the deferred set may shift if underlying state changed between passes — operator review of the deferred-list delta is the trust signal that progress is real. Convergence may take more passes when churn is high.

Asymmetric manifest renderer: during dry-run plus bootstrap-strict, outbound emits totals (counts of creates/updates/deletes); inbound emits per-ticket detail (full field manifest so erroneous Jira data is catchable). During bootstrap-throttle, both directions emit summary plus operator-spot-check sample. During live, GHA workflow log only; operator attention only via anomaly path.

Conflict policy (preserved). Local wins on state (status, assignee, priority, type, title, description, deletions). Additive merge inbound for set-valued fields (comments, watchers, labels, links) with per-element provenance (origin: local | jira). Attachments explicitly out of scope (no-op in inbound_create and outbound_create).

Identity model (preserved, verified at ACLI layer). Every outbound_create writes both label dso-id:<uuid> and entity property dso_local_id with mandatory-or-alert discipline. Search-by-identity uses label JQL as primary; per-issue REST property read is confirmation/audit. JQL on entity properties is not supported on Jira Cloud (verified during prior epic).

Modules deleted by this epic: bootstrap.py, orphan_band.py, duplicates_band.py, stale_band.py, open_count_skew_band.py (banded-bootstrap construct retired; derivable design treats every pass identically). All bridge_state/ write paths removed. All mapping.json write paths removed; reads removed.

Modules preserved: conflict_resolver.py (still applies), alert_store.py (BRIDGE_ALERT sink), health.py (per-pass health record), capability_check.py, _concurrency.py, _attestation.py. ACLI layer unchanged (36 contract tests plus 4 bug fixes shipped on main from prior epic).

Out of scope. Attachment sync (binary handling, documented as explicit no-op). Project-key reuse handling (single-project usage; not relevant until DIG is renamed or recreated). Webhook fan-in (pull-only design avoids webhook-ordering footguns).
## Success Criteria

1. Direction safety: zero new duplicate Jira issues created across all reconciler passes in this epic. Verify by ACLI JQL `project = DIG AND labels NOT LIKE "dso-id-*" AND status != Closed AND created >= <epic-start-ts>` cross-referenced against `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --status=open` filtered to jira-* IDs; assert zero mismatches.

2. Stateless convergence: 2 consecutive workflow_dispatch runs on unchanged (local, Jira) state produce byte-identical mutation manifests under canonical serialization. Manifest serialization MUST use json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2) with mutation list pre-sorted by tuple (direction, action, jira_key or local_id) and per-mutation field dicts also sorted by key. Byte-equality is asserted on this canonical form, not arbitrary Python dict-insertion-order output. Verify by triggering reconcile-bridge.yml twice back-to-back on converged state; diff the manifests; assert mutation list identical and byte-equal.

3. Pagination stability: pass against a working set with simulated mid-fetch update emits exactly one mutation per affected issue. Verify by inserting a marker update on a throwaway DIG issue immediately after pass-start; assert manifest contains exactly one mutation referencing that issue.

4. Disappeared-from-Jira fork: for each of {hard-delete, trash-and-restore, project-move, out-of-window}, the appropriate branch fires with correct outcome. Verify by per-branch throwaway-issue test executing the disambiguation; assert correct behavior per branch (hard-delete creates new Jira with fresh dso-id; redirect updates local mapping to new key; trash-and-restore no-op; out-of-window silent exclusion).

5. Status-taxonomy fallback: workflow-illegal local-to-Jira status push produces a Jira comment, not a 400 retry storm. Verify by picking a Jira issue in a status from which `Done` is illegal in the workflow scheme; trigger a local status change to a state that maps to `Done`; assert the next reconciler pass emits a Jira comment containing `local status changed to <X>` and zero update_issue 400 errors in pass health record.

6. Schema-drift anomaly: removing dso_local_id property from a managed Jira issue triggers check_dual_identity_complete to file a bug ticket within the same pass. Verify by REST-DELETE the property on a throwaway managed DIG issue; trigger workflow_dispatch; assert bug ticket appears within the same pass tagged with appropriate dedup_key.

7. Dedup-fossilization defense: a label-only orphan (Jira issue with dso-id label but missing dso_local_id property) claiming an active local id does NOT bind via JQL dedup; the differ emits (inbound, repair_property) on first encounter and quarantines if repair fails. Verify by manually constructing the failure state (write dso-id label without entity property to a throwaway DIG issue claiming an active local id); assert the next pass emits inbound_repair_property and that the local outbound for that id is suspended pending property write success or operator intervention.

8. Stale-label cleanup: the 197 bridge orphans visible at epic start (Jira issues with dso-id labels pointing to nonexistent local ids) resolve via inbound_clean_label across the first 5 capped passes. Verify by capturing bridge-fsck label-only-orphan count BEFORE Phase 1 and AFTER Phase 2 completes; assert count drops to 0.

9. Synthetic drift heals: existing tests/drift_injection/inject-and-heal.sh against live DIG with all 3 modes (orphan, mislabel, missing-prop) — each mode heals within 1 pass and bridge-fsck exits 0. Verify by harness returns exit 0 for all 3 modes in sequence with no operator intervention.

10. Steady-state convergence: 5 consecutive workflow_dispatch runs in Phase 3 (live-uncapped) on converged state exit 0 with <= 5 mutations per pass. Verify after anomaly heal SCs pass; run 5 sequential workflow_dispatch in mode=live; assert each run's mutation_count <= 5 and exit code 0.

11. Per-element-class round-trip idempotency, LIVE VERIFIED. For each syncable data element class — scalar (title, description, status, priority, type, assignee) and collection-with-provenance (comments, labels excluding dso-id, watchers, links) — exercise the create/edit/delete path bidirectionally and assert exactly-one application per pass with zero duplicate generation across 3 consecutive passes after the initial sync. Test matrix (executable in-session against throwaway DIG issues + local tickets): (a) inbound-comment-create: add a Jira comment; pass 1 mirrors into local; passes 2-3 emit zero mutations referencing that comment. (b) outbound-comment-create: add a local comment; pass 1 mirrors to Jira; passes 2-3 emit zero mutations. (c) comment-edit bidirectional: edit on each side; verify local-wins behavior plus zero re-application. (d) comment-delete: bidirectional, verify provenance-aware behavior (Jira-origin element removal does not auto-propagate to local; local-origin removal propagates). (e) label-create/edit/delete bidirectional (excluding the reconciler-owned dso-id label). (f) link-create/edit/delete bidirectional. Assert across 3 consecutive passes after any single element operation, the manifest mutation count for that element class is exactly 1 then 0 then 0.

12. No-duplicate-element invariant across full bootstrap, LIVE VERIFIED. After Phase 1 plus Phase 2 completion (350 cumulative tickets processed), for every synced ticket pair (local id and its mapped Jira key) assert: comments_in_jira count == comments_in_local count; labels_in_jira count (excluding dso-id) == labels_in_local count; links_in_jira count == links_in_local count. Any mismatch indicates duplicate generation by the differ. Verify by bulk readout across the post-Phase-2 mapped set; assert zero count mismatches.
## Scenario Analysis

The canonical scrutiny pipeline (Red Team plus Blue Team) surfaced 22 surviving failure scenarios after filtering. Critical and several high-severity scenarios are addressed by inline spec amendments above; the remaining are documented here as accepted risks with mitigation notes.
Addressed by inline amendments above:
- Concurrent workflow_dispatch race (critical) — concurrency contract (GHA group + advisory lockfile)
- ACLI 1000-result silent truncation (critical) — silent-truncation detector in fetcher
- RECONCILER_MODE input validation gap (critical) — strict allow-list validation at orchestrator entry
- Bootstrap module deletion breaks remaining imports (high) — no-remaining-imports closure check
- local_to_jira_status missing-entry silently falls through (high) — StatusMappingError on missing entry
- Byte-identical mutation lists across passes (high) — canonical serialization spec in SC2
- Phase boundary approval is informal (high) — .reconciler-phase-gate lockfile
Accepted risks with documented mitigation:

- Pagination drift under steady DIG churn (runtime, high): Issues updated during pagination can shift between pages, causing duplicate or omitted mutations. Mitigation: the anomaly path catches the persistent corruption signature; oscillating mutations across passes are visible in per-pass manifest diff at SC2 verification time.

- Local state read non-atomic w.r.t. in-flight ticket transitions (runtime, high): While a pass runs, parallel sessions may transition/create/close tickets. Mitigation: outbound write attempts include a pre-write recheck against the snapshot source state; mismatches abort the individual mutation with a local-state-changed-mid-pass alert; the next pass re-derives.

- Inbound probe REST GET storm during dry-run (runtime, high): Phase 0 dry-run runs inbound_probe REST GETs for every previously mapped jira-* whose twin is absent; could trigger Jira rate limits. Mitigation: cap inbound_probe at 50 REST GETs per pass during dry-run; deferred probes log to manifest with probe-deferred-rate-limit annotation; next pass picks up the remainder.

- Cap-overflow ordering — non-monotonic progress under churn (runtime, high): Deferred mutations re-derive each pass; underlying state changes can shift the deferred set. Mitigation: spec defines deterministic ordering (direction, action, jira_key or local_id) for cap-overflow; the deferred-list delta between passes is itself an operator-visible signal.

- GHA 6-hour timeout vs uncapped Phase 3 pass (runtime, high): A bulk Jira admin operation producing 100K issues in the updated-1h window could kill the pass mid-apply. Mitigation: reconcile.py emits a pass-duration alert if elapsed time exceeds 4 hours mid-apply; partial-write state is auto-detected by check_dual_identity_complete on the next pass.

- Phase 2 to 3 cron-enable race (deployment, high): If operator merges the cron-enable PR while a Phase 2 workflow_dispatch pass is still running, the next cron tick could fire mid-pass. Mitigation: the .reconciler-phase-gate lockfile means the cron tick reads the lockfile and refuses to advance past bootstrap-throttle until the operator commits the lockfile update to live.

- ACLI binary version drift local vs GHA runner (deployment, high): GHA runner may install a different ACLI version. Mitigation: reconcile-bridge.yml pins ACLI to a specific version via the install step; the 36 contract tests are tagged with the pinned version. Closure check verifies the pin is present in the workflow yml.

- JIRA_API_TOKEN rotation mid-rollout (deployment, high): Token rotation between passes invalidates auth and could leave partial identity writes. Mitigation: 401 response triggers fatal pass abort; operator alert escalates to P1 bug filing via the anomaly path; the rollback retry wrapper is bounded by the 200-call REST budget.

- Anomaly cap 5/pass + 24h dedup suppresses signal during outbreak (configuration, high): A 200-issue bulk anomaly burns the budget on the first 5; remaining silently suppressed. Mitigation: introduce a same-class-anomaly-burst-detected meta-alert that fires when a class hits the cap; this single meta-alert summarizes the burst rather than enumerating each.

- Atomic snapshot pair assumption (assumption, high): The differ assumes (local, jira_state) is read as a consistent pair, but Jira fetch is network-bound and slow. Mitigation: SC2 byte-identical verification is performed with both passes triggered back-to-back on enforced quiescence; the assumption is documented and the eventually-consistent failure mode is explicitly acceptable.

- Probe REST GET disappeared-key response pattern stability (assumption, high): Jira Cloud trash/redirect/404 semantics have changed historically. Mitigation: SC4 verification is re-runnable at any time against live Jira; if Atlassian changes trash semantics, the test catches the misclassification.

- Operator can rollback Phase 1 within hours (assumption, high): No explicit rollback playbook exists for Phase 1 damage. Mitigation: a dedicated rollback script plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/rollback-phase-1.sh is included as a Closure Check artifact; the script bulk-strips dso-id labels added during a specified time window and deletes any local jira-* tickets created within the same window.

- No Jira admin schema-level operations during rollout (assumption, medium): Bulk admin operations between passes could produce 100s of repair_property mutations exceeding cap=100 in Phase 2. Mitigation: operator policy — coordinate with Jira admin to defer schema-level operations during the rollout window. Documented in the runbook.

- Closed-on-both-sides reopens always touch updated field (assumption, medium): Rare Jira automation rules can flip status without touching updated. Mitigation: the weekly fsck audit (CC4, carried forward from 3a03) catches drift that escapes the 1-hour grace window.
## Closure Checks

mapping.json NOT present on tickets branch. Verify by `git ls-tree tickets bridge_state/mapping.json` returns nothing.

Verify by `git ls-tree origin/main plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/{bootstrap,orphan_band,duplicates_band,stale_band,open_count_skew_band}.py` returns no entries.

inbound_clean_label, inbound_repair_property, inbound_probe dispatch leaves present in applier.py with DirectionMismatchError guards. Unit tests confirm direction-mismatch raises.
Rollback delete_issue in outbound_create wrapped in _call_with_retry. Unit test confirms transient failure on rollback triggers retry then BRIDGE_ALERT (not silent corruption).

Rollout mode flag (workflow_dispatch input) honored by reconcile.py for dry-run / bootstrap-strict / bootstrap-throttle / live. Unit test confirms dry-run pass writes manifest with zero ACLI writes (mocked AcliClient assertion); bootstrap-strict pass aborts cleanly when mutation count exceeds cap=10 (deferred mutations recorded).

- Per-element provenance tracking present in conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES for set-valued fields (comments, labels, watchers, links). Verified live against a throwaway DIG issue plus its local mirror: add a comment via the Jira API; run pass 1 and confirm inbound_update produces exactly one mutation that adds the comment to the local mirror; run passes 2 and 3 and confirm zero mutations reference that comment. Repeat for labels, watchers, links. This is the load-bearing mechanism backing SC11 and SC12; the assertion is on live Jira plus live local tracker state, not on unit-test fixtures.

- Live bidirectional field-class disposition validation covers all 6 cases per (direction × action) combination for each FIELD_CLASS entry: scalar-divergence (local-wins), additive-collection-add (provenance-aware merge), additive-collection-remove (origin-aware: local-origin removal propagates outbound; Jira-origin removal stays local-preserved per the additive policy). Each case is exercised against a real throwaway DIG issue plus a real local ticket pair; the assertion is that the third consecutive pass on the converged state produces zero mutations for that field class. Live verification, not mocked. Test harness lives at tests/integration/test-derivable-bidirectional-field-classes.sh (new test file; pattern follows the existing 36-pattern ACLI contract harness at tests/scripts/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py).

This prevents the common failure mode where a single corrupt event crashes the entire ticket-show output. ## Existing Test File to Modify - `tests/scripts/test-ticket-show.sh` — add test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped ## .test-index RED marker required - `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-reducer.py: tests/scripts/test-ticket-show.sh [test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped]` ## Test Approach (Given/When/Then) **test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped:** - Given: a temp ticket dir with 2 PRECONDITIONS event files — one valid (parseable JSON) and one corrupt (truncated/invalid JSON) - When: `ticket-show.sh <ticket_id>` is run - Then: exit 0 (not a crash); stdout contains valid JSON with `preconditions_summary` from the 1 valid event; stderr contains a warning mentioning the corrupt file (not silent) ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped added to test-ticket-show.sh   Verify: grep -q "test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped" tests/scripts/test-ticket-show.sh - [ ] Test passes after T4 implementation   Verify: bash tests/scripts/test-ticket-show.sh test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped - [ ] .test-index updated with RED marker   Verify: grep -q '\[test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped\]' $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.test-index - [ ] ticket-show exits 0 on corrupt PRECONDITIONS (no crash)   Verify: bash tests/scripts/test-ticket-show.sh test_ticket_show_preconditions_corrupt_file_skipped 2>&1 | grep -v "^FAIL" ## Retry Budget MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model) On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages) On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately
