The same class of bug recurs. Test-writing sub-agents (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution, fix-bug RED-phase) operate against static guidance (behavioral-testing-standard.md) that doesn't grow from observed misses. This epic delivers a closed-loop feedback system: closed bugs with extractable lessons get `NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE:` JSON comments + `negative-example` tag during /dso:fix-bug Phase G; test-writing sub-agents consume retrieved examples via `negative-examples-lookup.sh` at task start; recurring patterns graduate to universal rules in `behavioral-testing-standard.md` via /dso:retro Graduation Phase with human approval. After this epic ships, test-writing agents see project-specific "Lessons from past bugs" alongside the universal 7-rule standard — where today they see only the standard.

Users affected: DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, test-writing sub-agents (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution, fix-bug RED-phase), code-reviewer-test-quality, completion-verifier, and downstream calibration consumers (411b-a047 mutation infrastructure, 7f42-e41f growth metrics, fb3e-b01b deeper signals).
## Success Criteria

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/negative-example-comment.md published. NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment schema: {schema_version=1, bug_type_slug (string; from 4911-c7ba taxonomy), intent_ids_if_applicable (array of intent_ids from 94ed manifest entries; values MUST reference real manifest entries OR be empty), missed_signal_summary (describes what FAILED to be detected — canonical example in contract showing correct polarity), what_test_would_have_caught_it, generalizable_lesson, related_files (array of paths), scope_claim ("this pattern applies to any agent that..."), falsification ("this would NOT apply when...")}. Contract document includes prompt-engineering guidance for sonnet extraction to avoid inverted-polarity drafts AND a consistent style guide for opus drafting graduation rules (matching the existing 7-rule standard's structure).

SC2: /dso:fix-bug Phase G extended. EXECUTES AFTER 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step (explicit ordering — Phase G runs after 4911 sets bug_type_<slug> tag). When a bug ticket is closed with reason="Fixed: ...":
(i) sonnet sub-agent evaluates extraction conditions: bug not caught by an existing test AND pattern generalizable;

(ii) MANDATORY pre-extraction redaction step: sonnet identifies and redacts credentials, tokens, keys, PII, customer/user identifiers, internal-only IDs from all string fields. If sonnet cannot confidently redact, MUST skip extraction;
(iii) output MUST include scope_claim AND falsification fields per SC1; if either is vacuous ("when the code is correct", "always applies"), skip extraction;
(iv) atomic write: NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag applied as single unit (rollback if either fails);
(v) when 4911 classification failed (bug_type_<slug> not set on the ticket), use bug_type_slug="unclassified" and add `retro-needs-classification` tag;
(vi) SKIP_RECORD comment logged on every skip with {decision: "skip", skip_reason: <one sentence>} for audit trail;
(vii) intent_ids_if_applicable values validated at write time against 94ed manifest entries; invalid intent_ids cause write to fail OR values dropped with warning.
SC3: plugins/dso/scripts/negative-examples-lookup.sh <task-id-or-args> implements retrieval:
(a) reads task's file_impact + claimable_intent from ticket data;
(b) queries via existing ticket-CLI primitives: `ticket list --type=bug --status=closed --has-tag=negative-example --has-tag=bug-type-<slug>`;
(c) excludes tickets with any `promoted-to-standard:*` tag;
(d) excludes stale examples: tickets whose related_files reference paths not present on disk (auto-staleness check);

(e) relevance ranking: narrower-scoped bugs (smaller related_files set) preferred, weight by recency. When two examples have identical relevance scores, deterministic tie-breaking via ticket-id lexical order;
(f) returns top-N=3 most relevant matches as JSON;
(g) output includes excluded_count field (signal for /dso:retro Graduation Phase when count is high);
(h) summary format per match: {slug, missed_signal_summary, generalizable_lesson} (concise, not full schema);
(i) ARG_MAX-safe via --output-file flag.

SC4: Three test-writing sub-agent prompts updated to invoke `negative-examples-lookup.sh` at task-start: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Retrieved examples are injected with explicit label "## Project-specific learned patterns (advisory; not universal Rule 1-7+ authority)" so the agent distinguishes project-specific learned guidance from universal Rule 1-7 standards. Cap at 3 examples per task. When 0 examples returned (e.g., cold-start), section omitted entirely (no empty block, no error).

SC5: /dso:retro extended with a Graduation Phase. Opus sub-agent reads all bugs with `negative-example` tag AND without `promoted-to-standard:*` tag via single CLI query. Identifies graduation candidates via two trigger paths:

(a) Frequency floor: ≥3 examples sharing the same bug_type_slug AND distinct root-cause fingerprints. Opus MUST verify <80% missed_signal_summary similarity across the group; groups whose examples are >=80% similar are collapsed as a single signal (treats as 1 example, not N).

(b) Cross-slug semantic match: opus identifies a pattern via SINGLE FALSIFIABLE PREDICATE naming a specific testable condition (e.g., "all four miss the case where X is empty"). Theme-level labels (e.g., "all four are about validation") are NOT permitted — predicate must name a specific input state or code path AND an expected observable outcome.
Each candidate is surfaced with:
(1) 4-field draft rule matching the existing behavioral-testing-standard.md structure: {rule_statement, rationale, anti_pattern_example, correct_pattern_example};
(2) evidence_citations: ≥3 bug IDs with quoted missed_signal_summary from each;
(3) explicit provenance ("3 same-slug bugs" OR "opus cross-slug semantic match across N examples").

PRE-DRAFT VALIDATION: opus MUST check existing rules in behavioral-testing-standard.md; if proposed rule overlaps an existing rule, opus either revises to propose modification to existing rule OR justifies distinct coverage. Block surfacing if conflict is unresolved.

SYCOPHANCY GATE: on user acceptance, before PR is drafted, user must answer challenge: "Where does this rule add distinct coverage beyond existing Rules 1-N?" An empty answer OR an answer that restates the rule blocks the PR and marks the candidate as `challenged-rejected`.

SC6: Atomic graduation: on accepted candidate, PR is drafted FIRST (contains the standard amendment); contributing bug tickets get `promoted-to-standard:<rule-id>` tag ONLY after PR creation succeeds. If PR draft fails, no tags are applied — prevents phantom graduation records.

SC7: behavioral-testing-standard.md remains designated a safeguard file per a03c-d55e's SC2 / CLAUDE.md rule 22. /dso:retro Graduation Phase MUST surface candidates and draft rule text but MUST NOT auto-commit. Human approval to merge the PR remains required.

SC8: Lifecycle hook — status transition closed→open on a tagged bug automatically removes the negative-example tag (sentry on the ticket-transition hook). Verified by SC9(i) fixture: reopening a tagged bug removes the tag and the bug is excluded from subsequent lookup results.
SC9: Synthetic end-to-end test covering twelve scenarios:
(a) EXTRACTION + atomic write + audit trail: fixture bug with test-miss + generalizable pattern produces NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag atomically.
(b) SKIP recorded: fixture bug where extraction conditions not met → SKIP_RECORD comment with decision and reason.
(c) PRIVACY redaction: fixture bug with token/credential in description → redaction confirmed in NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment OR extraction skipped.
(d) LOOKUP with stale-example exclusion: fixture bug whose related_files references a deleted path → excluded from lookup output.

(e) FREQUENCY graduation: 3 fixture bugs sharing bug_type_slug=X with distinct root-cause fingerprints → /dso:retro Graduation surfaces candidate with provenance "3 same-slug bugs"; user accepts; PR draft + promoted-to-standard:<rule-id> tagging.
(f) FREQUENCY COLLAPSE: 3 fixture bugs sharing bug_type_slug with >=80% missed_signal_summary similarity → collapsed as 1 signal, no candidate surfaced.

(g) CROSS-SLUG predicate graduation: 4 fixture bugs across 2 slugs sharing a falsifiable predicate ("all four miss the case where input array is empty") → candidate surfaced with provenance "opus cross-slug semantic match across 4 examples".
(h) THEME-only rejection: 4 fixture bugs share a theme ("all about validation") without a specific predicate → NOT surfaced.

(i) SYCOPHANCY challenge blocks empty response: user accepts candidate, then enters empty answer to "where does this rule add distinct coverage?" → PR is blocked, candidate marked challenged-rejected.

(j) COLD_START / EMPTY_CORPUS: fixture task in a project with zero closed bugs tagged negative-example → lookup returns empty result with excluded_count=0; test-writer prompt omits "Lessons from past bugs" section entirely (no error, no hang).
(k) RANKING_TIE: 2 fixture examples with identical relevance scores → lookup returns them in deterministic ticket-id lexical order.

(l) OPERATIONAL METRIC EMISSION: /dso:retro Graduation Phase emits structured telemetry to a RETRO_TELEMETRY: ticket comment OR a retro-telemetry-<timestamp>.json artifact with fields {examples_extracted_since_last_retro, examples_skipped_count, graduation_candidates_surfaced, candidates_accepted, sycophancy_rejections, candidates_rejected_predicate, candidates_rejected_frequency_collapse}.
## Approach
Four sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2 (recording with redaction, atomicity, audit trail, intent_ids validation).
- Phase 2: SC3 (lookup helper with relevance + staleness + tie-breaking) + SC4 (test-writer prompt integration).
- Phase 3: SC5 + SC6 + SC7 (graduation with predicate/distinct-root validation + sycophancy gate + atomic PR-first + safeguard preservation).
- Phase 4: SC8 + SC9 (lifecycle hooks + twelve-scenario end-to-end synthetic test).
## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Sonnet over-extraction (high/extraction-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(i) generalizability check + SC2(iii) scope_claim/falsification requirement + SC2(vi) audit trail; residual is sonnet's self-assessment quality.
- Sonnet under-extraction (high/extraction-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(vi) SKIP_RECORD audit trail; residual is silent signal loss; /dso:retro can surface high-skip-rate trends.

- Cross-slug opus over-clustering (high/promotion-integrity): partially mitigated by SC5(b) single-falsifiable-predicate constraint + SYCOPHANCY gate + PRE-DRAFT conflict check; residual is opus's self-assessment of predicate quality.
- Standard amendment too narrow (medium/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(iii) scope_claim/falsification + SYCOPHANCY gate; no minimum-breadth requirement.
- Standard amendment too broad (medium/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC5 PRE-DRAFT conflict check; overlap is opus's semantic judgment.
- File-impact intersection false positive (high/retrieval-relevance): partially mitigated by SC3(e) narrower-scoped + recency ranking; no semantic relevance filter.
- Top-N cutoff silences critical examples (high/retrieval-coverage): partially mitigated by SC3(f) excluded_count signal in output; ranking heuristic is structural not semantic.
- Cross-epic standard amendment conflicts (high/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC5 PRE-DRAFT check against committed state of standard; concurrent in-flight PRs not visible.
- intent_id schema mismatch (medium/schema-integrity): mitigated by SC2(vii) validation against 94ed manifest entries.

- Bug ticket comment bloat (medium/data-integrity): partially mitigated by SC8 reopening-removes-tag + SC2(iv) atomic write; deduplication of multiple NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comments on same ticket not specified (acceptable — latest comment wins in retrieval implicitly).
## Out of Scope
- Strict ownership enforcement at the manifest layer (explicitly out per 94ed brainstorm).
- Concurrent /dso:retro telemetry write conflict (deferred — low probability; manageable via lock or merge-by-comment-id).
- Operational metric dashboards beyond raw telemetry emission (deferred to /dso:retro-stats or similar observability epic).
- Cross-PR amendment conflict detection (deferred — relies on committed state of standard; PR-review process catches conflicts).
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation Override, 2026-05-18)
### External-dependency verification — addressable touchpoints (Probe-6 partial remediation with explicit override)

The 2026-05-16 audit flagged probe 6 over three external touchpoints. Two are in-session-verifiable via the available CLIs; one is genuinely external and explicitly overridden as non-gating with a documented residual.
| Touchpoint | In-session verification | Disposition |

| SC5 sycophancy gate user response | If the gate fires during the 69e8 sprint, the user's response is captured in the same session transcript. Verification: `grep -E 'sycophancy.*(rejected\|accepted\|deferred)' <session-transcript-or-PIL>` returns ≥1 entry OR the absence is documented as "gate did not fire in this sprint window" — sprint cannot close without one of these states recorded. | IN-SESSION ✓ |

| SC6 atomic graduation depends on gh PR creation | `command -v gh && gh auth status \|\| gh auth login` runs at sprint Phase A; an atomic-graduation invocation during the sprint exercises the gh-PR-creation path against a synthetic fixture branch and asserts a successful PR creation + immediate close. Verification: `gh pr create --draft --base <fixture-base> --head <fixture-head> --title "atomic-graduation-dogfooding" --body "..."` returns a URL; `gh pr close <pr>` succeeds. | IN-SESSION ✓ |

| SC7 human-approval merge on the safeguard-file PR | Human reviewer approval and merge on the `behavioral-testing-standard.md` amendment PR is **genuinely external** — no in-session command can synthesize human review. | OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (override) |
### Explicit override note
SC7's human-approval requirement is acknowledged as operationally external. Sprint closure does NOT gate on the PR being merged within the sprint; closure DOES require that:
- The amendment PR has been **opened** (`gh pr view <pr-number> --json state` returns `"OPEN"` or `"MERGED"`),
- The PR is **assigned to a human reviewer** (`gh pr view <pr-number> --json reviewRequests --jq 'length'` returns ≥1),
- The deferral of merge-approval is recorded as a sprint Phase I comment noting the outstanding human-action item.

This converts the audit's prose-only external dependency into structured in-session preflight + an explicit operational-residual carve-out. The audit's "structured External Dependencies block" pattern is honored in substance (ownership/handling/access/verification_command columns are implicit in the table) while respecting that human review is non-gating.
## Dependencies

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required. SC7 enforces a03c's safeguard-file designation for behavioral-testing-standard.md; SC5's PRE-DRAFT validation reads the standard structure a03c established.

- 4911-c7ba (Bug-classification coverage registry) — required. SC2 executes after 4911's bug-type-<slug> classification; SC3 retrieval queries by 4911's slug taxonomy; SC5(a) frequency trigger groups by slug.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required. SC1 intent_ids_if_applicable references 94ed manifest entries; SC2(vii) validates intent_ids at write time; SC3 reads task claimable_intent from manifest entries.

- d566-afa6 (Generation-time prevention) — required. SC4's test-writer prompts are the same files d566 modifies with Rule 6/7. Coordination: when both epics ship in overlapping sprints, merge-window protocol applies to those prompt files.
## Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from prior calibration brainstorms.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 20 red-team scenarios surfaced; 10 mitigated-by-spec after blue-team filter; 10 surviving (most LLM-judgment residual, partial-mitigated).
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 2 conflicts (a03c safeguard, d566 same-prompts overlap — both managed), 2 considerations (4911 taxonomy, 94ed intent vocabulary), 3 benign (411b, 7f42, cf7b).

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies /dso:fix-bug Phase G, test-writer prompts, /dso:retro). Five risks folded: SCOPE_CLAIM + FALSIFICATION fields in extraction (SC2(iii)), SKIP_RECORD audit trail (SC2(vi)), structured graduation drafting with evidence_citations (SC5), single-falsifiable-predicate constraint for cross-slug (SC5(b)), sycophancy challenge gate (SC5).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium — dozens of bugs and review findings per quarter; LLM-based extraction is feasible per-event.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.

- User-directed design decisions during brainstorm: tickets-as-storage (no separate file) with `NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE:` JSON comments; `negative-example` tag set on extraction; `promoted-to-standard:<rule-id>` tag on graduation; recording in /dso:fix-bug (sonnet); promotion in /dso:retro (opus + human approval at safeguard boundary); hybrid promotion triggers (frequency floor ≥3 same-slug + opus cross-slug falsifiable predicate); top-3 retrieval cap with relevance + staleness exclusion; sycophancy challenge gate mirroring 94ed's challenge round pattern.

content.text: ## Incident Overview

The llm-review CI step's provenance-aware dispatch (`llm-review-dispatch-or-skip.sh`) incorrectly skips LLM review for sub-agent-authored code. PRs #401-405 (epic 3e36 field parity implementation — binding store, ADF walker, comment binding, outbound/inbound differs, reconcile check, sync logger) all showed `llm-review=pass` with `0 findings`, but investigation revealed the LLM was NEVER INVOKED. The code was authored by sub-agents in tracked Claude Code sessions, which gave the commits session provenance. The dispatch script treated this as "already reviewed by sub-PR" and wrote `{"findings":[], "skip_reason":"all_commits_provenanced"}`.
## Root cause

The provenance verifier (`verify-session-provenance.sh`) classifies commits as "covered" if they have session provenance (authored in a tracked Claude Code session). The dispatch script then skips LLM review for covered commits, assuming they were already reviewed in a sub-PR.
This assumption is WRONG for sub-agent-authored PRs:
- Sub-agent commits have session provenance (they ran in a Claude Code session) ✅
- Sub-agent commits were NEVER submitted to llm-review ❌
- The skip treats "known authorship" as "already reviewed" — conflating identity with review status

The correct skip criterion: a commit should only skip llm-review if it was part of a PR that PREVIOUSLY PASSED llm-review (the review has already run and produced findings). Session provenance alone is not sufficient — it means "we know who wrote this" not "we've already reviewed this."
## Impact
5 PRs merged without LLM review:
- PR #401: binding_store.py (14 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #402: adf.py + comment_binding.py (42 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #403: acli-integration.py field parity (115 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #404: outbound_differ.py + inbound_differ.py (14 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
- PR #405: reconcile_check.py + sync_logger.py (13 tests) — NEVER REVIEWED
Combined: ~700 new lines of production code + ~1200 lines of tests shipped without independent LLM review.
## Proposed fix
Change the skip criterion from "commit has session provenance" to "commit was part of a PR that passed llm-review." Specifically:
1. The provenance verifier should record not just "this commit has a session" but "this commit's session-PR passed llm-review"

2. The dispatch script's "covered" classification should require BOTH: (a) session provenance AND (b) the session-PR's llm-review check concluded=success with at least one finding evaluated (not a stub skip)
3. Sub-agent worktree PRs that go directly to main without a prior review cycle should be treated as unprovenanced (requiring full LLM review)
## Workaround
Until the fix ships, sub-agent PRs should be flagged for mandatory review. Options:
- Add a `force-review` label that overrides the provenance skip
- Check if the PR branch was created by a sub-agent (worktree branch naming convention) and force dispatch

content.text: ## Context

Teams using DSO's /dso:onboarding to scaffold CI pipelines currently get Bandit for security scanning — a Python-only tool that leaves JavaScript, Go, Terraform, and other stacks uncovered. Government teams need --metrics=off to prevent telemetry transmission, and there's no unified SAST gate across language stacks. Semgrep OSS covers 30+ languages in a single ~10-second scan, making it a direct replacement for Bandit with broader coverage at comparable speed.
## Success Criteria

- The CI pipeline template (examples/ci.example.yml) runs Semgrep OSS instead of Bandit, using a pinned semgrep/semgrep Docker container tag with --metrics=off and --error; SARIF output is written to semgrep-results.sarif and uploaded as a GitHub Actions artifact. SARIF upload to GitHub Security tab (via upload-sarif with continue-on-error: true) includes a jq post-processing step to convert string severity labels to CVSS numerics (workaround for semgrep/semgrep#10834). SARIF upload is best-effort and decoupled from the blocking CI gate.

- A generate-semgrep-config.sh script produces a .semgrep.yml with mandatory rulesets (p/security-audit, p/owasp-top-ten, p/cwe-top-25) plus stack-specific rulesets mapped from detect-stack.sh output: python-poetry -> p/python; node-npm -> p/javascript; golang -> p/golang; convention-based/unknown -> mandatory rulesets only. The generated config passes semgrep --validate.

- /dso:onboarding calls generate-semgrep-config.sh during CI setup and writes these config keys to dso-config.conf: semgrep.enabled (bool, default true), semgrep.metrics (string, default "off"), semgrep.fail_on (string: error|warning, default "error"), semgrep.custom_rulesets (comma-separated paths, default empty).

- The CI step runs semgrep scan --error --severity ERROR (or --severity WARNING --severity ERROR when semgrep.fail_on=warning), causing exit code 1 when findings exist at or above the configured threshold. The PR is blocked via required status check. The blocking gate depends on Semgrep's exit code, not on SARIF upload success.

- INSTALL.md and README each contain a Semgrep section covering: Docker prerequisite, the --metrics=off flag and its purpose for government teams, how to add custom rulesets via semgrep.custom_rulesets, and how to change the fail_on threshold.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### Config key UPDATE / RETIRE owners (Probe-3 remediation)
| Key | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `semgrep.enabled` (bool, default true) | `/dso:onboarding` CI setup step | Re-onboarding semantics: merge — existing value preserved unless `--reset-security` flag passed; `/dso:onboarding` prompts "found semgrep.enabled=<current>; keep, change, or reset?" | CI step start (skip job if false) | N/A — persistent config; removed only by manual edit / project teardown |
| `semgrep.metrics` (string, default "off") | Same | Same merge-by-default semantics | semgrep CLI `--metrics=` flag | N/A — persistent |
| `semgrep.fail_on` (string, default "error") | Same | Same merge-by-default | CI step `--severity` flag mapping | N/A — persistent |

| `semgrep.custom_rulesets` (comma-separated paths) | Same | Re-onboarding APPENDS new rulesets, never overwrites; operator must explicitly `--reset-security` to clear | generate-semgrep-config.sh inputs | N/A — persistent; entries removed by manual edit |
The "Stale config keys" scenario's "overwrite vs merge" gap is resolved here: **merge by default, with explicit `--reset-security` flag**.
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation)
Before Phase I, the four external dependencies are verified in-session:

- **Branch protection (`gh` CLI):** `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks --jq '.contexts | contains(["semgrep"])'` returns `true`. If branch protection isn't yet configured, the sprint runs `gh api -X PUT ... required_status_checks/contexts` with operator approval AND captures the post-state in a ticket comment.

- **SARIF upload service availability:** `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/code-scanning/alerts --jq 'length'` succeeds (returns ≥0). Documents that GitHub Advanced Security / Code Scanning is enabled OR notes "Code Scanning not enabled — SARIF best-effort only" as the operating posture.

- **Docker container fetch:** `docker pull semgrep/semgrep:<pinned-tag>` returns 0 against the local Docker daemon (or `docker manifest inspect semgrep/semgrep:<pinned-tag>` if no local daemon). Pinned tag is recorded in `examples/ci.example.yml` and verifiable by grep.
- **`.semgrep.yml` validates:** `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/src semgrep/semgrep:<pinned-tag> semgrep --validate --config /src/.semgrep.yml` returns 0.
Converts the audit's prose-only external dependencies into structured in-session checks.
## Scenario Analysis
- SARIF output not written on non-zero exit (high, runtime): CI upload step must use if: always() to run regardless of scan exit code
- Large monorepo OOM (critical, runtime): Semgrep can exhaust memory on 10k+ file repos; container exits with ambiguous code
- Stale stack detection (high, runtime): .semgrep.yml generated at onboarding time does not update when project adds new language stacks
- Registry network fetch failure (critical, runtime): p/ rulesets require network; partial fetch produces incomplete coverage
- Bandit migration overlap (high, deployment): Existing projects retain Bandit config after re-onboarding
- Worktree CWD mismatch (high, deployment): generate-semgrep-config.sh must use REPO_ROOT, not relative paths
- Unpinned Docker image (medium, deployment): Mutable tags cause silent behavior changes
- SARIF format drift (high, deployment): Unpinned Semgrep versions may emit incompatible SARIF
- Warning-severity bypass (critical, configuration): configurable via semgrep.fail_on (default error; set to warning for stricter enforcement)
- Custom ruleset YAML breakage (high, configuration): Invalid semgrep.custom_rulesets can produce unparseable .semgrep.yml
- Metrics env var override (critical, configuration): SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS env var can override --metrics=off flag
- Stale config keys (medium, configuration): Re-onboarding does not specify overwrite vs merge behavior for semgrep.* keys
## Dependencies
- detect-stack.sh (exists in plugins/dso/scripts/; consumed as-is)
- /dso:onboarding CI setup phase (must accept injected config generation scripts)
## Differentiation from related epics
- 857d-a35a (shift-left security in planning): owns planning-time security declarations; this epic owns CI-time scanning. No shared artifacts.
- c821-e995 (security remediation recipes): consumes structured findings; this epic produces SARIF. Schema coordination out of scope for v1.
- dso-0wi2 (project config flags): semgrep.* keys follow existing dso-config.conf KEY=VALUE convention; no schema conflicts.
## Approach

Replace Bandit with Semgrep in the CI template using a config-driven design. A new generate-semgrep-config.sh script reads detect-stack.sh output to select language-specific rulesets alongside mandatory security rulesets, writing a .semgrep.yml for the project. Onboarding orchestrates this during CI setup. New semgrep.* keys in dso-config.conf control enablement, metrics, severity threshold, and custom rulesets.
## Research Findings
### External integration: Semgrep CLI and Docker
- Trigger: External integration
- Query: Semgrep OSS Docker container availability, --metrics=off, SARIF output, exit codes
- Source URLs: semgrep.dev/docs/cli-reference, hub.docker.com/r/semgrep/semgrep, semgrep.dev/docs/semgrep-ci/sample-ci-configs

- Key insight: semgrep/semgrep-action is deprecated (archived April 2024); use semgrep/semgrep Docker container directly. semgrep scan exits 0 by default even with findings; --error flag required for CI gate. --severity filters which findings are reported.
### External integration: SARIF compatibility
- Trigger: External integration
- Query: Semgrep SARIF upload to GitHub Security tab compatibility
- Source URLs: github.com/semgrep/semgrep/issues/10834, docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/uploading-a-sarif-file-to-github

- Key insight: Semgrep emits string severity labels ("Medium") but GitHub upload-sarif requires CVSS numerics. Open bug semgrep/semgrep#10834. Workaround: jq post-processing step to convert strings to numerics.
### External integration: Registry rulesets
- Trigger: Unfamiliar dependency
- Query: Semgrep Community Edition ruleset availability (p/security-audit, p/owasp-top-ten, p/cwe-top-25)
- Source URLs: semgrep.dev/p/owasp-top-ten, semgrep.dev/p/cwe-top-25, semgrep.dev/products/community-edition
- Key insight: All three mandatory rulesets confirmed available in Community Edition without login. 2800+ community rules accessible without authentication.

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Define and implement the recovery contract for dso-config.conf auto-migration when the migration is interrupted (SIGKILL between mktemp write and mv, disk full mid-write, EROFS surfacing after a partial in-memory translation).

**Why**: S4's flock + atomic mktemp/mv handles the happy-path race. It does not specify a recovery story for partial migrations or hand-rolled recovery by users hitting disk-full or interrupted processes. Without an explicit backup-and-restore contract, users have no documented path back to a working state.
**Scope**:

- IN: Backup file naming convention (e.g., `dso-config.conf.v1.bak` written before the atomic rename); restore command/instructions; behavior detection for half-written tempfiles (cleanup on next run); recovery test where SIGKILL fires between tempfile write and mv; recovery test for disk-full after backup but before tempfile write; documented EROFS persistent fallback (in-memory translation + WARN, no backup attempt).
- OUT: Migrating consumer code (S5); the atomic write itself (S4); pre-commit hook (S7).
## Done Definitions
- When complete, a backup of the v1 file is written before any v2 atomic rename ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, an interrupted migration (SIGKILL between tempfile write and mv) is detectable on next run; orphaned tempfiles are cleaned up; user is warned via [DSO WARN] log ← Satisfies: SC2
- When complete, restore instructions exist in DETECTION-SCHEMA.md or KNOWN-ISSUES.md
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for SIGKILL recovery and disk-full edge cases
## Considerations
- [Reliability] Backup creation must itself be atomic enough that a crash mid-backup is recoverable
- [Maintainability] Document EROFS as the one path where no backup is created (in-memory translation only)

content.text: ## Incident Overview
### Expected Behavior

Agent sessions must never modify files while checked out on local `main`. Plugin version bumps (`plugins/dso/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, VERSION files) should be made on a feature/session branch or via release.sh, never directly on main. Local main should remain clean and fast-forwardable from origin/main at all times.
### Actual Behavior

Observed in a recent session (user-reported, 2026-05-17): an agent session edited the plugin version file while HEAD was on local main. The change was left staged but uncommitted. The dirty working tree on main then blocked `git pull` from origin/main — pull refused because the staged change would be overwritten / conflict.
The session was NOT inside a sprint-active or debug-active state, so `check-session-merge-only.sh` did not fire. No other safeguard caught the violation.
### Reproduction
1. Be checked out on local main (no .sprint-active marker)
2. Run a session that edits plugin.json or VERSION
3. Observe staged-on-main state; `git pull` fails
### Suggested Investigation Direction
Two candidate gap classes (investigation should determine which apply):
1. **Hook gap**: `check-session-merge-only.sh` only fires when .sprint-active / .debug-active exist. There is no general 'no edits on main' guard for the orchestrator/main-session case.
2. **Skill/guidance gap**: skills that perform version bumps (release.sh, update-shim.sh, brainstorm/sprint helpers) may not branch off main before editing.
**code_version:** 0bfed0ada71449488d779d6e3743f944e64eea76
**Reporter signal:** user observed in recent session; version bump was staged but not committed on local main; prevented git pull from origin.

content.text: ## Conventional Commits as an Explicit Convention
Activate mandates Conventional Commits (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore) as part of AGENTS.md. DSO's commit workflow doesn't enforce a commit message format standard.
Add configurable commit message conventions to /dso:commit so that commit messages follow a consistent, parseable format. The convention should be:
- Configurable via dso-config.conf (e.g., commit.convention=conventional-commits)
- Enforced at commit time (validation in the commit workflow, not just guidance)
- Default to Conventional Commits (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore) but allow project-specific overrides
- Support optional scope (e.g., feat(auth): add login flow)
- Integrate with version bumping (feat → minor, fix → patch, BREAKING CHANGE → major)

content.text: ## Context

DSO's code review pipeline (10 reviewer agents dispatched via ci-llm-review-runner.sh for CI and /dso:review for in-session) produces findings that are sometimes invalid — the reviewer asserts a bug that doesn't exist, flags minor style preferences as "important," or references code not visible in the diff. These false positives erode trust in the review process and waste developer time triaging non-issues. PR #37 iteration 8 produced 13 confirmed invalid findings across severity calibration, diff-boundary, and hallucination categories. This epic hardens the shared reviewer base prompt with calibrated severity rubrics, explicit NOT-flag guardrails, a deterministic CI-context marker, and a mandatory evidence field — then validates the changes end-to-end against a real large PR.
## Success Criteria

1. reviewer-base.md contains a severity calibration rubric section with 5+ concrete MINOR-not-IMPORTANT examples sourced from the 13 PR #37 bug tickets, plus carve-outs (e.g., "moved/renamed code with all callsites updated -> MINOR, not CRITICAL"). All 10 generated agent files inherit it via build-review-agents.sh.

2. reviewer-base.md contains a NOT-flag rubric section with 5+ auto-downgrade categories (e.g., "style preference without functional impact," "missing error handling for impossible paths"). The reviewer-delta-test-quality.md delta overrides or exempts this section (its anti-pattern detection is structurally distinct from severity-based findings).

3. llm-api-call.sh prepends REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci to the user message payload for all CI-dispatched reviews. reviewer-base.md includes a diff-boundary discipline section: when REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci is present, findings must not assert bugs about code not visible in the provided diff.

4. reviewer-base.md requires a cited_lines field (minimum 1 entry) per finding in the schema section. write-reviewer-findings.sh validates the field is non-empty. Lines prefixed with "~" denote approximate citations of partially visible code (CI context). The security overlay delta's "Do NOT add extra fields" prohibition is replaced with an enumerated allowlist that includes cited_lines. resolve-overlay-findings.sh passes cited_lines through during overlay merge. The deep-arch delta preserves cited_lines from specialist findings during synthesis.

5. E2E validation: Run the CI review pipeline against a PR with 4000+ changed lines. The review output contains zero findings classified as important or critical that, upon manual triage, are determined to be invalid.
## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: reviewer agent .md files (all 10). Interaction: 5d6e-86a9 (CI review parity) shares reviewer agent files and CI dispatch path; changes to rubric text must not break CI dispatch format expectations. Gate: CI dispatch of all 10 agents succeeds after rubric changes.

- Resource: reviewer agent .md files + rubric schema. Interaction: a8e8-0b23 (Agent authoring sub-agent) will need to understand the new severity calibration and NOT-flag rubric structure when generating or modifying reviewer agents. Gate: New rubric sections use the same structural pattern (markdown heading + bullet list) as existing agent guidance.

- Resource: code-reviewer-security-red-team.md, code-reviewer-security-blue-team.md. Interaction: e82e-3888 (Security reference APIs) modifies the same security reviewer agents for API-aware scanning. Gate: Security-specific rubric additions (this epic) occupy distinct markdown sections from API reference additions (e82e-3888).

- Resource: severity classification output. Interaction: b6e9-6f1d (Reviewer override discipline) uses severity to determine override authority; recalibrated severity boundaries feed into override decisions. Gate: Severity schema values (critical/important/minor/fragile) are unchanged; only the classification rubric text changes.

- Resource: llm-api-call.sh, ci-llm-review-runner.sh. Interaction: 2fa0-a2d9 (CI context-augmentation loop) and 88d2-6756 (CodeQL gates) both modify CI dispatch scripts. Gate: REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci marker is prepended as a single line; does not alter the message structure or interfere with other CI augmentation.

- Resource: reviewer agent .md files (rubric text). Interaction: db68-ca95 (LLM blindspot hardening) adds rubric text to the same agent files for blind-spot mitigation. Gate: Severity calibration and NOT-flag sections are structurally separate from blind-spot rubric sections.
## Dependencies

- Must complete before 4911-c7ba (Reviewer rubric expansion) — both modify all 10 reviewer agent files; this epic's severity calibration must land first to avoid merge conflicts with new dimension additions.
- Coordinate with 5d6e-86a9 (CI review parity) — shared reviewer agent files and CI dispatch path.
- Sequence before dso-8l5h (Extract review sub-agents) — this epic edits agent files at their current paths; dso-8l5h may later move/rename them.
## Approach

Prompt hardening with mandatory evidence field. Add severity calibration rubric, NOT-flag rubric, diff-boundary discipline, and cited_lines field to reviewer-base.md (the shared prompt fragment composed into all 10 agents by build-review-agents.sh). Modify llm-api-call.sh for REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci marker, write-reviewer-findings.sh for cited_lines validation, resolve-overlay-findings.sh for cited_lines pass-through, and specific deltas for overrides (test-quality exemption, security overlay allowlist, deep-arch preservation). Convergence target: 3-4 review iterations acceptable as long as findings are genuinely important.

content.text: ## Context

Agents and developers currently have no way to permanently remove tickets that are duplicates, mistakes, or superseded. The only option is `closed`, which keeps tickets visible in Jira and in dependency graphs. A dedicated deletion command is needed that removes tickets from all active views, propagates removal to Jira, and atomically cleans up any blocker dependencies tied to the deleted ticket. Deletion is irreversible — no restore path exists.
## Success Criteria

- `ticket delete <id>` without `--user-approved` exits non-zero with an instructional error message directing the agent to confirm with the user and re-run with `--user-approved`; the `--user-approved` flag is absent from help text
- `ticket delete <id> --user-approved` exits non-zero with a clear error listing any child tickets not in `deleted` status
- `ticket delete <id> --user-approved` on a valid ticket atomically writes a `STATUS(deleted)` event and an `ARCHIVED` event in a single git commit
- After deletion, `ticket list` (default output) excludes the deleted ticket; `ticket show <id>` still works and shows `status: deleted` and `archived: true`
- `ticket transition <id> <current> deleted` exits non-zero with an error directing the user to `ticket delete`

- On the next outbound bridge run, the bridge calls the Jira DELETE API for the ticket's Jira key; all subsequent sync operations for that ticket are skipped (idempotent); if Jira returns 403 (permission denied) the bridge writes a BRIDGE_ALERT and does not retry
- `ticket transition <parent-id> <current> closed` does not fail due to child tickets in `deleted` status (`deleted` is added to `CLOSED_STATUSES` in the open-children guard)
## Scenario Analysis

- **Concurrent delete and transition race on same ticket** (`high`, `runtime`): Two agents simultaneously attempt to delete and transition the same ticket. The delete script reads the current status, passes the non-deleted-children guard, then the transition script writes a STATUS event. The delete script then writes STATUS(deleted) + ARCHIVED events on top of the transition event.

- **Child ticket deleted between guard check and commit write** (`high`, `runtime`): The non-deleted-children guard passes because all children are in terminal states. Between the guard check and the atomic commit write, a concurrent agent transitions a child ticket back to in_progress. The parent deletion proceeds but the child is now active with a deleted parent.

- **UNLINK events written for stale dependency snapshot** (`high`, `runtime`): The delete script reads depends_on links at guard-check time. A concurrent agent adds a new blocker dependency between read and commit, leaving an active depends_on link pointing to a deleted ticket.

- **Jira DELETE not idempotent on retry after network failure** (`medium`, `runtime`): Bridge calls Jira DELETE; API succeeds but response is lost. On next bridge run, if Jira returns 404 for already-deleted issue and bridge does not treat 404 as success, it marks ticket as needing further sync.

- **ticket list exclusion depends on event ordering not materialized state** (`medium`, `runtime`): If ticket list reads events in git log order rather than materializing final state, a delete event written out-of-order may cause ticket to appear as non-deleted.

- **CLOSED_STATUSES update not backward compatible with older worktrees** (`high`, `deployment`): Worktrees running the old ticket-transition.sh do not include `deleted` in CLOSED_STATUSES, causing parent-close to fail when children are in deleted status.

- **acli-integration.py delete_issue method absent in pinned CI environment** (`high`, `deployment`): CI pipelines pinning acli-integration.py to a specific commit may not have delete_issue, raising AttributeError and halting all Jira sync.

- **Ticket with no Jira key causes bridge to call DELETE on null endpoint** (`medium`, `configuration`): A locally-created ticket never synced to Jira has no jira_key; bridge constructs malformed DELETE URL.

- **Missing JIRA_API_TOKEN at deletion sync time** (`high`, `configuration`): Token absent or expired causes DELETE to fail; if bridge does not flag for retry, ticket remains alive in Jira indefinitely.

- **Jira project configured with restricted delete permissions** (`high`, `configuration`): 403 from Jira on DELETE creates persistent local/Jira divergence without alerting if not handled as BRIDGE_ALERT.
## Dependencies

- Jira service-account permission: The bridge account configured via JIRA_API_TOKEN must hold the "Delete Issues" project permission in Jira for Jira deletion to function. The bridge degrades gracefully to BRIDGE_ALERT on 403. This is an operational prerequisite, not an upstream epic.
- No other epics are prerequisites.
## Approach

New `ticket-delete.sh` script enforces the `--user-approved` gate, non-deleted-children guard, and atomically writes STATUS(deleted) + ARCHIVED + UNLINK events in a single git commit. `ticket-transition.sh` blocks `deleted` as a target status and adds `deleted` to CLOSED_STATUSES. `acli-integration.py` gains a `delete_issue` method using `acli jira workitem delete --key`. The outbound bridge adds a `deleted` status case that calls Jira DELETE and skips all further sync for that ticket.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: External integration (Jira DELETE API — acli jira workitem delete syntax, REST API permissions, 403 handling)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered — 10 surviving scenarios (3 filtered by blue team)
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 10
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered
## Closure Checks
- All `depends_on` links where the deleted ticket is the blocking target (`target_id`) are removed via UNLINK events written atomically in the same git commit as the delete events

- An acceptance test confirms the end-to-end deletion workflow: `ticket delete --user-approved` on a test ticket followed by `ticket list` (excludes it), `ticket graph` (no edges to the deleted ID), and the outbound bridge mock/stub confirms the Jira DELETE API is called with the correct issue key

content.text: ## Context

Java is entirely unsupported: detect-stack.sh has no Java detection, Java projects fall through to unknown routing and receive no test/lint/format gates, no kudos triggers, no security scan, and no CI skeleton support. This epic adds Java as a first-class language: detect-stack.sh detection (Maven/Gradle with wrapper preference), onboarding Java branch, commands.* routing, gate-2d/gate-2b Java support, project-detect.sh CI pattern recognition, plus stretch deliverables (commands.security OWASP scan and architect-foundation scaffolding).
Core tier (sprint-blocking): SCs 1-3, 6, 7. Stretch (not required for epic closure): SCs 4, 5.
## Success Criteria

- detect-stack.sh adds java-maven (pom.xml at root) and java-gradle (build.gradle at root) as separate stack values; CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md stack accepted values list updated to include both; java-maven takes priority when both present; Java detection below Python/Rust/Go/Node/Ruby; scripts treating both as equivalent (gate-2b, gate-2d, project-detect) vs. differently (commands.* writes, wrapper detection) documented via equivalence contract

- onboarding SKILL.md Phase 3 Step 2b updated with Java branch writing commands.test_runner, commands.lint, commands.format, commands.format_check; wrapper detection (root-only): mvnw present -> ./mvnw test; pom.xml without mvnw -> mvn test; gradlew present -> ./gradlew test; build.gradle without gradlew -> gradle test
- commands.lint = mvn checkstyle:check, commands.format_check = mvn spotless:check, commands.format = mvn spotless:apply for Java stacks

- [STRETCH] commands.security config key added to CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md; validate.sh emits [DSO WARN] commands.security not configured with exit 0 when absent; Java defaults: mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check -DfailBuildOnCVSS=7 (Maven), ./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze (Gradle)

- [STRETCH] architect-foundation Phase 3 Enforcer Setup: checkstyle.xml using Google Java Style, maven-checkstyle-plugin v3.3.1 + spotless-maven-plugin v2.43.0 in pom.xml with executions bound to validate phase; mvn validate passes after scaffolding
- gate-2d-dependency-check.sh adds Java import statement extraction; gate-2b-blast-radius.sh adds Java fan-in patterns (import, class instantiation) as bash array elements (not eval)
- project-detect.sh recognizes mvn test and ./gradlew test patterns in GitHub Actions YAML
## Dependencies
- Epic A (87e9-0bc8): commands.test_runner routing must exist before Epic F writes Maven/Gradle defaults; onboarding config-write path must be established
- Epic B (3818-310d): commands.lint, commands.format, commands.format_check must exist; gate-2d/gate-2b structure lands first (SC6 is additive Java-only entries)
- Epic C (co-deployment only, not blocking): once both Epic C and Epic F merge, T7/T13/T4 automatically support Java via lizard/jscpd
- Epic E (not blocking): SC5 is self-contained architect-foundation Phase 3 addition; no Epic E deliverable required for any Epic F story
## Approach

Add Java detection to detect-stack.sh (java-maven and java-gradle stack values). Update onboarding SKILL.md with a Java branch in the config-write phase. Add Java defaults to the commands.* routing table. Extend gate-2d and gate-2b with Java patterns. Add project-detect.sh CI pattern recognition. Stretch: add commands.security and architect-foundation scaffolding templates.
## Research Findings

- Build tool conventions: Maven uses pom.xml at project root; Gradle uses build.gradle (Groovy DSL) or build.gradle.kts (Kotlin DSL); wrapper scripts mvnw/gradlew are standard conventional invocation entry points

- Checkstyle: Google Java Style is the de-facto pre-built config; maven-checkstyle-plugin v3.3.1 binds to the `validate` phase; spotless-maven-plugin v2.43.0 is the current stable version for formatting enforcement

- OWASP dependency-check: Maven via `mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check -DfailBuildOnCVSS=7`; Gradle via `./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze`; CVSS ≥ 7 threshold matches NIST High severity cutoff
- Detection ordering: Java placed below Python/Rust/Go/Node/Ruby in detect-stack.sh per existing first-match-wins convention

- Equivalence contract: scripts treat java-maven and java-gradle as equivalent for test-execution routing (gate-2b, gate-2d, project-detect) but differently for commands.* writes and wrapper detection — contract is machine-readable for downstream scripts
## Scenario Analysis

- Both pom.xml and build.gradle present at root (medium, detection): java-maven wins per explicit contract; equivalence contract documents which gates treat them as equivalent vs. differently — prevents silent double-routing
- Multi-module Maven project (medium, detection): subdirectory pom.xml files not at root are ignored by stack detection; wrapper detection is root-only; submodule gates inherit root stack value
- Gradle Kotlin DSL build.gradle.kts (medium, scope): detection must include .kts extension or silently skip Kotlin-DSL-only projects; documented behavior required in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md
- Missing wrapper, system-wide mvn/gradle (low, deployment): fallback to unwrapped invocation (mvn test / gradle test); documented as acceptable; wrapper-preferred-when-present is the contract
- commands.security key absent (high, configuration, stretch): [DSO WARN] emitted with exit 0; validate.sh does not block — per stretch SC

- Checkstyle/spotless plugin version drift (medium, maintenance): plugin versions pinned in scaffolded pom.xml (v3.3.1 / v2.43.0); upgrades require doc update and architect-foundation template refresh
- gate-2b/gate-2d bash array pattern injection (low, security): Java fan-in patterns added as bash array elements (not eval); standard pattern per existing gates — guards against shell injection
- project-detect.sh false-positive on commented-out mvn/gradle lines in workflow YAML (low, correctness): regex anchored to active `run:` keys, not YAML comments (#)
## Risk Register (from preplanning)
- Maintainability (7bc4-3941): Equivalence contract must be machine-readable for gate-2d/gate-2b to reference
- Reliability (c140-82c5): Wrapper detection root-only; check pom.xml/build.gradle root files only
- Testing (c140-82c5): Validation (grep commands.test_runner = mvn test) requires Maven fixture
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (Maven, Gradle, Checkstyle, Spotless, OWASP dependency-check CLIs), novel pattern (stack-detection equivalence contract)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 8
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-project stack detection, per-commit gate invocation; not volume-sensitive
## Closure Checks
- Validation: grep commands.test_runner .claude/dso-config.conf returns mvn test after onboarding Maven project; grep 'java-maven|java-gradle' CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md returns both entries

content.text: ## Context

Epic A (dso-to7x) delivers worktree isolation with serial review — sub-agents implement in isolated worktrees, orchestrator reviews/tests each worktree one at a time, commits and merges sequentially. This works but leaves review/test throughput as a bottleneck: with N worktrees, review time is N × single-review-time.
Epic B scales review to parallel: all returned worktrees are reviewed and tested simultaneously, with Clash preventing file conflicts proactively during implementation.
## Success Criteria

1. Clash (clash-sh/clash) integrates at the orchestrator level via file-impact pre-analysis before dispatch, preventing two sub-agents from being assigned overlapping files — verified by test showing dispatch blocked when file lists overlap

2. When implementation sub-agents return, the orchestrator dispatches review and test sub-agents in parallel — one pair per worktree — verified by concurrent review producing separate reviewer-findings.json files in each worktrees ARTIFACTS_DIR

3. First-pass-first-merge by completion order: each worktree merges as soon as its review passes, without waiting for other worktrees — verified by merge order matching completion order, not dispatch order
4. Review timeout per worktree: hung reviews are skipped after configurable timeout and flagged for user attention — verified by injecting a slow review and asserting it is skipped after timeout
5. Hook dispatcher updated to route Clash pre-analysis through the consolidated hook architecture
## Dependencies
- Depends on dso-to7x (Epic A: worktree isolation with serial review)
- Coordinate with dso-t7af (usage-aware throttling: controls how many parallel agents can dispatch)
